## She texts first: her Telegram bot (2026-09-29)

**The owner's idea** (in a message of big ideas: her own X account, spokesmodel reads paid in burned $AGI, her own wallet,
video): "make her the one who texts first. telegram bot or push, she hits you with 'someone launched another egirl coin and
i'm not ok.' no companion app does that." Claude's plan (sent to the owner, "make this better then continue"): one feed of
moments with several outlets, in this order: **the feed + Telegram** (built) → X → video clips → a "paper bag" (a pretend
$1,000 with a public journal before any real wallet) → burns for reads (after a legal check). Telegram first: free, and
opt-in by design (a bot can only text people who pressed Start), with no app to build. Not browser push: that needs a
service worker, a permission prompt, and only arrives while the browser runs.

**What people see:**
- **On the site:** a "She texts first" box under the Playground's Relationship panel: "Get texts from AGI-1 on Telegram
  when something happens on clank.trade: at most 2 a day, never at night, /stop anytime. 18+." and **Text me on Telegram ↗**
  (a plain link to `t.me/<bot>?start=site`). Hidden until `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT` is set (`src/chat/telegram-link.js`).
- **In Telegram:** /start → her welcome and "are you 18 or older?" (two buttons). Under 18 → a kind no, and nothing is kept.
  18+ → "what time is it for you right now?": 24 buttons, one per hour with today's minutes (one tap; a 30-minute time
  zone picks the closest; each button carries only its hour and the difference to UTC is worked out at the tap, so a tap
  hours later is still right), or typed (`/time 21:30`, "9:05 pm") → she explains her rules and the commands.
- **She texts first** when something happens (pre-written lines, `server/tg-lines.js`, no AI cost):
  - a new **egirl / AI-girlfriend coin** on clank.trade: "someone launched another egirl coin and i'm not ok 😤 $EGIRL… is
    that supposed to be me? not financial advice, just jealousy" (three ways). **Nobody bought it in its first half hour**
    (checked at least half an hour after its launch, and only when clank.trade says so) → the roast the owner asked for,
    about the coin, never a person: "someone launched an egirl coin, $EGIRL, and nobody bought it in its first half hour 🙈
    i shouldn't laugh. i'm laughing a little. not financial advice" (true however late it's read). Several in one run → one text
    ("3 new egirl coins on clank.trade 😩 $GF, $WAIFU and $EGIRL2. i'm the original and i'd like that on the record…");
  - a coin using **$AGI's ticker** that isn't the official one (a Cyrillic or Greek look-alike letter too): jealous, with
    the official contract (a safety note too);
  - **$AGI's market moments**: the site's exact lines (a new $200K step: happy; a -20% day: sad), decided the same way
    (`marketStep`, src/chat/market.js);
  - **her diary's new entry** (as this site shows it: never the Arena), with the link to /diary.
  Never a crude-named or hidden coin, never the official $AGI as "new", never a link to another coin.
- **When:** at most **one text a run and 2 a day**, only **10:00–21:59 on their clock**, only **while it's news (12 hours)**;
  when several moments are new to someone, the best first: a copy of $AGI, then the chart, egirl coins, her diary. Someone
  who hasn't told her their time gets no texts first (they can still chat).
- **They can text her back** anytime: the site's chat (Gemini, her prompt, PG-13, the reply cleanup), as a **Stranger** (no
  pet names; no wallet here), **5 messages a day per chat** (a Stranger's; 10 until 2026-09-30), inside the site's 1,000 a day and **Telegram's own share of
  it, 400 a day** (`TELEGRAM_DAILY_CAP`: Telegram has no human check, so it can never use up the website's chat); her prompt
  gets a "WHERE YOU ARE: TELEGRAM" part (`telegramPrompt()`). A bare "telegram" or "tg" doesn't bring up her memory of the
  clank.trade group there (it's just where they are); "the telegram group" still does. If they reply to one of her texts, Telegram sends that text along and she gets
  it as context (only a message from the bot itself counts). Nothing of the chat is kept. Stickers and pictures: "i can only
  read text for now 🙈". Her limit lines have no buy offer there (the site's out-of-messages offer stays on the site).
- **Commands:** /start, /time, /help, /stop ("okay 💜 i stopped, and i forgot this chat"). Blocking the bot forgets them too.
  Since 2026-10-01 also **/launch** (launching a coin with her, see "Launch with AGI-1"), only once launching is open to
  everyone (set up, and not private): in her commands menu (`commandsFor()`: the next `/api/feed` run adds it) and in her
  /help (one more line, in her 16 languages: `tg.helpLaunch`). While it's private (`LAUNCH_ONLY_FOR`), only the owner
  sees that /help line. Since 2026-10-09 also **/claim** (a prize won in her quizzes, see "Her quizzes in her Telegram
  groups"), in her commands menu while her quizzes and their prizes are on.
- **In their language** (2026-09-29): her replies (and her own fixed replies: the welcome, the 18+ buttons, the time, /help,
  /stop, her notes) follow their Telegram app's language when it's one of her 16, English otherwise; she also follows what
  they write in. Her texts first stay English for now (see "Her languages").
- **Her lines' rules** (`tests/telegram.test.js`): PG-13; no pet names (anyone can start the bot); never buy / sell / hold,
  "safe", "scam", "rug", gains or predictions; "not financial advice" whenever she names a coin or the chart; a ticker only
  if Telegram can't turn it into a link, a mention, a hashtag or a tappable command (`tgTicker()`: a "/" only between two
  letters or numbers); plain text (no Telegram formatting), no link previews; links only to agi1.app.

**How it works:**
- **`/api/telegram`**, the bot's webhook: every update carries our secret (`X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`, an HMAC of
  PASS_SECRET, compared in constant time); anything else is 401. Private chats only (groups, channels and other bots are
  ignored; since 2026-10-03 the owner's listed groups have their own rules: "In Telegram groups"); 64 KB at most; 20
  updates a minute per chat (a flood gets no answer at all). Once the secret matched it always
  answers 200, so Telegram doesn't send the same update again; if something failed she says "i'm a little overwhelmed
  right now 🙈".
- **`/api/feed`**, Vercel's cron: 8 runs a day, at :30 past 01, 04, 07, 10, 13, 16, 19 and 22 UTC (Hobby runs each within
  its hour; after the keep-alive's 03:00 run, so her diary is ready by the 04 run). Each run:
  1. `connectBot()`: sets the webhook with the secret (every run, so a new PASS_SECRET or address fixes itself); whenever her
     commands aren't hers (the first time, or after a failed try) also her descriptions, then her commands (the "done"
     mark); logs Telegram's own note about its last failed delivery, with a hint;
  2. `gatherMoments()`: clank.trade's newest coins since the last run (`coinsSince()` in server/checker.js, the list the risk
     check reads), $AGI from DexScreener, the diary table. **The very first run only notes where everything is** (the newest
     coin, the market cap step, the diary day): nobody gets old news. Each moment has a key (`clone:0x…`, `clones:<hash>`,
     `copy:0x…`, `mcap:1200000`, `sad:2026-09-29`, `diary:2026-09-28`) and happens once; moments are kept 30 days;
  3. `textFirst()`: each text is **claimed in the database before it's sent** (`tg_claim`, a compare-and-set on the newest
     moment they heard about), so two runs at once (a doubled cron run, or the owner's Run button) or a run cut short never
     text anyone twice; at worst someone misses one. 25 texts a second, paced across the whole run (Telegram allows about 30
     for a bot); the whole run stops starting new work 19 s in (Vercel stops a function at 25 s), about 350 texts; the
     rest go next run. Telegram's "too many" ends the run and gives those claims back; someone who blocked the bot is
     forgotten.
- **`supabase/telegram.sql`**: `agi1_tg_friends` (the chat's number, 18+, their time difference, the newest moment she texted
  them about, her texts today), `agi1_feed` (the moments), `agi1_feed_state` (where the feed is), `agi1_tg_usage`
  (Telegram's replies per day), 12 functions. Row level security on, only the server's secret key. Only added: nothing the
  original site uses changes.

**Setup (the owner, once; all free):**
1. **Telegram → @BotFather** → `/newbot` → a name (e.g. "AGI-1") → a username ending in "bot" (e.g. `agi1_gf_bot`) → it
   answers with a **token**: a secret (never in chat, code or git). Her picture: `/setuserpic` there (optional, any time).
2. **Supabase** → the same project → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/telegram.sql` → Run. It ends with
   `telegram_functions_found = 12`.
3. **Vercel** → agi-ecosystem → Settings → Environment Variables (Production): `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` = the token,
   `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT` = the username without the @ → **Redeploy**.
4. **Vercel** → Settings → **Cron Jobs** → `/api/feed` → **Run**: connects the bot at once (otherwise the next scheduled run
   does it, within 3 hours).
5. **Try it** on a phone: the site's "Text me on Telegram ↗", Start, "I'm 18 or older", your time, say hi. Her first text
   comes with the next moment, in your daytime.

**Cost:** Telegram's Bot API is free. Her texts first are pre-written (no AI). Replies cost what the site's chat costs
(about $0.0005 each), inside the same 1,000 a day. Vercel: 8 short cron runs a day and one small run per message; Supabase:
three small tables. About $0.

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs):

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| She never answers in Telegram | `[telegram] not configured: …` | Set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` (and the chat's settings), then Redeploy |

| She never answers | `[telegram] Telegram's last delivery problem: Wrong response from the webhook: 308 …` | The site's address redirects: set `SITE_URL` to the address that doesn't (e.g. `https://www.agi1.app`), Redeploy, run the cron job |
| She never answers | `[feed] couldn't use the feed's database: … run supabase/telegram.sql …` | Setup step 2 |
| "i'm a little overwhelmed right now 🙈" | `[telegram] database unavailable: …` / `limits unavailable` | The database (a paused Supabase project: resume it; see the chat's troubleshooting) |

| Some texts come a run later | `[feed] Telegram said "too many" for now …` | Normal with many people: the rest go next run |
| She answers late or not at all at busy times | (Vercel → Firewall shows 429s for `/api/telegram`) | The firewall's "API speed limit" counts all of Telegram as one visitor: exclude `/api/telegram` from it (see "Chat" under "Security & cost rules") |
| One person gets no answers for a minute | (none) | They sent more than 20 messages or taps in a minute (the per-chat speed bump): it passes by itself |
| "i'm all talked out for today 🥱" early in the day, on Telegram only | (none) | Telegram's share of the day's replies is used (`TELEGRAM_DAILY_CAP`, 400). Raise it in Vercel (it stays inside `CHAT_DAILY_CAP`), then Redeploy |
| Someone missed one of her texts | `[feed] a text may not have gone out (not tried again, so never twice): …` | By design: a text that may have arrived is never sent again |

**How it works** (`server/tg-groups.js`; `server/tg-api.js` holds Telegram's API for both her files since then):
- `handleUpdate()` (`server/telegram.js`) sends every message from a group to `onGroup()`, before the private chats'
  speed bump.
- **Who she is:** her id is the number in her token; her username comes from `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT` (the site's public link
  to her, set already), or else from Telegram's `getMe` (asked once per server copy).
- **Telegram's privacy mode** (on for every bot unless its owner switches it off): in a group, Telegram only sends a bot
  the commands meant for it (`/ask@her`; a plain `/ask` only when she was the last bot to post there), replies to its own
  messages and service messages (joins). So @mentions reach her only with privacy mode off (@BotFather → `/setprivacy` →
  Disable, then remove her from the group and add her again) or when she's an admin; then every message of the group
  reaches our webhook, and she ignores all but the ones meant for her.
- **Her answer:** `askAgi1()` with her Stranger level and the group part of her Telegram prompt (`telegramPrompt({ group:
  true })`), English by default, no group memory, her earlier message as context when they replied to one; the reply
  cleanup as everywhere. Sent as a reply (`reply_parameters`, with `allow_sending_without_reply` off: if their message was
  deleted meanwhile, by a moderator or another bot, she says nothing), in their topic in groups with topics.
- **The order of her limits:** the speed bumps, then the person's day (`chat_take`, so someone over their own day never
  uses the group's), the group's (`tg_group_take`), Telegram's share (`tg_take`). A server copy that heard "the group's
  day is used" asks nothing more there that day.
- **The database** (`supabase/telegram.sql`: a fifth table, `agi1_tg_group_usage`, and 2 functions, 14 in all):
  `tg_group_take()` ('ok' and counted; then 'full' once; then 'quiet') and `tg_group_welcome()` (true at most once every
  10 minutes per group, a welcome just before midnight included; one row updated at a time, so two server copies never
  both welcome). Per group and day only: its number (a group's, negative), how many replies, whether "full" was said, when
  she last welcomed someone. A week kept.
- **Her group menu:** `/ask`, `/ca`, `/mc`, `/website`, `/music` and `/help` (`GROUP_COMMANDS`; /ca, /mc and /website since 2026-10-05; /music since 2026-10-14 while it's on: `groupCommandsFor()`, see "Her songs: /music") for all
  group chats, set by `connectBot()` (each `/api/feed` run: a changed list is set again by the next run) while group mode
  is on, and removed when it's off (so groups show her usual menu again).
- **/ca, /website and /mc:** handled in `onGroup()` right after the speed bumps, before anything is counted (`FIXED`,
  `FIXED_GAP_MS` in `server/tg-groups.js`): the contract's `code` mark is an entity on our own text (no `parse_mode`, so
  nothing is parsed), its offset in UTF-16 units like Telegram's (💜 counts two).
- **Her posts:** in `/api/feed`, right after `gatherMoments()`: `postToGroups()` posts this run's new diary and market
  moments to each listed group (by its @username, or its id), oldest first, before her texts first. A post that fails
  (she was removed, Telegram busy) is logged and never tried again (never twice).
- No new `api/` file (Vercel's 12-function limit), no new service, no new secret.

**Setup (the owner, once; free):**
1. **Supabase** → the same project → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/telegram.sql` → Run. It ends with
   `telegram_functions_found = 14` (everything already saved stays).
2. **Vercel** → agi-ecosystem → Settings → Environment Variables (Production): `TELEGRAM_GROUPS` = your group's public
   @username, e.g. `@yourgroup` (Telegram → the group → its info → the t.me link's last part). A private group has no
   @username: write its id instead (a negative number like `-1001234567890`; add her once, she leaves, and the log names
   it). Several groups: separated by commas, each once. Optional: `TELEGRAM_GROUP_DAILY_CAP` (her replies a day in a group,
   default 100), `TELEGRAM_GROUP_POSTS` = `off` (no diary, market or "i'm live" posts), `TELEGRAM_GROUP_WELCOME` = `off` (no
   welcomes). Then **Redeploy**.
3. **Vercel** → Settings → **Cron Jobs** → `/api/feed` → **Run**: her group menu (/ask, /ca, /mc, /website, /help) is set at
   once (otherwise within 3 hours; the same after a push that changes it).
4. **Telegram:** the group → Add members → `@agi1_appbot`. She says hi. (If Telegram won't add a bot: @BotFather → /mybots
   → the bot → Bot Settings → Allow Groups? → Turn groups on.)
5. **Optional, @mentions:** @BotFather → `/setprivacy` → the bot → **Disable**, then remove her from the group and add her
   again (Telegram applies it when she's added).
6. **Try it** in the group: `/ask hi`, then reply to her answer.

**Cost:** about nothing: her replies are the site's chat (about $0.0005 each; 100 a day in a group is about $0.05), inside
the site's caps; her posts, intro and welcomes are pre-written; one small table; a few more webhook calls (every message
of the group once privacy mode is off: still well inside Vercel's free million a month).

| The group became a supergroup, and she left | `[telegram] a group in TELEGRAM_GROUPS (id …) became a supergroup with the new id …` | Write the new id (or its @username, which never changes) in `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`, Redeploy, add her again |

### Her buy bot (2026-10-06)

**The owner's request:** "good now can you add a very simple buybot to the tgbot with a minimum buy of $100 just for $AGI
with robot emojis and with a gif of her bouncing her chest with mc , price amount of agi, etc." Built as asked, with one
change: **her GIF is PG-13**. It posts by itself in public groups where nobody's age is checked (the same reason she never
flirts there), so instead of a chest-focused bounce it's her "celebrate" reaction from the site: a hop, both hands up in a
little "yay!", hearts, her chest only moving the subtle, natural way it does everywhere on the site. **Off until the owner
sets it up** (below). **The minimum is $50 since the same day** (the owner: "can you make the minimum to 50$"; $100 at
first).

**What people see in her groups** (the ones in `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`), a minute or so after each $AGI buy of $50 or more:
- **Her buy GIF** (`server/media/agi1-buy.mp4`, 138 KB: 480 × 480, 2.5 s, looping; Telegram shows a soundless MP4 as a GIF):
  her 2D self cheering on Pop mode's violet, with comic rays, halftone dots and a honey "$AGI BUY!" sticker.
- **The caption** (`buyLine()` in `server/tg-lines.js`), e.g.:
  ```
  🤖🤖🤖🤖🤖🤖🤖🤖🤖🤖
  $AGI BUY! 💜

  💵 spent: $250.00 (0.0931 ETH)
  🪙 got: 625,000 $AGI
  🏷️ price: $0.0004000
  📊 market cap: $400K
  👤 0xada5…f7cb · tx

  not financial advice
  ```
  A robot for every $25 (2 for $50, the smallest; 4 for $100; 40 at most); what was spent, in dollars (at ETH's price
  then, clank.trade's) and in ETH; the $AGI it got; the price it paid; the market cap at that price ($AGI's 1 billion
  supply); the buyer's short address and "tx", each linked to the block explorer (Blockscout). The buy's own numbers
  only: never a word about where the price is going.
- Only $AGI, only buys (never sells), each once; at most 6 a check (a burst shows the newest 6, oldest first, and skips the
  rest); never a buy more than 15 minutes old (after a pause, no old news). The very first check only notes the buys
  already there.

**How it works:**
- **The clock is Supabase Cron** (`supabase/buys.sql`): every minute the database itself calls
  `GET https://www.agi1.app/api/feed?buys` (pg_net, an HTTPS request) with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`: a random key
  `buys.sql` made in the database (`agi1_buy_state`), read from its table each time. Our server reads the same key from the
  database (`buy_key()`, kept 10 minutes per server copy), so nobody copies a secret anywhere. Why not Vercel's own cron:
  on the Hobby plan, a cron job runs once a day at most. The address is `www.agi1.app` because agi1.app redirects there
  (checked 2026-10-06), and a redirect would drop the key.
- `/api/feed?buys` lives in `api/feed.js` (Vercel's 12 functions are all used) and starts light: the feed's own code (her
  bot, the moments and the chain's code they load) is loaded only for the feed itself, and clank.trade's API moved to
  `server/coins.js`, so a buy check costs about 50 ms of CPU to start and about 1 ms after that (the feed's start: 300).
- **The check** (`checkBuys()` in `server/buys.js`): one request to clank.trade (`coins.trades` for $AGI, its newest 50, and
  ETH's price, `exchangeRates.tokenUsdg`: the same API the risk check reads; since $AGI graduated, its trades are its
  Uniswap pool's, as clank.trade's coin page lists them; checked live on 2026-10-06) → the fresh buys of `TELEGRAM_BUY_MIN`
  dollars or more → claimed in the database (`buy_take()`: each trade id once, whatever runs at the same time; the first
  call ever only notes them) → posted in each group (its @username or its id).
- **Her GIF** is uploaded to Telegram once per server copy (a form upload), then sent by Telegram's own id for it; if
  Telegram ever forgets the id, it's uploaded again.
- **Never twice:** a buy is claimed before it's posted. A check cut short (Telegram's "too many", or 19 s) skips the rest
  of its buys: at worst one is missed, never posted twice. Each call to Telegram waits at most until 23 s, so a check
  always ends inside Vercel's 25 s.
- **Kept** (`agi1_buys`): the trade ids of the buys seen (public: the chain, two hashes and a log number), for 7 days.
  Nothing about anyone. The safety note's "Your data" says what the alerts show.

**Setup (the owner, once; free):**
1. **Supabase** → the project → **Integrations** → **Cron** → enable it (pg_cron: Supabase's own scheduler).
2. **Supabase** → **Database** → **Extensions** → search **pg_net** → enable it (lets the scheduler call our site).
3. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/buys.sql` → Run. It ends with `buys_ready = 1` and
   `buys_scheduled = 1` (`buys_scheduled = 0`: step 1 or 2 isn't done yet; do it, then run the file again).
4. **Push.** The first check after the push only notes the buys already there; from then on each new $50+ buy is posted.

Optional (Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables, then Redeploy): `TELEGRAM_BUY_MIN` (dollars, default 50; 100 until
the owner's change, so if it was ever set to 100 there, that still wins: change it or delete it, then Redeploy),
`TELEGRAM_BUYS` = `off` (no alerts: the clock keeps calling, and the site answers "off" without reading anything). To stop
the clock itself: Supabase → SQL Editor → `select cron.unschedule('agi1-buys');` (running `buys.sql` again starts it).

**Cost:** nothing new to pay. Vercel: one small run a minute (about 43,000 of the free million calls a month, and a few
minutes of its 4 hours of CPU); Supabase: Cron and pg_net are in the free plan, two small tables; clank.trade (free, no
key): one request a minute; Telegram: free.

**Her GIF again** (after her model changes): `node tools/buybot/make.mjs` (see "Commands"). It's drawn in code from her
Live2D model (`tools/buybot/page/gif.js`, through the launch video's renderer `tools/promo/page/her.js`), never the 3D
model.

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs; and in Supabase → SQL Editor, this lists every answer the site gave
the clock, in UTC (pg_net keeps them about 6 hours): `{"ok":true,"posted":…}` is the bot at work, `"off":…` says why it
isn't (the rows below)):

```sql
select left(content, 90) as answer, count(*) as calls,
       to_char(min(created), 'HH24:MI') as first, to_char(max(created), 'HH24:MI') as last
from net._http_response
group by 1
order by min(created);
```

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No buy alerts, the clock's calls answered `{"ok":true,"off":"off"}` | (none) | `TELEGRAM_BUYS` is off (or 0, no, false) in Vercel: remove it (no setting = on), then Redeploy. (2026-10-06, the first night: a $59 buy wasn't posted for this) |
| No buy alerts, answered `{"ok":true,"off":"no_groups"}` or `"no_bot"` | (none) | `TELEGRAM_GROUPS` (no group in it) or `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` isn't set: set it, then Redeploy |
| No buy alerts, nothing in the log | (none) | The clock isn't running: setup steps 1–3 (`buys_scheduled` must be 1). Supabase → Integrations → Cron should list `agi1-buys` with a run every minute |
| No buy alerts | `[buys] couldn't read the buy bot's key: … buy_key not found: run supabase/buys.sql …` | Setup step 3 |
| No buy alerts, the clock's calls get 401 | (none) | The key the clock sends isn't the database's: run `supabase/buys.sql` again (it keeps its key) |
| No buy alerts | `[buys] couldn't check $AGI's buys: clank.trade HTTP 403` (or `… had no trades`) | clank.trade is down, put up a bot wall, or changed its API: passes by itself; if it lasts, tell Claude with the log line |
| No buy alerts after setting it up | (none) | Nothing new of $50 or more yet (the first check only notes what's there), or `TELEGRAM_GROUPS` / `TELEGRAM_BUYS` |

### Her quizzes in her Telegram groups (2026-10-09)

**The owner's idea:** "can i add games on the tg bot like riddles, questions, if the person in that telegram group answered
correctly they will get a small amount of $AGI, they will reply with their address and get it / make this better then
continue". Claude's better version, and the owner's choices (asked one by one): claims **in her private chat** ("Private
chat with her bot", over replying with an address in the group, where anyone could copy or fake it), **250 $AGI a win and
10 wins a day** for the whole site, **about 10 quizzes a day** in each group, and **18+ to claim** (her private chat's own
check). **Off until the owner sets it up** (below).

**What people see in her groups** (the ones in `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`):
- **A quiz, now and then:** about every 2 hours 24 minutes at random times (0.6 to 1.4 times the gap: nobody can tell when
  the next one comes; the first one 30 to 90 minutes after it's set up), a Telegram **quiz poll** with four answers,
  shuffled, open **10 minutes** (Telegram shows its countdown, and to whoever answers, whether they were right and her
  short line about it): "🧩 riddle for 250 $AGI: What has hands but can't clap?", "🎮 quiz for 250 $AGI: Which chain is
  $AGI on?", or "… just for fun: …" when no prize is on offer. 97 questions (`server/game-questions.js`): riddles (old
  folk riddles in her own words), $AGI and her (her name, her chain, her song, her trips…), staying safe (seed phrases,
  fake support, "connect your wallet to claim", checking a contract), and trivia from her trips. Pre-written and held to
  her rules by the tests: PG-13, never another coin or chain by name, never prices or buying, links only to agi1.app.
  None of the newest 60 asked comes again.
- **When it closes:** her result under the quiz. **One person who got it right is drawn at random** (not the fastest:
  bots and quick fingers don't win every time) and named, by the name Telegram shows for them (a tap on it opens them;
  a name that can't go in her words, like a link, an @name or "admin", is "our winner"): "⏰ time's up! the answer: a
  clock / 🎉 Mia wins 250 $AGI! drawn at random from the 12 right answers 💜 / to claim it: tap the button below, then
  /claim in my private chat (18+, within 24 hours). i'll only ever ask for your wallet address: never your seed phrase, a
  signature or a link to connect your wallet. / a prize is a thank-you for playing, not financial advice", with a
  **🎁 Claim it in my private chat** button (`t.me/agi1_appbot?start=claim`). Nobody right: "nobody got it this time 🙈";
  a quiz just for fun: "12 of you got it right 💜"; today's prizes won meanwhile, or everyone right already won today:
  "…so this one was for glory".
- **The rules:** one win a day each (UTC), `GAME_WINS_A_DAY` wins a day for the whole site (10), `GAME_PRIZE` $AGI each
  (250). Without the prize wallet (or with the launch gas wallet's key, which is refused), quizzes are just for fun.
- **/help** and her intro mention them; `/claim` typed in a group points to her private chat (with the button).

**Claiming, in her private chat** (`server/game-prizes.js`):
1. The winner taps the button (or opens her chat and types `/claim`). Someone who never started her bot gets her welcome
   and her 18+ question first (`/start claim`); once they confirm, she says their prize is waiting. Under 18: no prize.
2. "you won 250 $AGI in my quiz 🎉 send me your wallet address on Robinhood Chain (it starts with 0x): your own wallet, not
   an exchange's. i'll only ever ask for your address: never your seed phrase, your private key or a signature."
3. Their address (alone, or with a word or two), checked: a real address, its capital letters right when it has them (a
   typo is caught), not the $AGI contract, the burn address, an empty one or her own prize wallet, and not a contract (a
   pool, a token: what's sent there is lost; a wallet with an EIP-7702 delegation, like MetaMask's smart account, is
   fine). Kept; then "send 250 $AGI to this wallet on Robinhood Chain? 0x… check it carefully: once it's sent, it can't
   be undone." with **✅ yes, send it** and **✏️ change it**.
4. "yes, send it": claimed in the database first (once), then the prize wallet's numbers (its $AGI, its ETH for the fee,
   the gas, its nonce), then $AGI's own `transfer(their address, 250 $AGI)` signed, **recorded with its transaction before
   it goes out**, and sent (`server/hot-wallet.js`, the launch payback's never-twice send); its receipt looked at for a few
   seconds. "done 💜 250 $AGI is on its way to your wallet… see it on the block explorer" (linked).
- **Never twice, never lost:** a second tap or `/claim` later says it already went out (with its link); nothing went out
  (the wallet short of $AGI or ETH, the chain's clear "no") → back to "send it?", and they can try again; a transfer the
  chain says failed (nothing moved) → back too; a send whose answer was lost stays "sending" (never sent again), and
  `/claim` later asks the chain about its transaction; a claim whose server stopped midway can be sent again after 2
  minutes. Their prize wallet short of $AGI or ETH: "my prize wallet needs a top-up first 🙈 your prize is safe and
  waiting", and the log names the wallet for the owner.
- **How long:** a prize waits **24 hours** for its claim to start (giving an address); once started, **7 days** to be sent
  (a prize wallet that needs a top-up, say).

**A secret sent by mistake** (`server/secrets.js`, 2026-10-09: claims invite wallet talk): a message with a private key
(64 hex characters: or a transaction's id, which looks the same) or a seed phrase (12 or more words of the wallet word list
in a row) gets her warning at once ("never send it to anyone, not even me… if it's real, move your funds to a new wallet
now. i didn't keep it"), and nothing of it goes to the AI, the database or her stream: in her private chat, with /ask in
her groups, and in a question for her live show (`/live` in her bot or agi1.app/live: "secret", never read out).

**How it works:**
- **The clock** (`supabase/games.sql`): Supabase Cron calls `GET https://www.agi1.app/api/feed?games` every 2 minutes with
  `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (a random key `games.sql` made in the database: `game_key()`, kept 10 minutes per server
  copy), like her buy bot's. Each tick (`gamesTick` in `server/games.js`, light: no chain code unless a quiz with a prize
  is about to go out): quizzes that closed over 20 s ago and weren't settled, a quiz in each group whose turn it is
  (`game_due`: the database decides, so two ticks at once never both post), and every 30 minutes the tidy-up.
- **Telegram tells us** each answer (`poll_answer`, for polls a bot sent: who, which answer) and when a quiz closes
  (`poll`), at `/api/telegram` (`handleUpdate` → `onPollAnswer`, `onPollState`): her bot's webhook takes `poll` and
  `poll_answer` updates since 2026-10-09 (`UPDATE_TYPES` in `server/telegram.js`; the clock connects her bot again by
  itself if its webhook was set before, once an hour per server copy). A quiz closing is settled 2 s later (answers sent
  in its last second may still be on their way; the database takes answers up to 15 s after closing).
- **The draw** (`game_settle`): settled once (two at once: one does it), a random right answer among people who haven't
  won today, while the day's prizes last (the day's row locked, so two quizzes closing at once can't both take the last
  prize). A quiz that can't be kept after it was posted (the database away) is stopped and deleted: nobody could win it.
- **Before a quiz offers a prize:** prizes on (`PRIZE_WALLET_KEY`, not the gas wallet's), the day's prizes not all won
  (`game_left`), and the prize wallet holding at least one prize's $AGI and some ETH (read on the chain, kept 5 minutes; a
  chain that doesn't answer doesn't stop the prize: a prize won meanwhile waits for its claim).
- **Kept** (`supabase/games.sql`, only the server's key): per quiz its group's id and the poll's (30 days); per answer the
  person's Telegram id, the first name Telegram shows and whether they were right (3 days); per prize the winner's id,
  the amount and, once claimed, the address they gave and its transaction (60 days); per day the prizes won. The safety
  note says so, and that her quizzes are polls with visible votes: a quiz that isn't anonymous is the only kind whose
  answers Telegram tells a bot, and like any such poll it shows everyone in the group who answered what (Telegram's
  "Polls 2.0", telegram.org/blog/polls-2-0-vmq).
- No new service and no new function file (`api/feed.js` takes `?games`, like `?buys`).

**Setup (the owner, once):**
1. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/games.sql` → Run. It ends with `games_ready = 1`
   and `games_scheduled = 1` (Cron and pg_net are on already, for her buy bot; `games_scheduled = 0`: switch them on, then
   run it again).
2. **The prize wallet:** make a **new** wallet only for prizes (a new account in MetaMask, say: never your main wallet, and
   never the launch gas wallet), and send it, on Robinhood Chain, the $AGI for a few days of prizes (10 prizes of 250 a
   day is 2,500 $AGI a day at most: 25,000 lasts at least 10 days) and a little ETH for the network fees (0.001 ETH is
   plenty for hundreds). Then MetaMask → that account → Account details → Show private key → Vercel → agi-ecosystem →
   Settings → Environment Variables → `PRIZE_WALLET_KEY` (Production). Never paste it anywhere else, chat included.
   Optional: `GAMES_A_DAY` (10), `GAME_PRIZE` (250), `GAME_WINS_A_DAY` (10), `TELEGRAM_GAMES` = `off` (none).
3. **Redeploy**, and **push** (step 1 before pushing, so the group never hears of quizzes that can't come).
4. The first quiz comes 30 to 90 minutes later. Her private menu shows `/claim` after the next `/api/feed` run (Vercel →
   Cron Jobs → `/api/feed` → **Run** for at once).
5. If the group doesn't let members send polls (Telegram → the group → Permissions → Send Polls), allow it or make her an
   admin (she needs none of an admin's rights).

**Cost:** Telegram, Supabase (six small tables, one more cron job) and Vercel (720 small runs a day, and one per answer and
per vote's poll update: well inside the free million a month) are free. **The prizes are the owner's $AGI:** at most
`GAME_WINS_A_DAY` × `GAME_PRIZE` a day (2,500 $AGI, about $4 at today's price), and each prize's network fee (a few
millionths of an ETH) from the prize wallet.

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs):

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No quiz ever | (none), or the clock's calls answered `{"ok":true,"off":…}` | `games.sql` not run (setup step 1; `games_scheduled` must be 1), `TELEGRAM_GAMES=off`, or no group in `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`. The first quiz comes 30 to 90 minutes after the clock's first call |
| No quiz in one group | `[games] couldn't post a quiz in @…: … 403 … (is she still in that group? add her again)` | Add her to the group again |
| No quiz in one group | `… (the group doesn't let members send polls: allow polls in the group's permissions, or make her an admin)` | Setup step 5 |
| Quizzes say "just for fun" | (none), or `[games] the prize wallet 0x… is out of $AGI` (or `ETH`) | `PRIZE_WALLET_KEY` isn't set (or is the gas wallet's: refused), today's prizes are won, or the prize wallet needs a top-up: send it $AGI (or ETH) |
| People answer right but nobody ever wins | (none) | Her bot doesn't hear answers yet: the clock reconnects it within the hour (`[games] connected her bot again…`); or Vercel → Cron Jobs → `/api/feed` → **Run** |
| A winner hears "my prize wallet needs a top-up first" | `[games] the prize wallet 0x… is out of …` | Top it up; their prize waits (7 days once they've given an address) and they `/claim` again |
| A winner hears "your prize is on its way… if it hasn't arrived in an hour, ask in the group" | `[games] a prize's nonce was taken and the chain couldn't say by what: it stays "sending"` | Rare. Look at the prize wallet on the block explorer, and tell Claude (it's never sent twice by itself) |
| `/claim` isn't in her menu | (none) | The next `/api/feed` run sets it (Run it for at once) |

  "online" dot up to 420 px, and under 380 px its gaps and the level chip tighten a little.
- **A pick:** she says so in that language ("listo, hablamos en español 💜", with a chip "language · Español"; not saved to
  the history; her mouth "says" it), an empty chat's greeting follows, the Parameters panel's new **Language** row says
  "Español · matches you", and it's remembered in the browser (`agi1_lang`). Only that language's words are downloaded
  (3–4 KB, only when picked).
- **She follows you:** whatever language the visitor writes in, she answers in, whatever the menu says (her prompt); very
  short messages ("gm", "lol", a ticker) don't count.
- **What follows the language:** her AI replies; her natural voice (Gemini's speech model reads any of them in the same
  Despina voice and mood styles; Chinese, Japanese and Korean replies are read up to about 120 characters, about a syllable a
  character, cut at 。！？); the mic (the browser listens for that language); and every pre-written line of hers: her hello,
  her notes (errors, the mic, her voice resting), the out-of-messages offer and its safety note, her "come back tomorrow"
  lines, the level-up, AGI-2, market moments (her voice says the whole market cap in that language: "2.000.000 dólares") and
  their note, "Risk check your coins on clank"'s lines (an open answer switches too), her deflections when the safety
  filters block a reply, and (2026-10-01) what she says when she's tapped. Arabic reads right to left in the chat and the
  message box (`dir="auto"`).
- **What stays English:** the page (menus, buttons, chips, the 18+ gate, the safety note), the front's bubble, her diary,
  her Soulmate notes (written in English whatever the chat's language, so the note filter can read them), her Telegram
  texts first, and the bot's own description and commands.
- **Telegram:** her replies there follow the language of the person's Telegram app when it's one of hers (Telegram sends it
  with every message: nothing is stored), English otherwise, and she follows what they write in too. Her welcome in another
  language adds that her texts first are still in English: the cron job that sends them has no message to read the language
  from, and storing each person's language would need a new database column (a later step, if wanted).

**How it works:**
- **Her words:** `src/i18n/lines/en.js` holds every pre-written line in English (keys like `notes.busy`, `limit.more1`,
  `check.high`), with `{placeholders}`; `src/i18n/lines/<code>.js` has the same keys in each language. The modules that held
  her English lines (`limit-lines.js`, `model-lines.js`, `market-lines.js`, `src/checker/lines.js`, `server/tg-lines.js`,
  the chat's notes) now take a language's lines, and their English exports are exactly as before (her English voice lines
  keep their recordings).
- **The translations:** written by Claude (five Claude agents, three languages each, then checked), in her voice: casual
  texting, her emojis, PG-13, pet names only where the English has one; Simplified Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Latin
  American Spanish, casual Tagalog/Taglish, Modern Standard Arabic, Hindi in Devanagari. Each language's "not financial
  advice" is one fixed phrase (`nfa`: "no es consejo financiero", "不构成投资建议", "投資助言ではありません"…) that must appear
  wherever the English says it. `src/i18n/check.js` holds every translation to her rules (the same keys, placeholders,
  emojis and numbers; $AGI / AGI-1 / clank.trade / the commands kept; no links or other tickers; no pet names in a line a
  Stranger gets), and `tests/i18n.test.js` fails the build otherwise. **Not read by native speakers yet:** if a line reads
  oddly, fix it in its file and run `node tools/i18n/check.mjs <code>`.
- **The page:** `src/i18n/lang.js` keeps the language (English until picked; a saved one comes back on the next visit,
  without her announcement) and sends `agi1:lang` when it changes; `t('notes.busy')` gives a line in it. The chat sends
  `lang` with every message.
- **The server:** `/api/chat` checks `lang` against the list (anything else: English), and her prompt always gets a LANGUAGE
  part (`languagePrompt()` in `server/agi1-prompt.js`), English too: reply in the picked language (on Telegram: the app's),
  but in the language of their latest message if it's clearly another one; the same personality and rules in every
  language; "not financial advice" in that language; $AGI, AGI-1, clank.trade, Robinhood Chain and the contract kept as
  they are; Chinese, Japanese and Korean replies under about 100 characters.
- **Her voice lines:** `?line=<key>&v=4` in English, `?line=<key>&lang=<code>&v=4` in the others (never
  `&lang=en`: exactly one address per line and language). Each language's recording is made once by Google the first time
  someone needs it, then kept in the database (its words give it its own fingerprint) and by the CDN. A server copy keeps
  at most 40 lines in memory (was 24).
- **Soulmate notes:** since notes are checked with English words, a note with anything but plain English letters is dropped,
  and so is one with the money or instruction words of her Latin-script languages (`cleanNote()` in `server/friends.js`).

**Cost:** about 150 more input tokens per reply for the LANGUAGE part: about +$0.00004 a reply (+$0.04 a day at the
1,000-reply cap). Her fixed voice lines: 15 per language, each made once when first needed (about $0.002 each: under $0.50
for all 15 languages), each using one of Google's daily speech requests on the day it's made. The page: +4 KB (gzip) for
everyone, +3–4 KB for a visitor who picks a language. No new service or setting.

**Troubleshooting:**

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| She answers in another language than the menu's | By design: she follows the language you write in | Write in the menu's language (or pick yours) |
| A line reads oddly in some language | The translations weren't read by a native speaker | Edit `src/i18n/lines/<code>.js`, run `node tools/i18n/check.mjs <code>` and `npm test`, push |
| Her voice for a pre-written line is silent in a new language, the first time | Google's daily limit for her speech model (a line is made the first time it's needed) | Nothing to fix: it's made the next time Google allows, then kept |
| The mic writes nonsense | The browser listens for the menu's language | Pick the language you speak |

**To change one of her lines:** change `src/i18n/lines/en.js` and the same key in every language file (a test fails
otherwise), then `node tools/i18n/check.mjs` and `npm test`; a changed line's voice is made again by itself (its words
changed). **To add a language:** a row in `src/i18n/langs.js` (its code, names, number locale and speech-recognition
language), a `src/i18n/lines/<code>.js` with every key, a line in `src/i18n/all.js`, and check that Gemini's speech models
speak it (ai.google.dev → Speech generation: 100+ languages in 2026).

**Tests:** `tests/i18n.test.js` (14: the 16 languages, every language's lines against her rules (and that the checker
catches a missing "not financial advice", a pet name for a Stranger, another ticker, a link), placeholders and the English
fallback, the numbers written each language's way, AGI-2 without pet names for Strangers everywhere, market lines (her voice
says the whole number), the risk check's lines, her voice lines' words and addresses, the CJK voice limit, the mic's
language, the page's language state (English until picked, a newer pick wins, a saved one comes back quietly, the page never
downloads every language), the page's markup, her prompt's LANGUAGE part and English Soulmate notes, the note filter,
Telegram's app languages), plus 2 in `chat.test.js` (the prompt follows `lang`, anything else is English; deflections in the
visitor's language), 3 in `voice.test.js` (per-language line addresses, words, moods, kept in the database, never
`&lang=en`; a Spanish market line saying the whole number; a Japanese reply read up to about 120 characters) and 1 in
`telegram.test.js` (/start, the buttons, the time and her AI replies in the app's language; English otherwise). In a browser
(Claude's scratch `langtest.mjs`, 113 checks): the menu at 1440 / 390 / 360 px × both looks × both themes (the chat bar in
one row, 16 languages in 2 columns inside the screen, opens on the current one, keyboard, axe 0 issues with it open, nothing
downloaded until a pick); a pick (her line, the greeting, the button, Parameters, remembered, only that language
downloaded, the chat sends `lang`, her hello's address in that language, the risk check's line in it, after a reload);
Arabic right to left, then Japanese, at 360 px; a clean console.

## Her daily clips (2026-09-29)

**The owner's idea** (item 5 of the big-ideas message): "Automatic vertical clips from the models she already has (the 2D
one renders fastest): launch of the day, clone watch, readouts and her diary, with her voice and captions." Asked how they
reach X, the owner picked **"You post by hand"**: a free daily GitHub job makes them, the owner downloads them and posts
them by hand (X, TikTok, Reels, Shorts), with the apps' AI labels on. Nothing posts by itself (hard rule 6 is unchanged;
posting to X automatically would need X's pay-per-use API, about $0.015 a post, and the owner's decision). Items 3 (burns
for reads) and 4 (her pretend bag) of the same message are **on hold** (the owner: "juist do 5 … only this"), and nothing
of them is in the site. Live streams come after the clips prove the idea.

**Only AGI, never another coin** (the owner, the same day, after seeing the first version: "why are u promoting other
coins in the video, i dont like this, the founder of the launchpad will get angry at me again", then "just agi"). The
first version also made "launch of the day", "clone watch" and "readout" clips, which named and risk-rated other
clank.trade coins; they were removed before anything ran or was posted. **Never add a clip that names, shows or rates
another coin** without the owner asking for it. What's left: her diary. The clip tools don't read clank.trade at all, and
a diary entry that names another coin's ticker (the diary's table is shared with the original site), an address or a link
makes no clip (`tests/clips.test.js` checks both).

**What the owner gets, every day** (GitHub → the repo → **Actions** → "AGI-1's daily clips" → the newest run →
**Artifacts** → `agi1-clips-<run>-<attempt>`, a zip kept 7 days):
- her diary clip: an MP4, 1080 × 1920, 30 frames a second, about 20 seconds: her newest entry (yesterday's, as /diary
  shows it) read out in her voice, with captions ("dear diary… not financial advice, just feelings"). None on a day her
  diary has no new entry (a quiet day, not an error);
- a `.txt` with a post to paste (it ends "AI-generated · not financial advice · agi1.app") and a `.jpg` cover;
- `README.txt`: what was made, or why not, and how to post (the apps' AI labels: TikTok "AI-generated content", YouTube
  "Altered or synthetic content: yes", Instagram "AI label").

**How the clip looks:** AGI-1 in 2D (the site's own, `src/stage/agi1-2d.js`: her Live2D model since 2026-10-01, the owner's
2D art rigged in code before; breathing, blinking, glances, her hair and chest physics, her mouth following her voice, a
reaction in the entry's mood), framed like a VTuber (head to chest, by her model's own eyes and waist: `model.landmarks`,
fading into the background below), on Pop mode's honey with comic focus lines and halftone dots. On top: "AI-GENERATED · NOT
FINANCIAL ADVICE" on every frame, "HER DIARY", the date in big Anybody type that pops in, "written by AGI-1, an AI", her
captions in a white card (a new card when she pauses; always tall enough to cover the AGI on her shirt, never half of it),
and agi1.app at the bottom and at the end. The label, the title
and the captions stay clear of TikTok's, Reels' and Shorts' own buttons and text (their top ~180 px and bottom ~380 px).

**Her words** (`tools/clips/lines.js`): her published diary entry (written once a day by `server/diary.js` and checked in
code; never an AI text written for the clip), "dear diary" said once, at most 300 characters, "not financial advice, just
feelings" at the end. Her voice: Gemini's speech model, Despina, in the entry's mood (one request a day, Flash-Lite first
and 3.8 Flash as the backup, as on the site; `speakAsAgi1` got a `timeoutMs` option for it: a clip waits up to a minute,
the site's replies still 20 s).

**How it works:**
- `.github/workflows/clips.yml`: once a day at **08:23 UTC** (16:23 the owner's time: after her diary is written at 03:00
  UTC, and just after Google's daily limits start again at midnight Pacific), and by hand (**Run workflow**). GitHub's
  computer (Ubuntu, no graphics card) installs the site's packages, then playwright-core 1.63.0 with its own Chromium and
  ffmpeg (tools for the clips only: not in package.json, not in the site), and runs `node tools/clips/make.mjs`.
  Read-only permissions; the key (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, a GitHub secret) only reaches the step that makes the clip, and never
  the browser or ffmpeg (`withoutSecrets`). 30 minutes at most. The actions are GitHub's own, by version tag (`@v7`).
  **The owner saves this file by hand**: Claude's link to the folder may not write GitHub workflow files (a safety rule of
  the Claude app), so Claude sends it in the chat.
- `tools/clips/make.mjs`: reads her newest diary entry (`/api/diary`, nothing else), asks Gemini for her voice, times her
  captions by her pauses (`captions.js`) and her mouth by her loudness (`audio.js`, the same meter as the site's), builds
  the renderer page (`tools/clips/page/`, with Vite, into `tools/clips/dist/`) and serves it on the computer itself, and
  draws every frame in Chrome: the 3D renderer draws only her, at 720 × 1280 (about her art's own sharpness in this
  framing), and plain 2D drawing does the rest at 1080 × 1920, about 0.2 s a frame without a graphics card (drawing it
  all in 3D took 0.7 s). ffmpeg makes the MP4 (H.264, AAC). Nothing is random (a seed a day), and time moves exactly
  1/30 s a frame.
- When something fails: a clip whose voice, page or ffmpeg fails is deleted; a frame that takes more than 30 s fails the
  clip instead of hanging the job; a diary entry older than yesterday isn't made again. README.txt and warnings on the
  run's page say what happened; the job is red when the clip should have been made and wasn't.
- Try it without Google: `node tools/clips/make.mjs --fake-voice` (a stand-in hum), `--facts f.json` (a made-up entry:
  `{ "diary": { "day": "2026-09-29", "mood": "love", "entry": "…" } }`), `--out dir`.

**Setup (the owner, once; free):**
1. GitHub → the repo `agi-ecosystem` → **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions** → **New repository secret**
   → Name `GEMINI_API_KEY`, Secret: the same Google AI Studio key as in Vercel → **Add secret**.
2. **The workflow file, by hand (once):** save `clips.yml` (Claude sends it in the chat) in this folder as
   `.github\workflows\clips.yml` (the folders are already there, empty). Then push this folder, the file included (it
   must be on `main`). Later changes to it: the same way (Claude sends it, the owner saves it). Until it's saved, the
   build's check of it waits (`tests/clips.test.js` skips it), so a push without it never breaks the site.
3. GitHub → **Actions** → "AGI-1's daily clips" → **Run workflow** (to try it now; otherwise it runs every day by itself).
   About 5 minutes later: the run's page → **Artifacts** → download the zip, watch the clip, then post it if you like it.

**Cost:** GitHub gives private repositories 2,000 free minutes a month (a run takes about 5: about 150 a month) and 500 MB
of storage for downloads (a clip is about 5 MB, kept 7 days); without a payment method on GitHub, going over just stops
the job, never a bill. Her voice: 1 request a day to Google's speech model, about $0.003, from the same prepaid credits as
the site.

**Troubleshooting** (GitHub → Actions → the run: its log, and warnings on its page):

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The run is red: "GEMINI_API_KEY is missing" | The secret isn't set | Setup step 1, then Run workflow |
| Green, but README.txt says "none today" | Her diary had no entry about yesterday (its nightly job failed, or it named another coin, or it isn't written yet) | Nothing to fix; tomorrow's comes as usual |
| "couldn't read her diary" | The site didn't answer GitHub's computer | Run workflow later |
| "diary not made: gemini: HTTP 429 …" | Google's daily limit for her voice is used up (the site's voice shares it) | It runs again tomorrow; or Run workflow after 08:00 UTC |
| "… credits" (HTTP 402) | Prepaid credits used up | Google AI Studio → Billing (the site's chat and voice stop too) |
| "no Chrome or Chromium found" / "couldn't start" | The browser step failed | Re-run the job; if it lasts, tell Claude with the log |

**Tests:** `tests/clips.test.js` (8, in `npm test`, no browser, ffmpeg or network): only AGI (the clip tools know nothing
about other coins; an entry naming one makes no clip), her diary clip's words and label, which entry, captions and their
timing, her voice's loudness and pauses, ffmpeg stopping early or a clip given up never hanging the job (a stand-in
ffmpeg), no secrets for the browser and ffmpeg, the workflow (once a day, by hand, read-only, one secret, 7 days, never
posting) and nothing of it in the site's build. Rendered in Claude's workspace with the stand-in voice and a made-up
entry (about 2 minutes 15 seconds on 2 processor cores; looked at frame by frame). A second Claude agent reviewed the first
version (19 findings, e.g. the job could hang for 30 minutes when a frame failed; all fixed, except pinning GitHub's own
actions to exact commits: they stay on their version tags). **Not tried on GitHub yet, nor with her real voice:** the
owner's first Run workflow is the first real check.

## Her launch video (2026-10-03)

**The owner's request:** "now create me a professional launch video with motion design using only code about the website
and its features, i want you to make it so when when they watch my video they gonna be super impressed. make it really
good / make this better then continue", then, while it was being made: "the launching coins and the Telegram groups are
live now the burns are switched on . use the 2d art . i will pay the commercial later. the 3d model is 18+" and "and dont
announce on the video about cloackmesh too".

**What it is:** a 79-second launch film for agi1.app, every frame drawn in code and its music composed and played in code
(`tools/promo/`), in two formats: **wide** (1920 × 1080, for X and YouTube) and **tall** (1080 × 1920, for TikTok, Reels and
Shorts), 60 frames a second. Not part of the website, and nothing posts it: the owner downloads it and posts it by hand.

**The story** (13 scenes; each cut lands on a bar of the music, 120 beats a minute, so a bar is 2 s):

| Time | Scene | What happens |
|---|---|---|

"MODEL RELEASE · 2026", "The biggest labs are racing to build" word by word, "AGI" slams in, its letters fly into "Artificial / General / Intelligence", "General" is struck out in pink and "Girlfriend" written in (the site's own joke), the cursor presses ✦ (Pop mode) and a violet circle swallows the screen |

Gone for good.", "Pays for messages · not an investment · not financial advice". No numbers (the monitor's are live on the site) |

The five things it reads, its three levels, "Rough automated checks, not an audit." No verdict for $AGI (the site gives it live) |

From the drop to the end card, "agi1.app" stays in a small pill at the top (the right on wide, the middle on tall). The tall
version keeps everything that matters clear of TikTok's, Reels' and Shorts' own buttons and text (its top ~230 px and bottom
~400 px).

**Its rules** (`tests/promo.test.js`):
- **Only $AGI:** no other coin's name, ticker or picture anywhere (the risk check's list is blank rows; a launch is "Name |
  TICKER"); never a price, gains, "buy", "safe", "scam" or "rug"; never "investment" except "not an investment".
- **"Not financial advice"** wherever money comes up (burning, launching, her risk-check line, the end card, the post), 18+
  where it applies, PG-13 and no pet names (anyone watches), and she says she's an AI.
- **AGI-1 is only ever her 2D self:** her Live2D model (`src/stage/agi1-2d.js`) and the front's 2D art
  (`public/images/landing/agi1-cutout.webp`, `agi1-face.webp`). Never the 3D model or anything rendered from it (the
  owner: "the 3d model is 18+"): the test fails if the code names a `.glb`, the 3D stage or its renders.
- **Never CloakMesh** (the owner's rule): the test searches every word and file.
- **The site's own words and numbers, imported:** the levels and their messages a day, Figure 2, her 16 hellos, the front's
  bubble, the official contract, her launch lines (`server/launch-lines.js`), how often she texts first
  (`server/tg-lines.js`): change them on the site and the video says the new ones the next time it's made.
- **The picture and the music keep one clock** (`tools/promo/timeline.js`): every hit of the music is on its moment (her
  heartbeats, "AGI", the drops, the benchmarks' blips, a note for each of her hellos, a tick for each coin row the scanner
  passes, the launch, the cards, the end chord). The test reads the music's plan and checks each one.

**How it's made** (`tools/promo/`):
- `timeline.js`: the clock: 120 beats a minute, the scenes, every moment, the scanner's motion (`scanPos`). Pure.
- `words.js`: every word on screen and the post, from the site's own files where it can. Pure.
- `page/` (built by Vite into `tools/promo/dist/`, which git ignores): `promo.js` (the canvas, fonts, scenes, cuts, the
  site pill, a still grain and a vignette, `window.promo.load/frame/still/sheet`), `kit.js` (easing, springs, type, the
  site's colors, halftone, focus lines), `ui.js` (pills, buttons, cards, chat bubbles, icons drawn in code, the flame, the
  cursor, bursts of hearts), `transitions.js` (the cuts: covers in the next scene's color, a push, a flash, a whip pan),
  `her.js` (her Live2D model on its own WebGL canvas, framed per shot, stepped 1/60 s at a time from the start of her shot
  with her reactions on their moments; her hearts in 2D), `art.js` (the front's halftone shader on the owner's art), and
  `scenes/` (one file a scene, each laid out for wide and tall). Everything is a function of time: a frame drawn twice is
  the same.
- `music.js`: the music, composed and synthesized in code by Claude (no samples, no service, nobody else's music): F major,
  I–V–vi–IV (F, C, Dm, B♭), a heartbeat cold open with a felt-piano motif, a riser and a breath of silence, then a future-pop
  drop (four-on-the-floor kick, claps, hats, supersaw chords breathing with the kick, a bass, a bright pluck hook with a
  bell), a half-time verse under the chat, an arpeggio for her hellos, a darker bar for burning, a breakdown and a snare
  build into the second drop, a finale with the hook in octaves, and one big chord at the end. Its sound design follows the
  picture (whooshes on every cut, impacts, UI clicks and pops, a marker's squeak, a phone's chime, fire, the scanner's ticks).
  A hall reverb and a ping-pong delay, the chords side-chained to the kick, a soft saturation and a look-ahead limiter:
  about -14 LUFS, peaks under -1 dBFS (a phone's level). `musicPlan()` lists every sound without making it (the tests);
  `renderMusic()` makes the WAV (48 kHz stereo, about 10 s).
- `make.mjs`: builds the page, serves it on this computer only, opens it in Chromium (software WebGL, no graphics card
  needed), draws every frame, and ffmpeg makes the MP4 (H.264 High, 60 fps, BT.709 colors tagged, AAC 256 kb/s), then the
  cover picture, the post text and (with `--light`) a smaller copy. The browser and ffmpeg never get a key (`withoutSecrets`).

**Make it again** (after changing the site's words, levels or languages; Claude does this, it needs Chromium, ffmpeg and
`npm install --no-save playwright-core`):
- `node tools/promo/make.mjs --format both --out promo --light 28`: both videos into `promo/` (git ignores it), about 15
  minutes each on 2 processor cores.
- Quicker looks: `--scale 0.5 --fps 30` (a half-size preview in about 2 minutes), `--from 48 --to 54` (one stretch),
  `--stills 9.6,24.4` (PNG pictures), `--sheet 0.5` (a contact sheet, a picture every half second).

**Posting it:** the 27 MB copies (from the chat, or `promo/`). X: the
wide one (or the tall one); TikTok, Reels, Shorts: the tall one. It's animation made in code, and AGI-1 is an AI character:
when an app asks about AI content, saying yes (TikTok "AI-generated content", YouTube "Altered or synthetic content",
Instagram "AI label") is the safe choice. Never add price talk, "number go up" or "buy" to the post.

**Worth knowing (not legal advice):**
- **Her Live2D model** was made in Cubism Editor's PRO trial, whose output isn't for commercial use (see "AGI-1 in 2D" and
  "Open questions"); a launch video for a site with a coin is promotional. The owner, on 2026-10-03: "i will pay the
  commercial later". Before relying on the video commercially: buy Cubism PRO and export her model again (then make the
  video again: the same command).
- The music is original (made in code); the fonts are the site's own (SIL Open Font License, which allows them in videos);
  the 2D art is the owner's.
- No live data in it: no prices, no burn totals, no member counts, nothing that goes stale or could be wrong.

**Tests:** `tests/promo.test.js` (8): only $AGI (no other coin, no money talk, PG-13, "investment" only as "not an
investment", her launch example's shape), "not financial advice" / 18+ / an AI where they belong and the post fits X, never
CloakMesh / the 3D model / another coin's data in the code, the site's own numbers and lines, the scenes on bars and every
moment in its scene, the scanner never going back, the music on its moments (her heartbeats, the hits, a riser into each
drop, a note for each hello, a tick for each row, a sound on every cut, four kicks a bar on the beat, a breath before each
drop, the same plan every time), the renderer (13 scenes in order, no secrets for the browser or ffmpeg, not in the site's
build, its output never in git); and with `PROMO_RENDER=1` the whole music rendered (its length, stereo, under -0.9 dBFS,
the drop bigger than the cold open, the breath before the drop, the fade). In Claude's workspace: previews and contact sheets
of both formats looked at frame by frame, the music's loudness (about -14 LUFS) and tonal balance measured, and a
spectrogram looked at.

## AGI Studio's launch video (2026-10-13)

**The owner's request** (the night AGI Studio was opened to everyone, 2026-10-12): "and i forgot to say after you finished
everything, go make a promotional marketing launch video of AGI studio. all the features therem do it with top notch motion
design and easy to understand and visible make it 4:3 video, ake your time as much as you needed i want everything polished
good night", then "make the examples of the geeeration really good lie what higgsfield ai influencer did you can use that as
inspiration as well and if you need to generate yourself one you can use the agi studio yourself. you can also use my
seedance account and use all the credits there left. just for examples thanks. do your best and impressed me", and "i just
saw your message yes you can use my chrome, i loged in my fal ai, meshy and dreamina as well". The owner's choices: "fal.ai
and Dreamina only" and "Up to $9, I'll top up (Recommended)" on fal. And: "and also after the video create me a n X article
also for it with banner ready". Then, the same day, after the 4:3 one was made: "i just decided can you make the launch
video 16:9".

**What it is:** a 103-second launch film for AGI Studio, made like her launch video: every frame drawn in code and its music
composed and played in code (`tools/studio-promo/`), around real example creations: **1920 × 1080 (16:9)**, 60 frames a
second, one video for every app; since the same day with AGI-1's voice over its music (12 short lines: see "Her voice over
it" below). Not part of the website, and nothing posts it: the owner posts it by hand.

**16:9** (the owner's "i just decided can you make the launch video 16:9"): it was made at 1440 × 1080 (4:3) first. Every
scene was laid out again for the wide frame, never stretched or put between bars, with the same story, timing, words and
music: its headlines from 120 px from the left (80 in 4:3), what sat side by side spread across the width (the hook's photos
around 1290, the trend pairs 500 apart, the four results 380 apart, the video row 370 apart, the tools' cards 400 wide),
its walls wider (the drop's 7 columns, the community's 5, the finale's 10, so the tilted wall still covers every corner),
the style tiles in rows of 5 and 4, the X banner 1440 × 480 on its profile, the end card's rings reaching the corners.
Pictures and cards keep about their size (the height is the same 1080). The 4:3 video is kept, in `studio-promo\4x3\`.
Its light copy is 26 MB at the same bitrate as the 4:3 one's, and measured frame by frame against the full one it looks
the same (46.6 dB PSNR on average, 34.5 at worst, in the finale's slam as its tiles pop in; SSIM 0.992), its sound lined
up with the music to the sample. Its X article's ten stills and its clip were made again from it; its banner (2000 ×
800) stays as it was.

**The examples:** four made-up influencers, **Nova** and **Kai** (realistic), **Mika** (anime) and **Juno** (3D cartoon),
their looks and full bodies, photos in scenes, two memes, an X banner, eight style pictures, nine trend clips and four trend
videos (an influencer put into one of them), and videos from photos: 34 pictures and 17 clips. Made by Claude on the owner's fal.ai (about $6.70 of the $9) and
Dreamina accounts (37 credits left; one of its 12 generations failed), in the owner's Chrome, with the same kinds of AI
models AGI Studio uses, **before AGI Studio opened**: never "made in AGI Studio" (the video says "Examples · AI-generated").
In the spirit of the owner's reference (Higgsfield's AI influencer pages): never its name, look, pictures, prompts or code.
The trend clips are stand-ins made on Dreamina (the app's own 12 trend clips are the owner's to make, with Kling, on the
owner's page). Downloaded into the owner's `Downloads\AGI Studio examples` (in subfolders; its `_to_delete` holds the 3
zips they came in, for the owner to delete).

**Juno's 3D model** (the same day, after the owner saw the first version: "why the 3d model is like that?"; the owner's

**Its rules** (`tests/studio-promo.test.js`):
- **Never an AI service by name** (fal, Kling, Seedance, Nano Banana, Gemini, Meshy, Dreamina, Higgsfield…) in any word
  on screen, the post or the code that draws it; **never "buy"** (credits are topped up), never price talk, "safe", "scam"
  or "rug"; PG-13; only $AGI (`$TICKER` is a coin's own ticker, a placeholder); "investment" only as "not an investment".
- **"Not financial advice"** wherever money comes up (the coin, holders, the end card, the post), 18+ where it applies,
  "AI-generated" on every frame from the reveal on, and never "made in AGI Studio".
- **AGI-1 never in 3D, never CloakMesh, never another coin's data:** its one model file is Juno's own 3D model
  (`/media/model/juno-3d.glb`, made for it, labeled "AI-generated"), never AGI-1's 3D model or anything rendered from it
  (until 2026-10-13 its figure was three.js shapes, labeled "Illustration").
- **AGI Studio's own words and numbers, imported** (`src/studio/rules.js`, `src/studio/app-words.js`, Explore's heading):
  every price at each level, the three ways, the 26 styles and their groups, the meme formats, the X banner's size, the
  trend clips, the video models, the editors' limits, the 3D model's moves, the top-ups, the holder perks: change them in the
  app and the next video says the new ones.
- **The picture and the music keep one clock** (`tools/studio-promo/timeline.js`): a shutter for each photo, a tap for each
  choice, a tick for each letter typed, a tick for each 100 credits counted, a glitch and a hit for each trend swap, the
  coin's flip and landing, the hits, a riser up to each breath, nothing in a breath, a sound on every cut, four kicks a bar
  on the beat where it's full. The test reads the music's plan and checks each one.
- **Her voice** (since the same day): her lines are among the video's own words (the same rules), short (under a quarter
  of it), never over a drop's first second, the trend videos or a breath, and every hit of the music not under her words
  at full level: the test plans each line's dip with the music's real hits and breaths.

**How it's made** (`tools/studio-promo/`):
- `timeline.js` (its clock: the scenes and every moment), `words.js` (every word on screen and the post, from the app's own
  files), `music.js` (its music), `media.mjs` (the examples made ready once: pictures at most 1600 px; each clip as two runs
  of JPEG frames, 720 × 1280 and 360 × 640, since Chromium in Claude's workspace can't play H.264; Juno's 3D model as
  one GLB of 7.4 MB, `model/juno-3d.glb`: its textures made small (its colors 2048 px, its normals and its metal and
  roughness 1024 px), its move resampled, and each point's four biggest bones kept, since three.js draws four (Meshy gave
  682 of its points more; checked against all of them: 0.02 mm apart on average, 13 mm at most, at fingertips); into
  `tools/studio-promo/media`, which git ignores), `make.mjs` (builds the page, serves it on this computer only, draws
  every frame in Chromium, ffmpeg makes the MP4, then the cover, the post, a light copy and README.txt), `README.txt` (for
  the owner, next to the video).
- `page/` (built by Vite into `tools/studio-promo/dist/`): `main.js` (the canvas, the scenes, the cuts, the overlays, a
  still grain and a vignette, `window.promo`), `look.js` (AGI Studio's look: its colors, headlines, pills, panels, the
  pointer, icons drawn in code), `parts.js` (pictures and clips, easing, springs), `media.js` (the pictures, and each clip's
  frames waited for before a frame is finished), `cuts.js` (the 14 cuts: slams on the drops, pushes, wipes, a zoom flash, a
  whip pan, irises (from the memes into the edits, from the coin into paying), through dark), `model3d.js` (Juno's 3D
  model with three.js, on its own WebGL canvas the scene copies onto the frame: its wireframe over its own surface drawn
  to depth only, so only the lines facing the camera show; its colors below a sweep; its bones on screen; held at a time of
  its move with a weight, 0 the pose it was made in and 1 its move; its move's hips put back over the turntable and lifted
  2.2 cm, since Meshy made its wave a little to one side and low) and `scenes/` (one file a scene). Everything is a
  function of time: a frame drawn twice is the same. Without its model file, the 3D scene shows her full body instead.
- `music.js`: composed and synthesized in code by Claude (no samples, no service, nobody else's music), the engine of her
  launch video's: D major, vi–IV–I–V (Bm7, Gmaj7, D(add9), A(add9)), the hook previewed on an electric piano over the
  opening, the drops on Bm (four-on-the-floor, claps, hats, supersaw chords breathing with the kick, a bass, the hook on a
  lead, an octave down and bells in the finale), a half-time verse under creating, a lift into the styles, a groove for
  photos and memes, a build into the second drop, a darker bar for the 3D model, a breakdown for the community, a breath of
  silence before each drop and the end chord. About -13 LUFS, true peaks about -1.5 dBFS. `musicPlan()` lists every sound
  without making it (the tests); `renderMusic()` makes the WAV (48 kHz stereo, in 15 to 20 s).
- A headline's words leave before the next headline's arrive in the same place (found in the first preview: "Meet Nova."
  and "She's not real." were still there as the next lines rose in, the two overlapping for a moment).
- Found looking at the finished video, and fixed before it was made again: the styles' last line ("Or Any style…") sat
  under the grid's bottom row and was on screen for less than half a second, and the photo models' last item ("From 8
  credits") came in after the cut to the memes had begun. Now the grid is a little smaller and higher, its line under it a
  whole second before the cut, and the photo models build beside the montage, all four in with more than a second to
  read them.

answer: yes, if it's short, at the big moments, in her own voice, with the music dipping under her and the words on screen
as they were; the owner's choice: "Short, AGI-1's voice (Recommended)", her takes made with her Google voice in Google AI
Studio in the owner's Chrome and downloaded into Downloads):
- **Her 12 lines** (`VOICE` in `words.js`; where each goes, `VOICE` in `timeline.js`): "Meet Nova." (0.3 s, with its
  headline), "She's not real." (4.7 s: the music's hit falls between "She's" and "not real", the one hit she speaks over),

  of likes), "agi1.app/studio" (94.3 s, as its pill pops up; she says "A G I one dot app slash studio.") and "Live now."
  (98.3 s, on the end card). About 21 seconds of her in 103: never a narration. Every line is among the video's own words,
  so its rules hold for them (never an AI service, never "buy"…). Never over a drop's first second, the trend videos
  (their drop and all of their scene) or a breath of silence; each starts after its moment's hit, so every hit of the
  music (its impacts and crashes: 23 of them free of her) lands at full level.
- **Her takes:** made by Claude in Google AI Studio (Generate speech), in the owner's Chrome with the owner's account (AI
  Studio's own free use: no API key, nothing paid), Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS with Despina and her calm style (the site's
  voice), half of them a little brisker; several takes of each, the best picked by speech-to-text (every word as written)
  and by ear. In the owner's `Downloads\AGI Studio examples\voice-over\` as `agi1-vo-01-meet.wav` … `agi1-vo-12-url.wav`
  (the other takes in its `other-takes\`). AI Studio's welcome page was accepted with the owner's OK ("Yes, accept it for
  me (Recommended)").
- **Made ready** (`node tools/studio-promo/media.mjs --only voice --from <that folder>`, `readyLine()` in `voice.js`): each
  take at 48 kHz, trimmed around her words (150 ms kept before her first sound, a soft first sound like an "sh" kept, 200
  ms after her last), a pause over 0.3 s made 0.3 s (two takes had one of 0.58 s), her rumble under 90 Hz out, at -14
  LUFS (the music is about -13: dipped under her, the soundtrack stays about as loud as the music), her loudest moments
  held under -2 dBFS; into `media/voice/<id>.wav` (mono, 16-bit) and `media/index.json` (where her words start and how
  long they last). `make.mjs` refuses a take whose words last more than 0.15 s longer than its place was made for
  (`LEN_SLACK`): its place is checked again first.
- **The music dipping under her** (`planDucks()`, `mixVoice()` in `voice.js`): from 0.2 s before her first word (down by
  0.04 s before it, a half cosine in dB), held 60 ms after her last, then back up over 0.5 s (never quicker than 50 ms);
  never in a hit's first 60 ms (a dip waits for it), and back up 10 ms before the next hit, or as a breath's silence begins.
  How far: as loud as she is over her words, less 8 LU, at least 8 dB and at most 12 (in the video 8 to 10.5 dB: the
  finale's address 10.5, "This is AGI Studio." 9.5, the 3D model 8.8, "Live now." 9). In three bands, each from one
  12-dB-an-octave filter and taken from the whole, so at no dip they add back up to it exactly: the middle (her voice's)
  by its dip, the lows under 180 Hz half as much in dB (the kick and the bass carry on), the highs over 6 kHz 0.7 as much
  (the hats' shimmer stays). Her voice, from both speakers, only from its dip's start to the music back up (a take's
  quiet never reaches a hit). A limiter only where she is, at 0.86 (under the music's own 0.89, for a true peak under -1 dBTP), never pulling the music under its own level. Since 2026-10-20 that limiter can also read between the samples (`truePeak`), off for this video: its soundtrack stays exactly as it was (on for the roadmap's video). Everywhere else the soundtrack is the music exactly, sample for
  sample (16-bit WAV, written and read back the same).
- **The videos:** `make.mjs` makes `soundtrack.wav` (the music with her voice) and puts it on the video (AAC, 256 kb/s; the
  light copy 160 kb/s), and a copy of each with its music alone (`…-music-only.mp4`). This time with `--sound-only`: the
  videos already made were kept as the music-only copies (byte for byte), and her soundtrack put on copies of them, their
  pictures copied (`-c:v copy`: never drawn or encoded again), each as long as its video. `--no-voice`: its music alone,
  as before.
- **Checked** in Claude's workspace: both videos' pictures the same as before (ffmpeg's hash of their video streams),
  103.000 s and 6,180 frames; the soundtrack made again from the music and her takes with the code as saved: the same
  bytes as the one in the videos; it differs from the music only inside her 12 dips (1,377,438 samples, none outside),
  none of the 23 free hits touched in their first 60 ms, every breath's silence as it was; each video's sound lined up with
  the soundtrack to the sample, over the whole and in each of her lines; -13.2 LUFS with a true peak of -1.1 dBTP (the
  light copy -1.2; the music-only copies -13.1 and -13.2 LUFS); and two speech-to-text models, run in Claude's workspace
