**How it works:**
- **Her stream runs on the owner's own rented server, in Docker** (`tools/live/Dockerfile`: Playwright's own image with its
  Chromium, plus ffmpeg and a virtual screen, run as the image's own user, never root; Vercel can't run a browser and ffmpeg
  for an hour). `tools/live/run.mjs` opens her set in Chromium on a virtual screen (Xvfb), and ffmpeg sends that screen and
  her voice (with her music) to **X Live Studio** by RTMP (1280 × 720 at 30, H.264 at 3 Mb/s with a keyframe every 3 s,
  AAC 128 kb/s 48 kHz, as Live Studio asks), or to a file (`--record`). Her mouth stays in step with her voice: her voice's
  clock follows ffmpeg's first picture, and `LIVE_AV_MS` fine-tunes it for the server (`--sync-check` measures it: 170 ms
  on a 2-core machine).
- **What she does next** (`tools/live/show.js`, pure): intro → questions (up to 4 in a row) → a segment every ~6 minutes
  (every ~2.5 when nobody asks) → a nudge when nobody asks → a chat line after a quiet moment → the outro 40 seconds before
  the end. The owner's "end" and the show's length come before a pause (a paused show still ends). Since 2026-10-07: 14
  segments (13 without her diary), each once before any comes again, so in a 3-hour show each comes round 3 or 4 times
  when nobody asks; the four with picks (`poolFor()`) take different ones each time.
- **The site** (`api/live.js`): the runner calls `/api/live` with `LIVE_SECRET` every 5 seconds ("beat": what she's doing,
  and the owner's controls back) and for each question ("next": her answer, made there; "done"; "back": back in line after
  a pause; "stop": with her next show's time, from `LIVE_DAILY_AT`, which the site keeps but since 2026-10-07 never
  shows anyone). If the site doesn't answer, she keeps going without new questions. The site's
  address must not redirect (`LIVE_SECRET` would be dropped on the way): the runner says so instead of following it.
- **"I'm live" in her Telegram groups** (2026-10-07): once, as she starts streaming (never for a recording), the runner
  says "on_x"; the site posts "i'm live on X right now 💜 come hang out, and ask me anything: https://agi1.app/live" and,
  under it, "i'm an AI, it's PG-13, and nothing i say is financial advice" (`GROUP_LIVE` in `server/tg-lines.js`,
  `postLiveNow()` in `server/tg-groups.js`) in each group of `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`, once a day at most whatever restarts
  (`live_tell` in the database: true only the first time today, UTC, for the show that's on; so with random times, a
  second show the same UTC day posts nothing), never with `TELEGRAM_GROUP_POSTS=off`. A group that fails is a warning in
  the log, and the show goes on either way.
- **Her voice** (`tools/live/voice.js`): Google Cloud's Vertex AI, the same model, voice and mood styles as the site
  (Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, Despina), signed in with a service account's key file (a signed token request) or an API key.
  A line Google doesn't make within 15 s: she says it silently (captions and her mouth), and that way rests a minute.
  Her pre-written lines are made once and kept on the server (`--warm` makes all of them ahead; her first lines are made
  during "starting soon" anyway); her answers are made each time.
- **When things go wrong:** her answers not coming (the AI down, the site away): questions wait (30 s, then longer, at most
  5 minutes) and she says so once ("my brain's lagging a little 🙈"); the stream to X dropping: ffmpeg starts again (5
  tries, counted afresh after 5 good minutes; a network that stops answering for 15 s ends a try), and the answer that was
  cut is said again; a show never runs more than 5 minutes past its length; `docker stop` ends it cleanly (her line stops,
  the site hears the show ended, X ends the broadcast when the stream stops).

**Her music** (`tools/live/music.js`):
- **Five original instrumental songs written in code by Claude:** "purple hour", "soft launch", "texts back", "after
  midnight", "no red flags" (chill lo-fi and soft synth, 72–92 beats a minute, about 2 minutes each). Each is chords (four
  bars, voiced close together), a bass line, soft swung drums and a little melody (a two-bar idea, said again, then an answer
  that comes home), played by small synthesizers: an electric piano, a warm pad, a pluck, a bell, with a little room and a
  little vinyl crackle. No samples, no outside service, nobody else's music; the same notes always make the same sound.
- Made once on the server (a few seconds each) and kept on disk with her voice lines; played on a loop (shuffled, never the
  same song twice in a row, each starting while the last one fades), quiet, and quieter while she talks (down in about a
  tenth of a second, back up slowly). It fades out at the end of the show.
- `LIVE_MUSIC=off` switches it off; `LIVE_MUSIC_VOLUME` (percent, 100 by default) makes it louder or quieter. The owner
  heard a sample of all five before it went in ("the music good").

**Setup (the owner, once).** Secrets go only where these steps say: never in chat, git or a screenshot.
1. **The site:** Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings → Environment Variables → `LIVE_SECRET` = 32+ random characters (the

1. **On the server:**
   ```
   cd /opt/agi1-live/site && nohup sh tools/live/live.sh --start-in 10 >> /var/log/agi1-live.log 2>&1 &
   ```
   The stream starts at once with "starting soon" and a 10-minute countdown (`--start-in` takes 0 to 30 minutes), then her
   show (`LIVE_MINUTES`: 3 hours; `--minutes 60` after `--start-in 10` for one hour this time). `nohup … &` keeps it
   going when the window closes; `tail -20 /var/log/agi1-live.log` shows how it's going (a line near the start of
   each show ends `streaming to X · 180 minutes`). (`--start-at HH:MM`, in UTC and at most 30 minutes ahead, still works too.)
   Three hours, for every show: `grep LIVE_MINUTES /opt/agi1-live/live.env` says `LIVE_MINUTES=180`, or this sets it:
   ```
   sed -i 's/^LIVE_MINUTES=.*/LIVE_MINUTES=180/' /opt/agi1-live/live.env && grep LIVE_MINUTES /opt/agi1-live/live.env
   ```

   `docker stop $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=agi1-live)`.

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `--check`: "NO LIVE_RTMP_URL and LIVE_STREAM_KEY" | | Fill them in from Live Studio's source (setup step 3) |
| It stops at once | `the site refused to start the show: start: HTTP 401 (LIVE_SECRET isn't the same as in Vercel)` | Copy `LIVE_SECRET` again on both sides; after changing it in Vercel, Redeploy |
| It stops at once | `… HTTP 503 (LIVE_SECRET or supabase/live.sql missing on the site?)` | Setup step 1 |
| It stops at once | `start: the site's address redirects to …: set SITE_URL in live.env to the address it goes to` | Set `SITE_URL` to that address (https://www.agi1.app) |
| `--check`: `NO the site accepts this server's LIVE_SECRET (beat: HTTP 400 bad_request)` | | The check itself, before 2026-10-06 (a 400 means the key was taken; a wrong key is 401): after the push, `sh tools/live/live.sh update` |
| `--warm` ends with `11 of 121 ready … run it again later for the rest` | `[voice] vertex: … HTTP 429 … RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | Google takes about 10 a minute for her voice model: since 2026-10-06 it waits by itself (`update` first); before, the loop in step 7 |
| It stops at once | `--start-at 20:00 is 23 h 45 min away (it's 20:15 UTC now)…` | The cron line runs too late for `LIVE_DAILY_AT` (or it was started by hand after the time): change one of them |
| She talks silently (captions only) | `[voice] vertex: … HTTP 403 … (enable the "Agent Platform API" for the project (formerly "Vertex AI API"), and give the service account the "Agent Platform User" role …)` | Setup step 2 |
| She talks silently | `[voice] vertex: … HTTP 404 … (the model or the project/location: check LIVE_VOICE_MODEL, …)` | Google renamed or moved the Preview model on Agent Platform: tell Claude with the line (`LIVE_VOICE_MODEL`, `LIVE_VERTEX_LOCATION`) |
| She talks silently | `can't read GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS (ENOENT): no file there …` | The key file isn't at /opt/agi1-live/google-key.json (setup step 6) |
| A few silent lines, now and then | `[voice] vertex: no answer within 15 s (it rests a minute)` | Google was slow; she goes on. If it's often: `LIVE_VOICE_TIMEOUT_S=25` |
| Questions wait, "my brain's lagging" | `her answers aren't coming (ai): questions wait 30 s` | The site's Gemini key (credits, limits): see the chat's troubleshooting |

An older one: VLC plays it, or `ffmpeg -i try.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart try-fixed.mp4` |

  the bar, with a bar 1% see-through, with the window put together on the "GPU" (SwiftShader), and with her drawn on a 2D
  canvas, the top of her head is round again. Now nothing plain and opaque covers her picture: it ends where the bar
  starts (`.her` in `tools/live/page/stage.css`, `--bar`), and the boxes that can be over her (the card, the "starting
  soon" box) are 1% see-through (the caption and the label already were). **Keep it that way:** a new box over her

**Not built** (said to the owner): "pumping" or any prediction (hard rule 8); anyone else's videos or posts (copyright, and
"only $AGI, never real people"); reading or typing in X's chat (X's approval first, and hard rule 6).

**Owner, after the push** (on the server, `root@agi1-live`, one line at a time):
1. `cd /opt/agi1-live/site && sh tools/live/live.sh update` (the new code; the image is built again, a few minutes).
2. `sh tools/live/live.sh --warm` (the voices of her 58 new lines, once: about 8 minutes at Google's pace, about $0.10).
3. Optional, **her videos**: `mkdir -p /opt/agi1-live/videos` on the server; then on the PC (PowerShell, in the folder with
   the video): `scp "my-video.mp4" root@<the server's IP>:/opt/agi1-live/videos/`. Only her own videos (her launch video,
   her daily clips). A video that's there is in the next show.
4. Optional, **her X posts**: an app in X's developer console (console.x.com) with pay-per-use credits; its **Bearer
   Token** goes into live.env on the server with this line (it stays hidden on screen, and the line prints 1):
   ```
   read -s -p 'X Bearer Token (hidden): ' B && echo && sed -i '/^LIVE_X_BEARER=/d' /opt/agi1-live/live.env && echo "LIVE_X_BEARER=$B" >> /opt/agi1-live/live.env && grep -c '^LIVE_X_BEARER=.\+' /opt/agi1-live/live.env
   ```
   Never paste the token in chat or a screenshot. The next show's log says `X: her posts and their replies`.
5. `LIVE_CHATTER=off` in live.env switches her new AI lines off (`LIVE_CHATTER_PER_HOUR=20`: fewer).

**Cost:** her new lines from the site's AI, at most about $0.06 an hour (40 lines: about $0.0005 to write each, $0.001 to
say); her reactions to her posts, replies and videos about the same each, a few a show; X's API (only with the Bearer
Token, on the X developer account's own credits): at most 60 posts read a show (about $0.30) and her account once
($0.010); the voices of her 58 new lines once (about $0.10). Her song, her dance songs, her outfits, rooms, moves and
effects cost nothing (made in code, or the owner's own). So about $0.20–0.50 more a 3-hour show with X on (the owner
approved about $0.50).

**Settings on the server** (live.env; none in Vercel): `LIVE_CHATTER` (on), `LIVE_CHATTER_PER_HOUR` (40),
`LIVE_X_BEARER` (none: she never reads X), `LIVE_X_READS` (60), `LIVE_X_USER` (agi1dotapp), `LIVE_VIDEOS_DIR` (/videos:
`live.sh` gives the show `/opt/agi1-live/videos` there, read-only, when the folder exists). Her buy alerts follow
`TELEGRAM_BUY_MIN` in Vercel (our server reads the buys).

**Trying it** (Claude, on a recording): `node tools/live/run.mjs --demo --fake-voice --record try.mp4 --minutes 8 --try
song,dance,video,room,outfit,market` puts those extras first, 45 s apart (`--try` changes the pace: 45 s / 90 s / 20 s);
the demo's made-up questions ask her to jump, dance, blush, change her outfit or room and sing, and a made-up buy comes

### Her painted set (2026-10-07 and 08)

**The owner, after the preview of her trips:** "the agi1 trip preview i just watched is so bad btw". Asked what was worst:
"Her hat and outfit, The vehicle ride, The people she meets, The places, everything". Asked how to make it look good:
**"Painted art (Recommended)"**: anime-style paintings of each place and each person, made once by Google's image AI with
the Google Cloud key already on her server (about $5–10 once), every picture checked by Claude before it goes in.

**Step 1, built: the art tool** (`tools/live/art.mjs`; on the server `sh tools/live/live.sh --art`):
- **What it paints (152 pictures):** her 20 places and 7 rooms (two of each, 16:9: a hand-painted anime background, the
  landmark in the left half and the right side open scenery; never people, text, letters, logos or signs; since the
  first run "one continuous painting from edge to edge": told that "a character will stand in front of the right half, so
  keep it calm", both models now and then painted a see-through white panel there, or a second, blurred picture), the inside of
  each of her 12 vehicles (two each: the seat she rides in and the view out of the window), the 21 people she meets (two
  each, waist up, turned toward her, on pure green to be cut out; made up, never anyone real; one of the two with her
  picture as the art style to match: her 2D self, rendered from her Live2D model and cut above the "AGI" on her shirt,
  never the 3D model or a render of it), and the 32 things she wears on her head or around her neck in her outfits (one
  each, on green).
- **How:** Google's image models on Vertex AI (Agent Platform), signed in with the service account her voice uses (no new
  key, no new setting): **Nano Banana 2.1** (`gemini-nano-banana-2.1`) first, then Nano Banana 2 (`gemini-3.1-flash-image`)
  and older ones if the project doesn't have it (ai.google.dev's model codes, 2026-10-07; `LIVE_ART_MODEL` in live.env
  picks another). 1K pictures, two at a time at Google's pace (a "wait" waits and tries again); a picture Google refuses
  is skipped; run again, it carries on with what's missing (`LIVE_ART_MAX`, 220, the most in one run); `--art-only
  paris,omar` makes one more of each named. Into `/opt/agi1-live/out/art/`: places, rooms and rides as JPEG, people and
  accessories as WebP (no JPEG blur on their green edges), and `manifest.json` (each file's prompt and model).
- **Cost:** Nano Banana 2.1 is about $0.034 a 1K picture (Nano Banana 2 about $0.067): about $5–10 for all 152, once,
  billed to the Google Cloud card like her voice (the $20 budget's emails). **About two hours**, not the 20 minutes first
  said: on the owner's first run (2026-10-07) Google said "wait" (429) again and again, about one picture a minute. The
  owner switched to Nano Banana 2 (`LIVE_ART_MODEL=gemini-3.1-flash-image` in live.env, Claude's suggestion) and it
  didn't help: Google's limit covers the whole project, not each model (Claude had said it would be faster; it wasn't).
  A run keeps going by itself through the waits; a bigger limit would be a request to Google that takes days.
- **The owner's run** (2026-10-07 and 08): **138 of the 152** (55 with Nano Banana 2.1, 83 with Nano Banana 2). Google
  gave nothing for 14: the second picture of one place, three rides and six people (each has its first), and four of her
  accessories, which had no picture at all: Berlin's yellow beanie, Sunny's mint star clips, Istanbul's blue scarf and
  Rio's pink flower. The owner's `--art-only` for those four (2026-10-08, Nano Banana 2) made all four: **142 of 152**,
  every accessory painted (until then three had stand-ins and the beanie was drawn in code: see step 2).
- **Nothing goes on stream by itself:** Claude looks at every picture, picks one of each, cuts out the people and
  accessories (the green keyed out) and makes them small for her set (step 2).

**Step 2, built: her set uses them** (the paintings are in `tools/live/page/art/`, found when her set is built):
- **Picking and cutting them** (`tools/live/art-cut.mjs`, Claude runs it on the copies in `_source-assets/art`): one of
  each, as `tools/live/art-picks.json` says (`"places/paris": 1`; 0 = none good enough, drawn in code; or
  `{ "k": 2, "flip": true, "panel": [905, 1324] }`), into `tools/live/page/art/<group>/<id>.webp`, picked by looking at
  her in front of both (a render of her set for each). `flip`: mirrored left to right (Tokyo: its tower was painted on
  her side). `panel`: a see-through white panel the model painted over those columns, undone (`unPanel()`: how washed it
  is, per color, measured on the picture carrying on at each edge of the panel, then turned back, and the few columns at
  each edge bridged; Rio and Chichén Itzá, about 37% white; checked side by side and up close). A picture split into two
  (Tokyo's first) isn't used. Her backdrops at the set's size (1280 × 720, WebP); the people she meets and
  the things she wears cut out of their green: the green joined to the picture's edges keyed out, and inside only the
  green's own color (a gap, or seen through a glass: `SEE_THROUGH` for her helmet, her clear glasses and Commander Nova's
  visor), each edge pixel as see-through as it's green against what the thing itself looks like nearby, the green taken
  out of its color, specks (a crumb, a mark in a corner) dropped, cropped to what's left and made small (people 640 px
  tall, things at most 512 px). Measured on her own 2D picture put on green: its edges come back within about 3 levels of
  255 on average.
- **The picks** (2026-10-08, each looked at with her in front of it): most places, rooms and rides as first painted; the
  second picture of Agra, Bali, Beijing, Berlin, Istanbul, London, the Moon, the bus and the robotaxi (and of 15 of the 21
  people), where it was the better one; Rio's and Chichén Itzá's panels undone; Tokyo's second mirrored; the plane and
  the train mirrored (their windows were painted on her side); the balloon's first only in part (`crop`: `[0, 115, 957, 538]`, 16:9, it
  was painted as two pictures, so its seam is behind her). Commander Nova and Rusty the rover at the size they're painted.
- **What the first paintings needed** (2026-10-08, `tools/live/art-cut.mjs`): a green behind the conical hat that was olive
  (150, 204, 69), so a background green is anything 40 levels greener than its red and blue (was 60); the hibiscus' own
  light-green leaves, which came out grey and half see-through, kept (`GREEN_INSIDE`: only what's nearly the background's
  own green is keyed from the edges in); the helmet's visor reflections, painted mint by the green behind them, made a
  see-through white (`GLASS_GLINTS`, `whitenGlints()`); **the headphones' cups**: painted from the front, cups facing us,
  their dark cushions showed by her eyes in the gaps between her face and the hair beside it, so only each cup's outer
  half is kept (`OUTER_CUPS`, `outerCups()`: per row, from its outer edge, the rest fading out over a few pixels) and they
  were drawn behind her face and that hair (until the owner's later message the same day: see "The headphones" below);
  **the cat ears' headband**: its two ends came down past her
  bangs beside her eyes (white lines with the white ears, black ones with the black), so below the ears it fades out
  (`BAND_ENDS`, `trimBandEnds()`: on a head, the rest of a headband is under the hair; the picture keeps its size, so
  where it sits doesn't change).
- **Stand-ins** (2026-10-08, `STAND_INS`): until their own painting is there, three accessories Google skipped are made
  from a painting asked for in the same words but another color, its colors turned (`turnHue()`: each pixel's lightness
  and saturation kept, greys and the line work as they are): Sunny's mint star clips from the golden ones (the stage
  outfit's), Istanbul's light blue scarf from Paris' light red one, Rio's pink hibiscus from Palawan's red one (only its
  reds turned: its leaves stay green). Their own painting, once it's there, is used instead (`cutAll` logs which): since
  the owner's `--art-only` the same day all four have their own, so the stand-ins are only for a picture Google skips
  later (Berlin's beanie had no painting like it: drawn in code until then).
- **The beanie** (2026-10-08): painted a little from below, its inside showed under its cuff as a brown oval, over her
  forehead like a visor, so it goes (`HAT_INSIDE`, `dropHatInside()`: found from its middle by its color, where it's that

### Her arms, her hands and what she holds (2026-10-08)

**The owner, after the painted set's preview:** "theres so many problems her arms doesnt even move naturally lol it so bad
and clnky looks and when she holds things she doesnt even look shes holding it and some hats not even wearing to her head
and headset not even on her ears please fix those things you can see it right use max effort and make it better", "and i
know other things have these problems as well i just didint see them yet", and on the way: "why did you switched her
hands", "and she doesnt even grabbed it lol". All of it is her live show's (`tools/live/page/`, and options of
`src/stage/agi1-2d.js` and `agi1-2d-arms.js` that only her show passes): the website's AGI-1 moves exactly as before.

**What was wrong** (her preview, frame by frame, and Claude's own recordings): her hands were her model's one flat drawing,
turned like a board: a cookie or a croissant floated past her fingertips with her open palm under it, nothing ever touched
her fingers; raised, both hands were stiff "jazz hands"; on their way up to a clap her forearms crossed in an X over her
chest, and the clap itself was at her neckline; a blown kiss swept down across her chest; held up in her hand, her umbrella
showed her hand floating by her shoulder with her arm hanging under it; the conical hat sat above her head with its painted
chin straps across her forehead; the headset's ear cup was up by her eye. (Her hats and her headset: see "Her painted set".)

**Her hand is one drawing, so every pose shows her palm, the right way round** (`src/stage/agi1-2d-arms.js`,
`tools/live/page/moves.js`):
- Her Live2D hand is one picture: an open palm facing us, fingers straight. On her show each arm now does with it, in
  2.5D, what a real arm does: her forearm (and her upper arm) seen shorter as it comes toward us (`fore`, `upper`), her
  hand turned about its length (`twist`: narrower as it turns, at most `HAND_TURN`, 40°, 0.81 as wide; further it's
  squeezed thin), and her fingers curled (`curl`: shorter, closer together, her thumb in over her palm; relaxed at most
  `CURL.open`, 0.35, round something she holds `CURL.hold`, 0.5, never past `CURL_MAX`, 0.55: past it her drawn fingers
  fold back over her palm and crumple). `HAND` in `agi1-2d-arms.js` is her hand's own frame (along it from her wrist to her
  fingertips, across it from her thumb's side), measured on her drawing; `handPoint()` gives where a point of her hand is
  now.
- Her poses say where her hand goes, not angles: a spot on her face (her mouth, chin, cheeks, eyes, ears: they follow her
  head as it moves and tilts) or her body (her shoulders), which way her hand points and which point of her hand goes
  there (`at()` in moves.js; her model's arms and spots come from her set every frame, `body()`). `reach()` works her arm
  out on her model as it is that frame: her elbow comes forward and her upper arm is seen shorter when her hand goes up to
  her face, her forearm comes toward us, her shoulder stays near where the pose says, her wrist bends little; never a
  forearm out flat with her elbow pulled in (the "paddle" rule, 2026-10-07), never a whole turn of her forearm between two
  frames (the nearest way round from where her elbow is).
- A hand by her face is drawn over her face and her hair (`front`: a bite, her hand over her mouth as she laughs, her
  fingertips at her chin); otherwise under them, as her model has it.
- Every pose shows her palm, her own hand the right way round: a wave, "yay!", her hands by her cheeks, over her mouth,
  her fingertips at her lips, in her hair, palms up low, on her hips. Never her palm drawing flipped to stand in for the
  back of her hand (the owner, of her hands on her cheeks: "why did you switched her hands": a flipped palm reads as her
  other hand), never a fist (one cut from her drawing read as a claw: "are you even fixing it lol").
- Her elbow bent far (her hand up by her face): it turns as a hinge (`fold`, from 115° to 160° bent: `RIGID`), and a small
  round elbow in her skin's colors is drawn just under her forearm (`ELBOW_FRAG` in `outfits.js`, as wide as her forearm
  is drawn there): her drawing has no round of a bent elbow, and the soft ends of her upper arm and forearm showed below
  it as a pale, see-through cuff with odd lines.
- Her hands stay off her chest (PG-13: by her face, at her sides or low); her right hand leads, her left a moment behind.

**What she holds** (`HOLD` in moves.js, drawn by `outfits.js`): in front of her palm, the way a hand seen from its palm's
side holds something, and her own fingers or thumb drawn again over it (her hand's own drawing, only that part: a shader
on her hand's own frame, so it follows however her hand turns or curls):
- her mug, a drink (boba, a coconut…) and her phone in front of her palm, her thumb over its edge (`grip: 'thumb'`): her
  mug's rim and a drink's straw at her lips; her phone up beside her face, its screen to us;
- a snack up at her fingertips, her fingertips over its bottom (`grip: 'fingers'`), brought to her mouth twice (a bite
  each time);
- it fades in and out over a few frames (`HELD_FADE`, 6) instead of popping into her hand and out of it;
- the hand mic picture, which nothing used, is gone (she sings in her stage outfit's headset).
`studio.hold('mug')` and `studio.holdAt('mug', { a, b, w })` show and tune it on her set.

**Her umbrella** (`UMBRELLA` in `outfits.js`) rests on her right shoulder, held behind her, its clear canopy over her (its
shaft from where it rests on her shoulder, leaning out 15°, its pink grip and little hook behind her, out of sight): her
drawn hand can't close round a handle, and held up in her hand it showed her hand floating by her shoulder. While she
carries it her talking gestures are her left hand's, and something her right hand does (a laugh, a sip, a clap…:
`USES_R`) puts it down until she's done. `studio.umbrellaAt({...})` tunes it.

**Her arms on their way** (moves.js `blend()` and `post()`):
- from her side up to her face, her hand comes up at her side, then in (her elbow turns her forearm out and up), never
  across her chest: the nearest way round from her side to a hand pointing up at her face was often across her, so on
  the way to a clap her forearms crossed in an X;
- her forearm comes toward us on its way, as an elbow bending in front of a body does: seen shorter while it points across
  her, when it still has far to go (`SWING_DIP`, at most half) and halfway on its way into or out of a pose that turns it a
  lot (`TRANSIT_DIP`, up to 0.75, and for `TRANSIT_TAIL`, 0.35 s, after). It's worked out after her springs: her
  controller calls `moves.post()` with her pose as it will be drawn (`src/stage/agi1-2d.js`, only when it has `moves`).
  Worked out on her targets it came a moment late (her elbow follows them a moment behind) and pulled her hand down
  across her chest just as it turned;
- her claps by her chin (they were at her neckline); a blown kiss from her lips out to us without dipping across her chest
  (her hand between two spots takes the second spot's nearest turn from the first's).

**Her hats, her headset and her headphones**: the conical hat worn with her head inside it and its painted straps gone,
the cap a little bigger and lower, the headset fitted to her head, and (the owner, after: "and i just noticed this headset
is too big for her right") the headphones of her midnight and gamer outfits smaller and worn: their band on her hair,
their cups at the sides of her head by her ears, and her glasses' lenses clear (painted solid, they hid her eyes) (see
"Her painted set"). Every outfit with something on her head was then looked at, still and moving (looking around,
laughing, dancing, a confused tilt, a twirl, a jump), and every outfit again after the headphones.

**Not picked** (tried, and dropped the same day): a fist cut from her hand's drawing (`fist.js`: a claw) and a picture of
her hand round a handle (`grip.js`: her umbrella's handle floated by her shoulder, the owner: "????"); her palm flipped for

generate new images just to fix the arms and hands you can": never needed, her own hand turned and curled holds
everything and stays in her drawing's style). `tests/stream.test.js` keeps those files out.

**Tests:** `tests/stream.test.js` (2 new): her hands (never turned past `HAND_TURN`, curled at most `CURL.open`, or
`CURL.hold` round something she holds, and `CURL_MAX` under 0.6, in every action, gesture and dance; how she holds each

**The owner's list** (after a show): "i have few changes on my live this time on X / - there would be no restrictions on
howr short their message are. / - agi will now read the full question / -she will do everything asked to her / - the last
stream i check she doesn't watch her own ivdoes on the live and didn't sreact to her post / - when she sings the full
lyrics on the subtitle must shown with the full video on the live as well / -she can say names now no restrictions, and
she will know every person's real name on the telegram just like in the website version of her with her memories / -she
can mention other coins as well / -she can sing the full song everytime if requested / -she will know every popular person
in cypto spcae like elon musk marc andressen, Michael saylor etc. / -she now mentions that she can read the mesages on X
and telegram and the website", then "and can you also include on her watching the live trading chart of $AGI". Asked how
her music video should look, the owner picked **"Full screen, her small (Recommended)"**. Hard rules 6 and 8 say what
changed. All of it is her show's: the website itself only got its live page's words, its safety note's sentence about
Telegram names, and `supabase/live.sql`'s length rule.

**What's new:**
- **Any length** (the owner: "no restrictions on howr short their message are"): a question is 1 to 200 characters (a
  "gm", a "?", an emoji; 3 to 200 before): `LIVE.Q_MIN` in `server/live.js`, the table's check and `live_ask` in
  `supabase/live.sql` (**run it again before pushing**), the page. Still refused: links, addresses, contacts, crude words,
  10 or more of the same character in a row (spam), a shill that isn't a question (see "Other coins" below), and someone
  in distress (her caring note, never on stream).
- **She reads the whole question out loud** (the owner: "agi will now read the full question"): who asked and every word
  of it, then her answer, in one line of her voice (one request to Google: `readAndAnswer()` in `tools/live/run.mjs`):
  "Mochi asks: what's your favorite color? purple, obviously 💜". She looks at its card while she reads it and at everyone
  as she answers; her reaction waits for her answer (`reactAt`). Her live prompt knows she just read it, so her answer
  never says it again (the demo's made-up answers neither).
- **She does everything asked** (the owner: "she will do everything asked to her", "she can sing the full song everytime if
  requested"): a viewer's request never waits any more (`tools/live/acts.js`: the rests only pace what she does by herself),
  her song every time it's asked for (all of it when they ask for all of it), and something that isn't on her list gets
  the closest one, played along in her words, never just a no (`actsPrompt()` in `server/live-acts.js`). In her answers she
  does what they ask right there: a joke, a short story, her own little rap or poem, a gentle roast, a shout-out, a fun
  fact, a word in another language (never other artists' lyrics: her own lines instead). Never anything that isn't PG-13.
- **Names** (the owner: "she can say names now no restrictions, and she will know every person's real name on the
  telegram"): any display name of up to 24 characters (a famous person's, a coin's, an emoji), except crude ones, links,
  addresses, contacts, and names passing for her, her team or a moderator (`checkAskName()`: "owner", "host" and "dev" are
  everyday names now). A question from her Telegram bot shows the person's Telegram name (`telegramName()`: their first and
  last name, else their first name, else their username; checked like any name; none that passes: "someone on Telegram");
  her bot says so before they ask (`HOW` in `server/live-lines.js`) and after ("you're #1 in line, as Kai Tan"); the
  safety note too. Never their account or their chat's number.
- **Her memory of the clank.trade Telegram group, on stream** (the owner: "just like in the website version of her with her
  memories"): as on the site, only when a question is about the group or its people (`memoryFor()` → `recallGroup()`, the

### Holder perks on her show (2026-10-10)

**The owner's request** (with the next big plan, see the roadmap): "you can also add more utiliy to $agi so holders are
happy", and from which holding: "10,000+ $AGI (Recommended)". Item 2 of the plan, after her quizzes. Things to see and do
on her show, never an investment promise: nothing is spent, nobody is paid, nothing about prices (Claude's rule for every
holder perk, said to the owner with the plan).

**What people see:**
- **At agi1.app/live**, in the question form after the name: "💜 Crush and Soulmate perks (optional)": what they are, and
  **Connect a wallet**: the site's own sign-in (an address and a free signature, never a transaction: `src/lib/wallet.js`,
  hard rule 9), the wallets this browser has (with their logos), or without one, "Open in MetaMask / Phantom / Coinbase
  Wallet". The same wallet session as the home page's (`agi_wallet`): a wallet connected there is connected here, and
  **Disconnect** here signs this browser out of it everywhere (it follows another tab too). Connected: "0x12ab…cdef ·
  Crush 💜 Your questions get her badge and a head start in her line." (Soulmate: "…, and a shout-out from her"; a
  Stranger: "Her 💜 badge starts at Crush (10,000+ $AGI held, or burned for messages).", never "buy").
- **After sending:** the question waits with its badge ("“…” · as Mochi · 💜 Crush") and what it got: "💜 With your Crush
  badge: a head start in her line." (or the Soulmate's), or why not: "Your wallet's 💜 badges for today are used (5 a
  day)", or "Your wallet's session ended, so this one went in without her badge" (the page forgets it). A question never
  fails because of its wallet.
- **Her line:** a question with her badge goes ahead of the questions sent in the 10 minutes before it (`LIVE.HEAD_S`),
  never further: one waiting longer than that stays ahead of it, so everyone still gets their turn. At most **5 badges a
  day per wallet** (UTC; `LIVE.PER_DAY`, the same 5 as everyone's questions a day): after that its questions go in like
  everyone's.
- **On her stream:** the question's card shows a pink pill, **💜 Crush** or **💜 Soulmate**, next to "Question · from
  Mochi" (never the wallet or how much it holds). A **Soulmate**'s question gets confetti and one of her four shout-out
  lines ("ooh, a soulmate is here 💜", "soulmate alert 💜 my heart just did a little jump."…) before she reads it out loud
  and answers.
- **The host's panel** (the owner's phone link): "Mochi · agi1.app · 💜 Crush" in her line.
- **The words:** a rule on agi1.app/live ("A thank-you for being here: nothing is spent, it's not an investment, and it's
  not financial advice", 5 a day, never further than 10 minutes) and the safety note (01: "a thank-you for being here, not
  an investment"; 04: what's kept). Only on agi1.app/live: a question from her Telegram bot or the host's box for X's chat
  never has a badge (no wallet there).

**How it works:**
- The page sends its wallet session with the question (`session`); `/api/live` reads it (`liveHolder()` in
  `server/live.js`; the page's own idea of its level is never used): its level now, read again on Robinhood Chain when it's
  30 minutes old (held + burned for messages: `checkLevel`, `burnedAgi`), as her chat does. A level read again comes back
  with a new session; an old or broken session answers `signedOut` (the page forgets it, the question goes in without a
  badge); the chain away keeps its last level.
- At Crush or Soulmate, the badge (2 or 3) and a daily code of the wallet (`holderCode()`: an HMAC of its address and the
  UTC day with PASS_SECRET, never the address, a new one each day, and not the code her chat's memory files a wallet
  under, so a question can't be matched to a name or notes) go to the database (`live_ask` in `supabase/live.sql`, with
  `p_holder`, `p_holder_code`, `p_head`). It gives the badge only while that code has had fewer than 5 today, and sets the
  question's place in line, `line_at`, to the time it was sent minus 10 minutes; every place in her line is read by
  `(line_at or the time it was sent, id)`: the next question for her (`live_take`), "#3 in line" (`live_ask`,
  `live_lookup`) and the host's panel (`live_state_get`, `live_control`).
- **Old and new together:** the new code with live.sql from before 2026-10-10 asks a question without a badge exactly as
  before, and a question with one without it (the log says once to run live.sql again); the new `live_ask` takes the old
  call too (its new settings have defaults).
- **On her stream** (`tools/live/run.mjs`): the card's badge (`card-badge` in `tools/live/page/`: only "Crush" or
  "Soulmate", for a question card; 99% opaque, like everything over her picture), then for a Soulmate confetti and a
  shout-out (`SHOUTOUTS` in `tools/live/lines.js`: four pre-written lines, all about her being happy they're there, never
  about money or holding), then the question read out loud and her answer as always. `--demo` has a Soulmate (Jun) and a
  Crush (Nia) among its made-up questions.

**Owner, in this order** (no Vercel setting):
1. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/live.sql` → Run: it ends with
   `live_functions_found = 13`. **Before pushing** (it keeps everything saved).
2. **Push** (the PC).
3. **On the server:** `cd /opt/agi1-live/site && sh tools/live/live.sh update`, then `sh tools/live/live.sh --warm` (the
   voices of her 4 shout-out lines, once).

**Cost:** nothing new to pay: a wallet's level is read at most every 30 minutes per session (Robinhood Chain's free node),
and her 4 new lines' voices once (about $0.01).

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs):

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A question sent with a Crush wallet shows no badge | `[live] a question came with a 💜 badge, but supabase/live.sql is from before 2026-10-10: it went in without one…` | Run `supabase/live.sql` again |
| "Your wallet's 💜 badges for today are used (5 a day)" | (none) | By design: a new day at 00:00 UTC |
| A wallet with 10,000+ $AGI says "Stranger" | (none) | Its level is read again at most every 30 minutes (it just got its $AGI): Disconnect, then Connect a wallet again (a new sign-in reads it at once) |
| No shout-out for a Soulmate's question on stream | (none) | The server's code is from before 2026-10-10: `sh tools/live/live.sh update` |

**Tests:** `tests/live.test.js` (3 new: her 💜 badge and its 10-minute head start through `/api/live` (never further), 5
a day per wallet, a Stranger's, a broken session, never the address in the database, live.sql from before; `liveHolder()`
(the session, its level read again when it's 30 minutes old with burned $AGI counted, the chain away); the page's words

day per wallet code, the head start never further than 10 minutes, the line's order in every function that reads it, the

## AGI-1's 3D character studio (2026-10-10)

**Since AGI Studio (the same day, see "AGI Studio, the AI influencer app"):** its page is the app's (agi1.app/studio is AGI
Studio, and a character's page, agi1.app/studio/<id>, its 3D model view: `src/studio/views/model3d.js`), and a character
is made from an influencer's full-body picture inside the app (Meshy's image to 3D, its first step `image`, then its bones
and moves), paid in credits. Ordering a character from words (`studio-quote`) answers 410 `moved`; a character's page, its
files, and finishing an order made before still work. `src/studio/page.js`, `src/studio/words.js` and
`src/styles/studio.css` are gone. What follows is the studio as it was first built, that morning.

**The owner's idea** (in the next big plan, item 3): "what if i launched a where they can create a 3d model with meshy ai
api that can move on chat just like vladcat. they can get it by burning $AGI tokens and can launch token with it", and
"you can also add more utiliy to $agi so holders are happy". The owner's choices (asked one by one): paid **by burning
$AGI or in USDG** ("Burn $AGI or USDG"), with **holder discounts** and **a free one a month for Soulmates**, burns capped a
month (a burn pays nobody, while each character costs the owner Meshy's credits); **Meshy Pro** (the owner's account,
about $20 a month) and **Vercel Pro** ($20 a month: selling characters is commercial use, which Hobby doesn't allow), the
owner switching them on when ready. Telegram bots for people's own characters: later. Short videos of the characters
(Seedance, item 4 of the plan): built the same day (see "Its videos" below). **Off until the owner sets it up, then private to the owner's wallet** (`STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`)
until Meshy says its terms allow selling what it makes (`STUDIO_OPEN`: see "Open questions"). Visitor-facing words never
name Meshy ("an AI service"; a character that couldn't be made is kept as `ai:<step>`, never the service's name).

**What visitors see** (agi1.app/studio: `studio.html`, `src/studio/page.js`, `src/styles/studio.css`; not linked from the
other pages while it's private):
- **The studio:** "Make a 3D character", how many are left this month ("12 characters left to make this month"; private:
  "The studio is private for now…"; sold out: "…opens again on the 1st (UTC)"), then its steps, each once the one before
  is done: **18+ only** (the chat's own confirmation, shared with it); **1 Your wallet** (the site's sign-in: an address and
  a free signature, the same session as the home page's; its price by level: "0x12ab…cdef · Crush. Your price: $4 in USDG
  or 12,000 $AGI burned (Crush: 20% off)."; a wallet not on the private list: "The studio is private for now, and this
  wallet isn't on its list"); **2 Describe it** (its name, up to 24 characters; what it looks like, 10 to 400; its style:
  Anime, Cartoon or Realistic), **Get my price** (the human check, Turnstile action `studio`, or the 2-hour pass), our
  server's "no" in words under it with the keyboard on the box to fix ("Never a real person: describe someone of your
  own."); **3 Pay for it**: its price, USDG and/or Burn $AGI (and for a Soulmate, Free), where to send it ("Send $4 in
  USDG", the studio's wallet or the burn address with **Copy**, "from your connected wallet, in your own wallet app, on
  Robinhood Chain", only the official token counts), **Check my payment** (or a pasted transaction link or ID; payments add
  up: "Counted: $1.50 of $4. Send the rest ($2.50) from the same wallet, then check again."), **Start over**. A quote
  holds its place in the month for a day; the browser remembers it (`agi1_studio_order`) to come back to. Paid: "Payment
  found: your character is being made now 💜", then its own page.
- **Your characters** (with a wallet: Ready, Being made, Couldn't be made: try again free, Waiting for payment), **Made
  in the studio** (the newest 24, with their pictures), **Before you make one** (its rules: made by an AI service and may not
  look exactly as pictured, PG-13 and never a real person or someone else's character, paid from your own wallet app,
  holder discounts "a thank-you for holding, not an investment", no refunds but made again free if it can't be made,
  public by link, a limited number a month, not financial advice).
- **A character's page** (agi1.app/studio/<id>, the same page: `vercel.json` rewrites `/studio/:id` to `/studio`; public to
  anyone with its link): its name, its description, its style and day. **While it's made:** its five steps (Shaping it,
  Painting it, Giving it bones, Teaching it moves, Saving it), the one now with the AI's percentage, "It takes about 5 to
  10 minutes. You can close this page: it keeps going", asked again every 5 s while the page is open (which also moves

  message naming a move, or a word for one ("hi", "yay", "thanks", "boogie"…: `MOVE_WORDS` in `src/studio/rules.js`),
  plays it, anything else gets a reaction (a wave, a cheer, a jump or a bow), and it stands again after; nothing typed
  leaves the page (a log of the last 6). On computers a drag turns it (never a zoom: the wheel scrolls the page); on phones
  a swipe scrolls the page. **Download its picture** (PNG, 1024 px) and **its 3D model** (GLB: its bones and its 8 moves,
  for a 3D stream or a 3D app), **Share on X ↗** (the visitor posts: "Meet Mochi, my 3D character from AGI-1's studio 💜
  type a move and watch it go:"), and **Launch a coin with its face** (save its picture, send it to her bot with
  `/launch`: the launch's own rules, 10,000+ $AGI in the wallet that launches; shown when `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT` is set).
  Without WebGL, or when its file can't be read: its picture, and "It can't be shown in 3D in this browser: here's its
  picture."
- **A paid character that couldn't be made** (the AI's safety check stopped its words, its bones didn't fit, it took too
  long, its files couldn't be kept): its page says why, and the wallet that paid can make it again with new words, free
  (its words to change, as they were).

**How it's made** (`server/studio.js`, `server/meshy.js`, `server/studio-words.js`):
1. **Its words, checked first** (`checkCharacter()`): PG-13 (the site's crude-word lists and adult words), never a child,
   nothing hateful, never a real person (the live show's list of famous people too), never someone else's character or a
   brand's mascot, nothing passing for AGI-1, no links, @names, emails or phone numbers. Then **Meshy's own screening**
   (`moderation: true`) when it starts.
2. **Meshy's four tasks, one after another** (its API, `docs.meshy.ai`, read 2026-10-10): a model from its words (text to
   3D, `preview`: one humanoid figure with two arms and two legs in an A-pose, about 20,000 triangles, its style's words
   added: `meshyPrompt()`), painted (`refine`, a 2K texture: `meshyTexture()`), given bones (`rigging`, 1.7 m tall: Meshy's
   rigging is for two-legged humanoids), taught its 8 moves (`animations`, Meshy's library: Idle 0, Big_Wave_Hello 28,
   FunnyDancing_01 22, Happy_jump_f 44, Victory_Cheer 59, Formal_Bow 41, Casual_Walk 30, All_Night_Dance 64; one file with
   a clip each, in that order). **59 credits** a character (20 + 10 + 5 + 3 a move). A task that fails gives its credits back.
3. **Moved along one step at a time**, by its page while someone has it open and by the clock: Supabase Cron calls
   `GET /api/feed?studio` every minute (`supabase/studio.sql`, its own key from the database, like her buy bot's), up to 6
   characters a run; never two at once for one character (a lease in the database).
4. **Its files kept** (`server/studio-files.js`): Meshy keeps what it makes for 3 days, so our server reads its files
   (only Meshy's own https addresses, never a redirect), makes its model small (under 4 MB: Vercel answers at most 4.5 MB;
   its textures 1024 px, or 512 if still too big, as JPEG, or PNG where they're see-through: glTF's own formats, so the
   file opens anywhere, never only in a browser; its moves resampled, copies merged, what nothing uses pruned; its geometry,
   bones and moves as made; gltf-transform and sharp) and its picture (the refine's: a 384 px WebP for the pages, a 1024 px
   PNG to download), and keeps them in **Supabase Storage**, a private bucket (`agi1-characters`, 40 MB a file since its videos, 8 MB before), served from
   our own address (`/api/launch?studio-file=<id>.glb|webp|png`: only a done character's, kept a day by Vercel's CDN, in a
   sandbox: `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `nosniff`). Saving starts only with 15 s left in the run, each wait bounded, so
   it always ends inside Vercel's 25 s. gltf-transform and sharp are loaded only for that (a dynamic import), so the clock's
   other jobs in `/api/feed` (her buy bot, her quizzes) start as light as before; Vercel's own file tracer puts
   `/api/launch` and `/api/feed` at about 45 MB each with them (Vercel allows 250 MB a function).
5. **When things go wrong:** Meshy's key refused, no credits, or its queue full → the character waits (never failed), and
   the log tells the owner once per server copy; a step that fails at Meshy → tried again twice, then failed with a
   credit (made again free); its words stopped by Meshy's screening, or its bones that can't find its pose → failed with a
   credit; not done 3 days after it started → expired (failed, with a credit: Meshy has let go of its files); its files
   that can't be kept → tried 4 times, then failed with a credit (too big to serve: the same).
6. **On its page** (`src/studio/viewer.js`): its clips by move (by the library's names when every clip has one, "Armature|
   Idle" too, else in the order asked for: `clipsFor()`); each move in place (`inPlace()`: of the node that travels
   furthest across the floor, the drift from its first key to its last is taken out, as the world sees it, whatever its
   armature's turn and scale: a walk stays put, a jump still jumps, a dance still sways); framed for every pose of every
   move (`movesBox()`: each move looked at 8 times a second and at its hips' highest and lowest, a sample of its points
   each time, so a jump or raised arms never leave the picture); its whole height filling most of the picture, a little
   from above; light from a soft room, a sky light and a sun (`NeutralToneMapping`); glTF's default metalness tamed (it
   read as chrome); drawn only while on screen and the tab is shown, at most about 60 times a second.

**Paying** (`server/studio-chain.js`; hard rule 9: never asked of a wallet):
- **USDG** (Paxos' Global Dollar on Robinhood Chain, `0x5fc5…d168`, docs.robinhood.com/chain/contracts) sent to the
  owner's wallet (`STUDIO_PAY_TO`: an address, not a secret), or **$AGI burned** (to `0x…dEaD`, or the coin's own
  `burn()`): the visitor sends it from their own wallet app, then presses **Check my payment**.
- Our server reads it on Robinhood Chain (read-only: its receipt and its block's time from the public node; the block
  explorer's list of the wallet's transfers only to know which to read, at most 3 a check): it counts when it succeeded,
  moved the official token (its contract's own Transfer events, never a look-alike) from the connected wallet to where it
  should go, after its quote (a minute's leeway) and in the last 7 days. **Each payment counts once** (`studio.sql`); **a
  burn shares burns.sql's ledger** (it counts for messages or for a character, never both), and what's burned for a
  character counts toward the wallet's level like a burn for messages. Payments add up; the last one that completes it
  starts the making.
- **Prices** (a Stranger's, in Vercel): `STUDIO_PRICE_USD` (5) and `STUDIO_PRICE_AGI` (15,000); **Crush 20% off, Soulmate
  40% off and one free a month** (`DISCOUNT` in `src/studio/rules.js`; the level read on our server, again when it's 30
  minutes old, burned $AGI counted). A Soulmate's free one is paid at once.
- **Per month (UTC):** `STUDIO_A_MONTH` characters (15), `STUDIO_BURNS_A_MONTH` of them paid by burning (5); a quote
  holds a place for a day; 2 quotes waiting at once per wallet. A character paid in full is always made, even if it goes
  over the month's number (a payment that completes a quote held more than a day).
- No refunds (the page and its rules say so); a paid one that can't be made is made again with new words, free.

**What's kept** (`supabase/studio.sql`, row level security on, only the server's key): per character a scrambled code of
its wallet (an HMAC with PASS_SECRET, `studioWallet()`: never the address, and not the code her chat's memory or burns
use), its name, words and style, the level and price it was offered, how it's paid and how much so far, where it is in the
making (Meshy's task ids, a lease), and once done its files' sizes and its moves; per payment counted, a scrambled code of
it (never the transaction); per month, characters paid and paid by burning; per wallet code and month, its free one; its
files in the private bucket. A done character stays (its page is public); a quote never paid goes after 2 days; a failed
one after 30 days (60 with a credit to make it again). The safety note's 01, 02 and 04 say so (shown with the burns'
sentences: the studio needs burns.sql).

**Taking one down:** Supabase → SQL Editor → `select studio_hide('<its id>', true);` (`false` shows it again), or Vercel
→ `STUDIO_HIDE` = its id (several: commas), then Redeploy. Its page, files and gallery entry go (404); nothing is deleted.

**Setup (the owner, in this order):**
1. **Vercel Pro** (the owner's choice): Vercel → the team's Settings → Billing → upgrade to Pro ($20 a month). Selling
   characters is commercial use, which the Hobby plan doesn't allow.
2. **Meshy:** meshy.ai → an account on **Pro** (about $20 a month, 1,000 credits: about 16 characters at 59 each) → its
   developer platform → **API keys** → a new key (name it "agi1 studio"), **with a monthly credit limit** if Meshy offers
   one (a cap on what a bug could spend) → Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings → Environment Variables → `MESHY_API_KEY`
   (Production). A secret: never in chat, code, git or a screenshot.
3. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/studio.sql` → Run (after `burns.sql`; Cron and pg_net
   are on already, for her buy bot). It ends with `studio_ready = 1`, `studio_scheduled = 1` and `studio_storage = 1`.
4. **Vercel** → Environment Variables (Production): `STUDIO_PAY_TO` = the owner's own wallet's address on Robinhood Chain
   (where USDG goes: an address, never a key; a wallet the owner controls, not an exchange's), `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR` = the
   owner's own wallet address (private first: only it may make one). Optional: `STUDIO_PRICE_USD` (5), `STUDIO_PRICE_AGI`
   (15000), `STUDIO_A_MONTH` (15), `STUDIO_BURNS_A_MONTH` (5; 0 = no burns). Then **push**, and **Redeploy** if the
   settings came after the push.
5. **Try it** at agi1.app/studio with that wallet: 18+, connect, describe one, pay (a little USDG, or a burn; a Soulmate's
   free one), then watch its page (about 5 to 10 minutes). Its moves on its page, and its GLB in Blender or a 3D stream,
   are the first real check of what Meshy makes (see "Not tried live").
6. **Before opening it to everyone** (`STUDIO_OPEN` = `yes`, Redeploy): ask Meshy whether its terms allow a service that
   sells what it makes to others (see "Open questions"); then a link to it from the other pages (Claude adds it).

**Cost:** Meshy Pro about $20 a month (1,000 credits: about 16 characters; more: Meshy's bigger plans or credit packs), so
about $1.20 of credits a character; Vercel Pro $20 a month; Supabase Storage on its free plan (1 GB: a character is about 1
to 4 MB, so a few hundred), the chain's public node and the block explorer free. What it brings in: a Stranger's
character $5 in USDG ($4 a Crush's, $3 a Soulmate's) to the owner's wallet; a burned one brings nothing (5 a month at
most: about $6 of credits), and a Soulmate's free one costs its credits too. The owner's to check: Meshy's and Vercel's
own prices on their pages, and taxes on what's sold (not financial or legal advice).

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs):

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| agi1.app/studio says "The studio opens soon." | `[studio] MESHY_API_KEY is missing: the studio is off` (or none) | Setup steps 2–4, then Redeploy |
| "The studio opens soon." after setting it up | `[studio] … studio_month … PGRST202` (or none) | Run `supabase/studio.sql` (setup step 3) |
| Characters wait at "Shaping it" for ever | `[studio] a character waits: meshy HTTP 401 … (MESHY_API_KEY is wrong or was deleted …)` | A new key in Meshy, `MESHY_API_KEY` in Vercel, Redeploy. They carry on by themselves |
| Characters wait | `[studio] a character waits: meshy HTTP 402 … (no Meshy credits left …)` | Credits in Meshy (or the key's monthly limit raised). They carry on by themselves |
| Characters only move along while their page is open | (none: the clock isn't calling) | `studio.sql` (`studio_scheduled` must be 1); Supabase → Integrations → Cron should list `agi1-studio` every minute |
| The clock's calls get 401 | `[studio] couldn't read the studio's key: …` | Run `supabase/studio.sql` again (it keeps its key) |
| "Its files couldn't be kept." | `[studio] <id>'s files couldn't be kept: storage HTTP 400 … (run supabase/studio.sql: it makes the bucket)` | Setup step 3; the person makes it again, free |
| "It came out too big to keep." | `… the model is still 4.6 MB made small …` | Rare (Meshy's texture or mesh far bigger than usual); made again free. Tell Claude if it repeats |
| A character's page shows its picture instead of 3D | (none) | The visitor's browser has no WebGL, or its file couldn't be read (`[studio] a character's file: …`) |
| A done character plays the wrong move for a button | `[studio] <id>'s file has 7 moves (8 asked for)` | Meshy left a move out or named its clips differently: tell Claude with the id (the page maps clips by Meshy's library names, else by order) |
| "Couldn't look up your payments just now" | `[studio] checking a payment (explorer): …` | The block explorer didn't answer: paste the transaction's link, or try later |
| "Something went wrong on our side" on every action | `[studio] studio-…: …` | The database (a paused Supabase project: resume it) |

### Its videos (2026-10-10)

**Since AGI Studio (the same day):** a character's video isn't ordered any more (`studio-video-quote` answers 410
`moved`): an influencer's videos are made in the app, paid in credits. A character's videos still play and download, and
an order made before can be finished.

**The owner's idea** (item 4 of the plan): "they can create a viral content with it using seedance 2.5 api but they gonna
pay crypto like stables instead of $agi if they hold agi they get a discount, theyll be like ai influencers"; the owner's
choice: about $4 in USDG for a 5-second 720p clip, before holder discounts. Built the same day as the studio, as part of
it: the wallet that made a character can have short videos of it made by an AI video service (Seedance 2.5's
reference-to-video, on fal.ai), from the character's own picture and a scene it describes, paid only in USDG. **Off until
`FAL_KEY` is set** (and the studio is on, with `STUDIO_PAY_TO`), and private like the studio (`STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`). Words
visitors read never name fal, Seedance or ByteDance ("an AI video service"; a failure is kept as `ai:make`, `refused`,
`save`, `too_big`, `expired` or `no_char`).

**What visitors see** (a done character's page, "Its videos": `studio.html`, `src/studio/page.js`, `src/styles/studio.css`):
- **Its done videos, for everyone**, one a row: its player as tall, wide or square as the video (a vertical one 200 px wide
  beside its words, a square one 260, a wide one the card's width; on phones one under the other, at most 240 and 320 px
  wide), its picture first and nothing downloaded until it's played (`preload="none"`), its scene, "AI-generated · 5 s ·
  Vertical · with sound", **Download** (an MP4 named "<Name>-AI-video.mp4") and **Share on X ↗** (the visitor posts:
  "Mochi, my 3D character from AGI-1's studio, in an AI-made video 💜", with a link straight to that video on the page,
  `#v-<its id>`: the page goes there once its videos are shown). "No videos of it yet." while there are none.
- **Make a video of it** (while videos are on): "5 seconds of Mochi in any scene you describe: $4 in USDG. Crush (10,000+
  $AGI) gets 20% off, Soulmate (1,000,000+) 40% off. Only the wallet that made Mochi can make its videos." Then **18+**
  (the chat's own confirmation), **Connect the wallet that made it** (the site's sign-in: an address and a free
  signature), and its price for that wallet ("$3.20 in USDG (Crush: 20% off)"). Another wallet: "Only the wallet that made
  Mochi can make its videos."; a private studio, or the month's all spoken for: said, and no form.
- **The form:** what happens in it (10 to 300 characters: "dancing on a neon rooftop in the rain at night, the city glowing
  behind it"), its shape (Vertical for TikTok, Reels and Shorts; Wide for X and YouTube; Square), **With sound** (its sounds
  and music, made by the AI too), **Get my price** (the human check, Turnstile action `studio`, or the 2-hour pass). Its
  words checked here and by our server (the studio's rules: PG-13, never a real person or someone else's character); our
  server's "no" in words, with the keyboard on the box to fix.
- **Paying:** "Send $3.20 in USDG", for which video, from the connected wallet in its own wallet app, to the studio's wallet
  (**Copy**); only USDG counts (its contract), no refunds, and one that can't be made is made again with a new scene, free;
  **Check my payment** (or a pasted transaction; payments add up: "Counted: $1.50 of $3.20. Send the rest ($1.70) from
  the same wallet, then check again."), **Later** (it waits in its list with **Pay for it**; a quote holds its place a
  day). Paid: "Payment found: your video is being made now 💜".
- **While it's made:** in its list, "Waiting its turn… (#2 in line)", "Making it…", "Saving it…", with a pulsing dot (still
  with "reduce motion") and "It takes a few minutes: you can close this page.", asked again every 5 s while the page is
  open; then it plays right there.
- **One that couldn't be made** (the AI's safety check stopped its scene, it took too long, its file couldn't be kept, its
  character was taken down): why, and **Make it again, free** (its scene, shape and sound to change, as they were; even
  when the month's videos are all spoken for).

**How it's made** (`server/studio-video.js`, `server/fal.js`; `checkScene()` and `videoPrompt()` in `server/studio-words.js`):
1. **Its scene, checked first** (the studio's rules), then by the video service's own safety check.
2. **fal.ai's queue** (its docs, read 2026-10-10): `POST https://queue.fal.run/<model>` with `Authorization: Key <FAL_KEY>`
   (our server only ever sends the key there, never in a log or an error), then its state (in its queue with its place,
   in progress, done or failed) and its result. The model: `bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video` (`STUDIO_VIDEO_MODEL`
   picks another that takes the same inputs). What it gets: the character's own picture as `@Image1` (a signed address to
   it in the private bucket, good 6 hours), the scene in `videoPrompt()`'s words (keep its look exactly as in the picture;
   the scene; one continuous shot in its style; family-friendly; anyone else a made-up extra, never a real person; no
   text, captions, logos or watermarks), 5 seconds, 720p, its shape (9:16, 16:9 or 1:1), with sound or not, H.264 (so it
   plays in every browser), and an id for who asked that's an HMAC, never the wallet or its code here. fal keeps what it
   makes 7 days at most (`X-Fal-Object-Lifecycle-Preference`).
3. **Moved along** by its page while it's open (`studio-video-look`, every 5 s) and by the studio's clock every minute
   (`/api/feed?studio`, up to 4 videos a run, after the characters), never two at once for one video (a lease).
4. **Its file kept:** the MP4 read from fal's own media addresses only (`fal.media`, `*.fal.media`,
   `storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/`; https, no redirects, 40 MB at most, a real MP4 by its first bytes), kept as it is
   in the studio's private bucket (`videos/<id>.mp4`; the bucket takes 40 MB a file and `video/mp4` since then).
5. **When things go wrong:** fal's key refused, no balance left, its queue full or fal down for a moment → it waits (never
   failed; the log tells the owner once per server copy); its safety check → failed, with a credit; another failure → sent
   again twice, then failed with a credit; not made 12 hours after it started → failed with a credit; its file not kept
   after 4 tries (or too big) → failed with a credit; its character taken down → failed with a credit (`no_char`).

**Played from our own address, in parts** (`/api/launch?studio-video=<id>.mp4`: `videoFile()` in `server/studio-video.js`,
`byteRange()` and `getRange()` in `server/studio-files.js`): the page's CSP lets no other site's media in, and must keep
"no wildcard anywhere" (`tests/popout.test.js`; adding Supabase's address for videos failed it, 2026-10-10), so a video
never plays from Supabase's address. A video player asks for its file with "Range" (every browser's does; Safari plays
nothing without it): our server answers that part (206 Partial Content, at most 4,000,000 bytes: Vercel answers at most
4.5 MB), read from Storage with the same Range, and the player asks for the next part by itself. Without Range, a small
file (4 MB or less) comes whole (200, kept by the CDN a day); a big one opened in a tab, and **Download**, go to a
short-lived signed address in the bucket (302, 2 hours; the download named "<Name>-AI-video.mp4"). A part past its end is
416. Every answer in a sandbox (`default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `nosniff`).

**Paying** (USDG only, the owner's: "they gonna pay crypto like stables instead of $agi"): like a character's USDG (read on
Robinhood Chain, each payment once, in the same ledger as characters', so one payment never pays for two things), to
`STUDIO_PAY_TO`. **Prices:** `STUDIO_VIDEO_PRICE_USD` (4) for a Stranger, Crush 20% off ($3.20), Soulmate 40% off ($2.40):
the studio's discounts, "a thank-you for holding, not an investment"; never $AGI, no free ones. **Per month (UTC):**
`STUDIO_VIDEOS_A_MONTH` (30) for the whole site; a quote holds a place for a day; 2 quotes waiting at once per wallet. No
refunds; one that can't be made is made again with a new scene, free.

**What's kept** (`agi1_studio_videos` in `supabase/studio.sql`, only the server's key): per video the same scrambled wallet
code as its character's, its character, the scene, its shape and sound, its level and price, what's paid so far, where it
is in the making (fal's request id and the two addresses fal gave for it, a lease, its tries), and once done its file's
size; its payments' scrambled codes with the characters' (`agi1_studio_txs`); videos a month with the characters' months;
its file in the bucket. A done one stays (public on its character's page); one never paid goes after 2 days; a failed one
after 30 days (60 with a credit). The safety note's 01, 02 and 04 say so. **Taking one down:**
`select studio_video_hide('<its id>', true);` (`false` shows it again), or its id in `STUDIO_HIDE`, then Redeploy (a hidden
character hides its videos too).

**Setup (the owner, once the studio is set up):**
1. **fal.ai:** fal.ai → sign up → **Billing**: add a little balance (fal takes each video's price from it; when it's empty,
   videos wait) → **API Keys** → a new key (name it "agi1 studio videos") → Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings →
   Environment Variables → `FAL_KEY` (Production). A secret: never in chat, code, git or a screenshot.
2. `STUDIO_PAY_TO` must be set (videos are USDG only). `supabase/studio.sql` has its videos: run it again if it was run
   before them (it keeps everything; it still ends with `studio_ready = 1`).
3. Optional (Vercel, then Redeploy): `STUDIO_VIDEO_PRICE_USD` (4), `STUDIO_VIDEOS_A_MONTH` (30), `STUDIO_VIDEO_MODEL`.
4. **Push** (or Redeploy if it's pushed), then on your own character's page: "Make a video of it", a scene, pay a little
   USDG, and a few minutes later it plays there. Try it on an iPhone too (Safari is the strictest about video).

**Cost:** fal.ai about $2.40 a 5-second 720p video (about $0.47 a second, fal's page, 2026-10-10), taken from the balance
the owner tops up; a video made again (free for its owner) is one more video at fal. Supabase Storage holds it (a 5-second 720p video is a few MB:
the free plan's 1 GB holds a few hundred with the characters), and each play on its page is read through our server, so
it uses Supabase's egress (the free plan's 5 GB a month, shared with the database) and Vercel's bandwidth and function
calls (Pro). What it brings in: a Stranger's video $4 in USDG, a Crush's $3.20, a Soulmate's $2.40 (about fal's own
price: Claude told the owner), to the owner's wallet; at most 30 a month by default.

## AGI Studio, the AI influencer app (2026-10-10)

**The owner's request** (the same day as the 3D character studio): "in making the 3c character, why i cant upload a
refetence just like the meshy and wheres the trending video? , i i want it sopmething likehiggsfield ai influencer you
know that right and like higgsfield genjuts and then they can launch a token with it on clank and aan you make it
studio.agi1.app , the ui will be different on this it will be user friendly and easy to use". So a new app, **AGI Studio**,
in the spirit of Higgsfield's AI influencer and its trend videos (never its name, look or code): make your own AI
influencer, then its photos, trend videos, short videos, a 3D model and a coin with its face. The owner's choices (asked
one by one): uploads **"Their own face too"** (a live selfie with consent; since round 2 photos with consent instead),
**"2D influencer, 3D extra (Recommended)"**, trend moves **"Our presets + their clips (Recommended)"** (since round 2
real-looking clips), **"Kling V3 Standard (Recommended)"** for trend videos (since round 2 Kling O1 Edit),
**"Credits (Recommended)"** (1 credit = 1 cent, bought with USDG), **"Discounts + free credits (Recommended)"** for
holders, and the trend moves **"Made with AI once (Recommended)"**. It replaces the 3D studio's page: agi1.app/studio is
the app too, and a character from words and its videos aren't ordered any more (see "AGI-1's 3D character studio").
**Off until the owner sets it up** (below), then **private like the studio** (`STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`) until `STUDIO_OPEN`.
Words visitors read never name the AI services ("an AI service"; a failure is kept as `ai:<kind>`, `refused`, `save`…).
**Its round 2, the same day,** changed a good part of what follows: no "Use my face" (no camera at all), photos of real
people with consent, real-looking trend clips, example pictures, a new look, likes and a weekly spotlight, burn unlocks,
the share mark and a live stats board. See "AGI Studio, round 2" below; the parts here say what changed.

**What visitors see** (studio.agi1.app; agi1.app/studio and agi1.app/studio/<view> are the same app):

- **My studio** (`/me`): the wallet and its level, its credits (and how many are this month's free ones), **Buy credits**,
