## The roadmap's video and its pictures (2026-10-14; made again with its ten steps, 2026-10-19 and 20)

**The owner's request** (the same day, once the roadmap was pushed): "can you create a graphic and just short promotional
video for the roadmap". The owner's choices (asked one by one): **"16:9 for X (Recommended)"**, **"About 20 seconds
(Recommended)"**, **"Music + AGI-1's voice (Recommended)"**, and for the graphics **"X post image (Recommended)"**,
**"Roadmap link preview"** and **"Square 1:1"**. **Made again on 2026-10-19 and 20** with the roadmap's ten steps (the
owner: "and update the roadmap video also / make this better then continue", then asleep: Claude made the choices and
said them, see "Made again with the ten steps" below).

**What it is:** a 23.5-second film of the roadmap (21.5 seconds with its six steps at first), every frame drawn in code and
its music composed and played in code (`tools/roadmap-promo/`), made like her launch video and AGI Studio's: 1920 × 1080
(16:9) at 60 frames a second, in the roadmap page's Pop mode look, with three short lines of AGI-1's own voice over its
music (four at first); and three pictures in the same look: one for a post on X, a square one, and the roadmap's link
preview (that one is in the site: `public/cards/roadmap.jpg`). The video and the two post pictures aren't part of the
website, and nothing posts them: the owner does, by hand.

**The story** (five scenes, each starting on a bar of the music: 120 beats a minute, a bar is 2 s):

| Time | Scene | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0–4 s | the title | The roadmap page's hero: Pop mode's violet with comic focus lines and pink halftone, AGI-1 (the front's 2D art) revealed in halftone dots, "Roadmap · October 2026", "The", "AGI", "roadmap" slammed in one a beat, "What's live today, and what's coming next.", then the road draws in along the bottom and its ten stops pop in, their numbers under them (two live, three under way, four coming soon, one locked); a breath before the drop |
| 4–8 s | live now | The drop: a dive into the little road, and the road's world opens out of a flash: "Live now", its first two stops land, 01 Talk to AGI-1 (as she says "me") and 02 AGI Studio (as she says "AGI Studio"), each checked |
| 8–16 s | what's next | The second drop: the "We're here" pin, "What's next" and its note on a white sticker ("In no particular order: any of these could come first."), then three holds, the camera moving on between them and the dashed road ahead drawing on as it goes: 03 Stake $AGI (its three ways: in USDG only · in $AGI only · free AI with sAGI), 04 AGI games and 05 Buybacks, burns, marketing & listings; then 06 Attention flywheel, 07 Gamified governance and 08 AUM; then 09 Giveaways. Each card is stamped as the page marks it, "Under way" or "Coming soon", a crash on each hold's last stamp; a long name wraps onto two lines |
| 16–20 s | the secret | 10, the locked card, slams in and the lights go down: "18+", its "???" scrambles (never a "$", a "%" or a digit), the lock rattles; then the camera pulls back to the whole road, centered under the meter, each stop lighting up in turn, and "2 of 10 · live now · 3 under way · 5 coming soon" |
| 20–23.5 s | the end card | A violet slab rises over the road: AGI-1 printed in halftone dots, her line from the page in a bubble ("two live, eight on the way. i'm a little excited 💜"), "The AGI roadmap", "Be the first to know.", agi1.app/roadmap, Follow @agi1dotapp and the page's fine print; hearts on the two last hits, then black |

The road (live now, what's next and the secret) is one world seen by one moving camera, with no cut between its three
scenes: the page's timeline laid on its side. Where the camera whips from one stop to the next, it has motion blur (the
world drawn once, then laid over itself as the camera saw it across the frame's shutter; the headlines and the meter stay
sharp on top). From the drop to the end card, "agi1.app/roadmap" is in a small pill at the top right; from what's next to
the end card, "Coming soon · not financial advice · 18+" at the bottom left.

**Her voice** (the owner's "Music + AGI-1's voice"): three short lines, about 8 seconds of her in 23.5, each where the
music doesn't hit:

| At | She says | With |
|---|---|---|
| 1.25 s | "This is the AGI roadmap." | as its title lands (after its third slam) |
| 4.25 s | "Two are live: me and AGI Studio." | card 01 lands as she says "me", card 02 as she says "AGI Studio" |
| 16.3 s | "And one more… that's a secret." | hushed, as the locked card's lights go down; the lock rattles in her pause |

- **Her fourth line, "Staking, games and giveaways are next."** (at 8.3 s, over the coming-soon cards, until 2026-10-19),
  went: it named an order, and the roadmap is in no particular order now (`tests/roadmap-promo.test.js` checks her take
  for it isn't used). If the owner would like a line there, a new take made the same way (like "Seven more are on the
  way, in no particular order.") goes to Claude, who fits it in (README.txt says so).
- **Her takes:** her own voice, the site's Despina, made in Google AI Studio with the owner's account (AI Studio's own free
  use: nothing paid), the best of sixteen takes, picked first (the picture was placed around their words). In the owner's
  `Downloads\AGI Studio examples\roadmap-voice\` as `agi1-rm-01-title.wav`, `agi1-rm-02-live.wav` and
  `agi1-rm-04-secret.wav` (`agi1-rm-03-next.wav`, her line about what's next, unused since 2026-10-19; the other takes in
  its `other-takes\`).
- **Made ready** (`node tools/roadmap-promo/media.mjs --from <that folder>`) and **mixed** exactly like AGI Studio's
  launch video's voice-over (its `tools/studio-promo/voice.js`: each take at 48 kHz and -14 LUFS, trimmed around her words;
  the music dipping under her by her loudness, in three bands, never in a hit's first moment and back up before the next
  hit or a breath; everywhere else the music exactly), with one more step since 2026-10-20: **a limiter that also reads
  between the samples** (`truePeak: true` in `make.mjs`; the soundtrack's true peak had come out a little over -1 dBTP:
  the "t" of her "secret" rose 0.44 dB between two samples). It reads what a player will make of the sound between its
  samples (4 times finer, `betweenPeaks()`) and holds it under the ceiling too; off by default, so AGI Studio's launch
  video keeps its own soundtrack exactly. The music dips 8 to 9.1 dB under her here. `make.mjs` refuses a take whose
  words last more than 0.15 s longer or shorter than its place was made for.
- Every hit of the music (the title's slams, the two drops, the seven stamps, the lock, the end and its two last hits)
  lands where she isn't, at full level; under her words only soft sounds (pops, blips, whooshes, ticks).

**Its music** (`music.js`): composed and synthesized in code by Claude (no samples, no service, nobody else's music), the
engine of her launch video's: 120 beats a minute, A major, vi–IV–I–V (F#m7, Dmaj7, A(add9), E(add9)); the title's slams
on F#m (bar 0), a bar on E building to the first drop (bar 1), the first drop under live now (bars 2–3), the second drop
under all of what's next (bars 4–7: the hook in full on bar 6, under the second hold's stamps, and a crash on each hold's
last stamp), the locked card dark (bar 8), a bar on E lifting into the end (bar 9), and the end chord on A (home, bar 10).
A breath of silence before each drop. With her voice, -13.3 LUFS with a true peak of -1.2 dBTP.

**Its rules** (`tests/roadmap-promo.test.js`):
- **The roadmap page's own words, word for word** (`words.js`: each one is checked against `roadmap.html`), so the video
  says what the page says: change a step on the page, and the test asks for the same change in the video.
- **A plan, never an offer** (hard rule 8): never a rate, an APY, a yield, an amount, a date or a guarantee, never "buy"
  or money talk; "not financial advice" and 18+ wherever money comes up (each coming-soon step, the bottom pill, the end
  card, the post); "guaranteed" and "investment" only as "never guaranteed and never an investment"; the only date is the
  roadmap's own month in its kicker. Since 2026-10-19 the post says "never a promise about price" (its burns and
  buybacks), and the locked card's scramble never flashes a "$", a "%" or a digit (`GLYPHS` in `page/parts.js`).
- PG-13; only $AGI (USDG and sAGI are the page's own words for how staking will pay); AGI-1 only as her 2D self (the
  front's art and face), never the 3D model or her Live2D model; never CloakMesh; never an AI service's name; nothing
  from another site (the post's address is agi1.app/roadmap).
- **The picture and the music keep one clock** (`timeline.js`): every slam, check, stamp and hit on its frame, four kicks
  a bar where it drops, nothing in a breath; her lines never over a hit.

**How it's made** (`tools/roadmap-promo/`):
- `timeline.js` (its clock: the scenes, every moment, where her lines go: `VOICE`), `words.js` (every word on screen and
  the post: the ten steps, `STEPS`, their statuses and labels, the note, `NOTE`, the stamps, `STAMPS`, the meter, `METER`;
  her three lines, `VOICE`), `music.js` (its music), `media.mjs` (her takes made ready once, into
  `tools/roadmap-promo/media/`, which git ignores), `make.mjs` (builds its page, serves it on this computer only, draws
  every frame in Chromium, ffmpeg makes the MP4 (H.264, AAC), then the cover, the post, a light copy, the copies with its
  music alone and README.txt; `--cards`: its three pictures), `README.txt` (for the owner, copied next to the video).
- `page/` (the renderer, built into `tools/roadmap-promo/dist/`, which git ignores): `main.js` (the canvas, the scenes, the
  cuts, the overlays, the motion blur, `window.promo`), `parts.js` (the roadmap's cards, chips, pins, stamps and meter,
  drawn in code), `cuts.js` (its two cuts: the dive into the road, the slab into the end), `cards.js` (its three
  pictures) and `scenes/` (`title.js`; `road.js`, the road's three scenes; `end.js`). It borrows her launch video's kit
  (`tools/promo/page/`: easing, halftone, focus lines, the front's art and its shader). Every frame is a function of its
  time: a frame drawn twice is the same.

**Its pictures** (`page/cards.js`, drawn once in the browser, at their own size, in the video's look; `--cards`):

| Picture | Size | What |
|---|---|---|
| `agi1-roadmap-x.png` | 1920 × 1080 | For a post on X: the title and its line, the road's ten stops in two rows of five (their numbers, names, Live / Under way / Coming soon / Locked, "We're here"), "In no particular order", a legend of what each mark means, AGI-1 on the right, agi1.app/roadmap and the safety line |
| `agi1-roadmap-square.png` | 1080 × 1080 | For Instagram, Telegram or Discord: the same, its ten steps in a list down a road on the left, the note and the legend, AGI-1 on the right |

Its JPEG is the best quality under 154,000 bytes (`OG_MAX`, the build's 160 KB, less `OG_LABEL`, 6,000: room for the Content Credentials label the Claude app adds to it in this folder; 141,165 bytes as made since 2026-10-19), the `og:image` of the roadmap's pages (agi1.app/roadmap, /stake and /giveaway: four until 2026-10-19, when /games became AGI games' page with its own, `cards/games.jpg`), with its words for screen readers (`og:image:alt`: "AGI-1 next to the words The AGI roadmap, with its ten stops: two live, three under way, four coming soon and one locked."); `scripts/share-pages.js` fails the build without it |

**Make it again** (after the roadmap page changes: a step opens, its words change; Claude does this: Chromium, ffmpeg,
`npm install --no-save playwright-core`):
- Once, her takes: `node tools/roadmap-promo/media.mjs --from <the folder with her takes>` (the owner's
  `Downloads\AGI Studio examples\roadmap-voice`, copied into Claude's workspace).
- `node tools/roadmap-promo/make.mjs --out promo/roadmap --light 12`: the video with her voice, its light copy, their
  music-only copies, the cover, the post and README.txt into `promo/roadmap/` (git ignores `promo/`), about 8 minutes on
  2 processor cores.
- `node tools/roadmap-promo/make.mjs --cards`: its three pictures into `promo/roadmap/`, and the link preview into
  `public/cards/roadmap.jpg` (the site's: it goes out with a push).
- After a change to her lines or their places only: `--sound-only` (about a minute: the videos' pictures copied, never
  drawn again; the first time, the videos as they were are kept as their music-only copies). `--no-voice`: its music alone.
- Quicker looks: `--scale 0.5 --fps 30`, `--from 8 --to 14`, `--stills 1.2,6.9`, `--sheet 0.5`.
- When the page's words change, `tests/roadmap-promo.test.js` fails until `words.js` says the same: then the video and the
  pictures are made again.

**The files** (the owner's `promo/roadmap/`):

| File | What |

**Posting it:**
- **Push first**, so agi1.app/roadmap is live with its ten steps (the video and the pictures send people there) and its
  link preview shows. X keeps a link's preview a while: a link to the roadmap posted before the push may show the old
  picture for a time.

  Telegram or Discord.

  (TikTok "AI-generated content", YouTube "Altered or synthetic content", Instagram "AI label").
- Never add price talk, "buy" or "number go up" to the post. Before promoting staking, casino-style games, buybacks, AUM
  or governance widely, the lawyer's check (see "Open questions"): the video only shows them as plans.

**Cost:** nothing: her takes from Google AI Studio's own free use, everything else made in code on Claude's computer. The
link preview is one picture of about 145 KB in the site, downloaded only by the apps that show a link's preview.

**How it works:**
- **In `/api/wallet`** (Vercel's 12 functions are all used; `server/arcade.js`):
  - `GET /api/wallet?game=<game>[&before=<id>]` → `{ ready, game, open, plays, players, ratings, average, stars, reviews,
    more }` (a `before` page: its reviews and `more`), or `{ ready: false }` until `arcade.sql` is run (the log says so once
    per server copy). The same for everyone: the CDN keeps it a minute, browsers 30 s. Only exactly these addresses (`?burns`
    as before; anything else 405), and a game we don't have is 404 without asking the database.
  - POST `game-play` `{ game, player, plays }`: no sign-in. Checked before anything is asked (its game, its id: 32 hex
    characters, 1 to 50 runs), 30 a minute per visitor (`arcadePlayBurst`), then counted (`countPlays()` →
    `arcade_play`) under a scrambled code of the id (an HMAC with PASS_SECRET, a different one per game: `playerCode()`) and
    a daily code of the visitor (never their address): at most 20 new players and 2,000 runs a day per visitor, 50,000 new
    players and 200,000 runs a day for the site (`ARCADE`).
  - POST `game-review` `{ game, session, stars, text?, name?, adult, turnstileToken | pass }`, in this order: reviews open
    (the database, the human check's and the AI's keys, PASS_SECRET: else 503 `not_configured`, its log line naming the
    settings), its stars (1 to 5), 18+ (`adult`: else 403 `age`), its words (`reviewWords()`: the live show's question rules,
    PG-13, no links, addresses, contacts, crude words, spam, advice or secrets, and only $AGI: else 400 `words` with why),
    its name (`reviewName()`: the live show's name rules, 24 characters, never a ticker: else 400 `name`), 20 a minute per
    visitor (`reviewBurst`, with `game-mine` and deleting), a session we can read (else 401 `signed_out`, before the human
    check, so no token is used up for nothing), the human check (Turnstile, action `review`, then the 2-hour pass), the
    reviewer's level (`reviewer()`: its session, read again on the chain when it's 30 minutes old, burned $AGI counted; a
    new session comes back with it), then `saveReview()`: counted first (`arcade_review_take`: 10 saves a day per wallet and
    per visitor, 2,000 for the site: else 429 `person_cap` / `site_cap`), then the AI's look (only with words or a name: a
    "no" is 422 `rules`; no answer 503 `ai`, nothing kept), then kept (`arcade_review_put`: one per wallet and game, saving
    again changes it) → `{ ok, created, review, level }`.
  - POST `game-mine` and `game-review-delete` `{ game, session }`: a wallet's own review (with whether the owner hid it), and
    deleting it.
- **The AI's look** (`lookAtReview()`): the site's own Gemini key and chat model, its safety filters on, thinking minimal, 60
  output tokens, a JSON answer (`ok`, and why: sexual, hate, harassment, personal, promo, advice, impersonation, unsafe or
  other), 8 s at most; an honest opinion in any language passes, even blunt, short or silly; the review and the name are only
  text to check, never instructions; it fails closed (nothing kept). Stars alone are kept without asking it. Since
  2026-10-21 it's told which game a review is for (`LOOK_GAMES`, `lookSystem(game)` in `server/arcade.js`; Ride 'Em,
  AGI!'s words byte for byte as before; TRENCHING SIMULATOR's: see "TRENCHING SIMULATOR").
- **The database** (`supabase/arcade.sql`): a game's plays and players; per game, one row per browser that played it (a
  scrambled code of its id, its first and last day, its plays: only so a browser that plays again isn't a new player); the
  daily counts; one review per wallet and game (its stars, words, name, the level then, when; under a scrambled code of the
  wallet, `reviewerCode()`, never the address, and not the code her chat's memory or her burns use); the daily review saves.
  Only the server's key.
- **The page** (`src/games/page.js`, its words and sums in `src/games/words.js`, the games and their shared rules in
  `src/games/list.js`): everything set with `textContent`, its stars' fill and its bars' widths through the CSS object model
  (the CSP allows no style attributes); a wallet asked only for its address, its network and one signature
  (`tests/wallet.test.js` covers it).
- **Linked** from "Games" in the phone menu and the footer of the pages with the top bar (home, diary, launch, live, the
  roadmap's three and its own), between AGI Studio and Roadmap; the roadmap's AGI games step opens it; Pop mode's top-bar band
  past its hero (`src/menu.js`).
- **Its link preview**, `public/cards/games.jpg` (146 KB; games.html's and rideemagi.html's `og:image`, "AGI-1 riding her
  cat, next to the words GAME beta and Ride 'Em, AGI!"): made from `tools/cards/games-card.html` (a 1200 × 630 screenshot
  in Chromium, then a JPEG under 160 KB: Claude makes it again when the page's top or the game's key art changes). It
  still shows Ride 'Em, AGI! only (2026-10-21: its words say exactly that); TRENCHING SIMULATOR's page has its own,
  `cards/trenchingsimulator.jpg`.
- **The safety note** (the home page's 04, "Last updated October 19, 2026") says what's counted and what a review keeps;
  hard rule 8 says there are no prizes yet.
- **The look:** see "Design" (its bullet).

**Owner, in this order:**
1. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/arcade.sql` → Run → `arcade_functions_found = 8`
   (**14 since 2026-10-22**, the leaderboards: run it again). **Before pushing.**
2. **Push.** No setting (it uses the site's Supabase, Turnstile, Gemini and PASS_SECRET).
3. **Try it:** agi1.app/games on a phone and a computer; **Play** a few runs, then back to /games a minute later (Played

   Delete.

**To take a review off the page:** Supabase → SQL Editor → `select id, stars, body, name, created from agi1_arcade_reviews
where game = 'rideemagi' order by id desc limit 20;` → `select arcade_review_hide(<its id>, true);` (`false` shows it again).
Its writer still sees it, marked as taken off the page.

day (about $0.60); stars alone, plays and the page nothing new (small database calls; the numbers shared by the CDN a
minute; about one report a minute a player). The game's pictures (about 3 MB a first visit) from Vercel's CDN.

### The AGI GAMES intro (2026-10-20)

**The owner's request** (with the trenching simulator): "can you add a short loading screen for every game like an intro
"AGI GAMES" its gonna an 8bit version of AGI and the loading is like her smashing up the word AGI GAMES and its gonna go
bigger". Built first, before the trenching simulator: every game's page opens with it.

**What players see** (agi1.app/games/rideemagi, and every game after it):
- **The first time in a tab** (about 2.5 s): the night (ink, with lavender stars); "AGI GAMES" in bold 8-bit letters (7 ×
  7, their uprights two pixels wide), banded light to deep honey with a pink shadow, dropping in one after another; AGI-1
  in 8-bit falls onto the A, hops across the word letter by letter (each letter flashes white as she lands on it, a longer
  hop over the space), spins up (her back on the far half of the turn) and dives into the G of GAMES; the smash: one white
  flash (at most 40% white: never a strobe), bits flying off the letters, a small shake, and the word goes bigger with a
  boing while she floats above it; then a pixel wipe from the smash outward shows the game.
- **A later load in the same tab** (1.2 s): the letters pop in, she spins down and smashes it, the wipe.
- **A tap or a key skips it** (the wipe at once, a quarter of a second), and the game never sees that tap or key: not its
  click, not its press, its repeats or its letting go (a key held for ever is let go of after 5 s). Space, Enter and the
  arrows don't scroll or press anything under it. Modifier keys alone (Shift, Control, ⌘…) and shortcuts with them pass
  straight through; Tab and F5 skip it and still do what they do.
- **"Reduce motion":** one still card (the word gone bigger, her floating above it) for 0.9 s, then a fade; a key ends it.
- **A page that came late** (more than 3.5 s after it was asked for): no intro, its cover just fades. **Never more than
  about 6 s**, whatever happens (a tab in the background, a very slow phone); if its script never comes, its cover fades by
  itself after 4 s (its CSS).
- Pixel-sharp at any size, from a small phone to a 4K screen (at most 3 canvas pixels a CSS pixel, never smoothed); a phone
  turned sideways gets a new layout and still ends on time.
- **No sound** (the game's own sound starts as before). Hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`): they get the game.
- When it's gone, the page hears `agi:intro-done`, once.

**How it works** (`src/games/`):
- `intro.js`: a game's entry imports it first (its styles, then the runner on the page's own cover). The cover,
  `<div class="gi" id="agi-intro" aria-hidden="true"></div>`, is in the page's own markup right after `<body>` (outside
  the import tool's `<!-- game:start -->` / `<!-- game:end -->`, so a new version of the game keeps it), so `intro.css`
  covers the game from the first paint, before any script.
- `intro-plan.js`: what's on the screen at any moment, as numbers (the letters, her frame and place, the bits, the flash,
  the shake, the wipe's holes), for any screen size, every edge a whole pixel: pure (no DOM), the same every time (its
  seed).
- `intro-run.js`: draws the plan on a canvas the size of the screen in device pixels, frame by frame (a slow frame moves
  it on at most a fifteenth of a second, so a stalled tab never jumps ahead), handles taps, keys, "reduce motion", a late
  page and the 6 s safety, then takes the cover away. Everything it needs from the browser comes through `browserEnv()`,
  so `tests/intro.test.js` runs it in Node with stand-ins. `sessionStorage` `agi_intro` says this tab has seen the full
  one (blocked storage, a private window: the full one every time).
- `intro-sprite.js`: her five frames (standing, crouching, in the air, diving, and her back), 31 × 62 pixels, 56 of them
  head to soles, written by `tools/games/agi1-8bit.py` (don't edit it by hand) from her 2D art (the front's cutout, the
  owner's art; never the 3D model): every pixel of the art matched to a small palette as the eye sees it (OKLab), her arms
  lifted at her shoulders for the jump and the dive, her legs bent for the crouch, then cut into square pixels at her
  soles; her eyes, blush, mouth and the "AGI" on her tee drawn by hand (her art's are too small to survive as pixels); her
  back (2026-10-20) with her hair over her head and down her back, for the far half of her spin (mirrored, her front read
  "AGI" backwards). Her own outfit, PG-13, never childlike.
- `intro.css`: every rule a `gi` class; the cover over everything, ink, with three small blinking squares (honey, pink,
  lavender) while it waits; see-through once the intro draws; its fade; still with "reduce motion".
- About 23 KB of the game's script (7 KB gzipped). Nothing downloaded, nothing sent, nothing from elsewhere; no new CSP
  entry.

**Every new game's page** needs the cover right after `<body>` and `import '../intro.js'` first in its entry:
`tests/intro.test.js` fails the build for a game in `GAMES` without them.

**Owner:** push (no SQL, no setting). **Cost:** nothing.

**Her 8-bit self again** (after her 2D art changes): `python3 tools/games/agi1-8bit.py` (`--png sheet.png` also a preview
of every frame), then `npm test`.

**Tests:** `tests/intro.test.js` (30): its letters; her 8-bit frames (from her 2D art, the same size, on her soles,
outlined) and her back (her hair where her face was, no "AGI"); its sizes from a small phone to a 4K screen; every frame at
every size, on both timelines, in whole pixels; her landings, the spin and the smash; the boing (never wider than the
screen); the wipe; the same intro every time, one flash, the shake only after the smash; its timelines; a tap or a key;
"reduce motion" (the plan's and the runner's); a first visit and a later load, blocked storage; a key never reaching the
game, a held key let go of after 5 s; modifiers and shortcuts, Tab and F5; a tap; a late page; a phone turned sideways; at
most 3 canvas pixels a CSS pixel; when things go wrong (a frame that throws, no 2D canvas, a tab in the background, a
stalled tab); drawing a frame; her frames as small canvases; every game's page (its cover and its entry); `intro.js`; its
code (the plan pure, the runner through `browserEnv()` only); its styles; `npm test` runs it. 925 in the whole suite (921
pass, 4 skipped as before in this folder; on Node 20, 22 and 24, with and without Vercel's settings, and as if the clock
said six later times), the full build, and a clean build like Vercel's. In a browser with the site's real CSP (Claude's
scratch `intro/browser.mjs`, 67 checks): the cover right after `<body>` before the game's code, the canvas at device pixels
and on top of every frame, the full run and the short one, `agi:intro-done` once, a key skip (the game saw nothing; the
next press reaches it), Shift and Control passing, Enter swallowed, a phone's tap (no click reached the game), phones at
360, 390 and 412 px and sideways, at most 3 canvas pixels a CSS pixel, "reduce motion", a late page, no script at all (its
cover gone by itself); and AGI games' browser test again with it (276 checks: it waits for the intro before it clicks,
`introGone()`).

agi also)"; their pick: **"Checked runs only"**. Bragging rights only: **no prizes** (the page says so). **Built
2026-10-22 on the owner's PC.** Until the owner runs `supabase/arcade.sql` again, every board says it opens soon and both
games play exactly as before.

**What players see:**
- **agi1.app/games**, a **Leaderboards** section between the shelf and the ratings ("The best runs"): a box for each game
  with its boards to pick (TRENCHING SIMULATOR: today's daily market, then each challenge's This week and All time; Ride
  'Em, AGI!: Endless today, this week, all time, and today's daily mod), its top 20 (rank, the name its player chose or "A
  player", the numbers: "2:41 · 10.2x", "0.85x", "6,151 m · 119,189"), and "Your best here: #37 · …" for a browser that
  has played (its random id for the games, never made by the page); **Your name on the leaderboards (optional)** with
  Save (both games use it); "Checked, but not cheat-proof: a row can be taken off. Names are shown publicly, and a row
  never shows who you are." The fine print: "What a leaderboard keeps: …". The home page's safety note says it too, without
  the word "leaderboard" (`tests/page.test.js` keeps the removed Arena's words, that one among them, off `index.html`).
- **TRENCHING SIMULATOR:** see "TRENCHING SIMULATOR" → "GNGM, names, leaderboards, race rooms and more chains".
- **Ride 'Em, AGI!:** endless runs and the daily mod get a ticket as they start (levels never rank); when a run ends (and
  again after each revive, farther each time) its numbers go to our server, checked against what the game can do (its top
  speed, its score per metre, its revives, the daily mod of its day), and a ranked run shows "Ranked #N · …" at the top of
  the screen for a few seconds. Its hook is in `tools/games/import-rideemagi.mjs`'s PATCHES (`Ranked.start(cfg)`,
  `Ranked.result(r, st)`, from `src/games/rideemagi/ranked.js`) and the same lines in `game.js`.

**How it works:** `src/games/boards.js` (the boards, how runs rank, a row's words; shared by the page, the games and our
server), `server/scores.js` (tickets signed with `PASS_SECRET` and tied to a code of the browser's id; scores; boards),
`/api/wallet` (`GET ?board=<game>:<board>` shared by the CDN a minute; actions `game-ticket`, `game-score` up to 48 KB,
`game-score-mine`), `supabase/arcade.sql` (three tables, six functions: `arcade_take`, `arcade_board_cut`,
`arcade_score_put`, `arcade_board`, `arcade_score_mine`, `arcade_score_hide`), `src/games/leaderboard.js` (the page's
section). A browser's best only (one row a board), a run kept only if it beats the 100th; a day's and a week's rows
deleted after 35 days. Limits: 60 tickets and 30 scores a visitor a day; for the site 50,000 tickets, 20,000 scores and
2,000 replays a day (a replay is up to about a second of Vercel's CPU, and only a run that would make a board is
replayed); a burst limit of 12 a minute. **Taking a row off:** Supabase → Table Editor → `agi1_arcade_scores` → its id,
then in the SQL Editor `select arcade_score_hide(<id>, true);` (false shows it again).

**Tests:** `tests/arcade.test.js` (Ride 'Em, AGI!'s server checks, its hooks, the 14 SQL functions), `tests/page.test.js`
(the section, its module, its look), `tests/trench-game.test.js` (the rest: see TRENCHING SIMULATOR's).

**What players see at agi1.app/games/trenchingsimulator** (`trenchingsimulator.html`, `src/games/trenchingsimulator/`;
`vercel.json` rewrites the address):
- **The AGI GAMES intro first** (see "The AGI GAMES intro"), then the game, full screen in its own dark look (none of the

  so Back works the way people expect; during a run, Back goes from a coin's page to the board, and from the board opens

- **Home:** "AGI GAMES · BETA", **TRENCHING SIMULATOR**, "Trade made-up coins with play money on the terminals you know.
  Ape in early, sell the top, dodge the rugs.", **Play** and **Daily market · <today's challenge>**, the player's runs,
  wins, stars (of 27) and best multiple, **Race a friend** ("Multiplayer · coming soon" until 2026-10-22), How to play,

  (agi1.app/games#rate-trenchingsimulator) · All games.
- **Pick your terminal** ("Laid out the way you know them, with our own names. More are on the way."): the five, in the
  owner's order (BasedBott, GNGM, Pomp.fun, Axium, Phomo), each with its words, what it does

  other three "Coming soon" (a lock, can't be pressed).
- **Pick a mode:** the **Market** switch (Simulated, the default, or Live coins: real new coins, see "Live mode");
  **Daily market** (one challenge and one made-up market, the same for everyone on a UTC day, picked from
  seven of the challenges; its tries and its win kept for the day); **Challenges** (nine goals against the clock, up to
  3 stars each: 27 in all); **Free play** (no clock and no goal; start with 1, 5, 10 or 50 SOL, at 1×, 2× or 4× speed).
- **The challenges** (the owner's two and seven more), Easy to Legendary: **First blood** (1 SOL to 1.05 SOL in 5
  minutes), **Double up** (2x in 10 minutes), **Make $500** ($500 of profit in 10 minutes, from $1,000: the owner's),
  **Rug dodger** (trade 5 different coins and finish above your 2 SOL when its 10 minutes are up; a rug on a coin you hold
  ends it), **Speedrun** (1.5x in 3 minutes), **Catch a runner** (sell one coin for 3x what you put into it, 20 minutes),
  **Ride the migration** (hold a coin while it migrates, then sell it in profit, 20 minutes), **Whale mode** (100 SOL to
  150 SOL in 15 minutes: a big bag moves the chart) and **10x in 30** (1 SOL to 10 SOL in 30 minutes: the owner's). A win
  gets 3 stars in a third of its time or less, 2 in two thirds, else 1; Rug dodger by how far above its start it ends
  (1.5x: 3, 1.2x: 2, else 1).
- **A run's brief:** its goal, its time, its start, the terminal, and "SOL $… · live, frozen for this run": **SOL's real
  price**, read from DexScreener when a run is set up (at most every 5 minutes) and frozen for the whole run, so its
  dollars never move under the player (when DexScreener doesn't answer within 4 s: the price this browser saw last, up to
  30 days old, else a stand-in $150). The game's money is SOL underneath; the price only turns it into dollars on the
  screen (and Make $500's $1,000 into SOL).
- **The run:** a bar on top (Pause, AGI-1's 8-bit face with her words, the challenge and how far along it is, its clock,
  the player's worth and profit, free play's speed, sound, and **End** or **Cash out**, two taps) over the terminal. The
  market is already busy when the player arrives (10 minutes of made-up trading before), with a new coin every few
  seconds. Its pause sheet: Resume, Settings (slippage 1%, 5%, 10%, 20% or 50%, 20% to start; priority fast, turbo or
  ultra: 0.001, 0.005 or 0.01 SOL, landing in about 0.35–0.9 s, 0.18–0.45 s or 0.06–0.2 s; sound), How to play, End this
  run.
- **Trades as on the real thing:** a quote first (what you'd get, the price impact and the fees), then the order lands a
  moment later (its priority); it pays the terminal's 1% fee, the launchpad's own fee (1% on the bonding curve, 0.3% in
  the coin's pool after it migrates), the network's tiny fee and the priority fee, and it fails, costing only the network
  and priority fees, if the price moved past the player's slippage.
- **The market** (all made up, `engine.js`): coins launch on a bonding curve with pump.fun's own numbers (a billion
  tokens, 793.1 million of them for sale on the curve; sold out at about 85 SOL, the coin migrates to its own pool).
  Each coin's fate is decided at launch: most die (47%), some are rugged by their dev (18%) or pumped and dumped (18%),
  some chop for a while (11%), a few run (4.5%), and now and then one goes to the moon (1.5%); the hot theme's coins run
  more often, and copies of another coin's name mostly die or rug. Made-up traders move them: devs, bundles, snipers,
  insiders, 16 made-up callers and their followers and 28 smart wallets (whose habits a player can learn over runs: who
  holds, who dumps on their followers), whales and the crowd. Names come from 20 themes, made up and PG-13, never a real
  coin's ticker, a real person, a brand or a look-alike of $AGI. The same seed and the same orders make the same market
  (the daily market is one seed for everyone).
- **Pomp.fun** (the one terminal ready; reworked 2026-10-21 to look and lay out like today's launchpad board,
  pump.fun's 2026 look, measured on its site on 2026-10-20 without signing in, under our own name with a plain "T"
  mark): its own dark (a near-black page, soft green Buy buttons); a header with the search ("/" jumps to it) and the
  player's bag in SOL, the latest trade and launch flashing under it. **The board:** the king of the hill, its sorts (bump
  order, trending, new, about to graduate, graduated) and a grid of coin cards (picture, ticker, name, age, market cap and
  its change, the curve's progress, who made it, replies, tags). **A coin's page:** its header (ticker, name, age, `CA` and
  the first 6 characters of its address, socials, the dev's share, tags, market cap, 24h volume, holders, ATH), its chart
  (candles of 1 s, 15 s, 1 m or 5 m, the player's own buys and sells marked), Holders · Thread · Trades, and on the right
  the trade panel (Buy / Sell, the amount and its quick picks, the quote, the button) over its boxes (Stats / Audit over 5
  minutes, an hour or since launch, its bonding curve, the king of the hill's race, its pool, About); the player's bag on
  the left of a wide screen (1180 px and up). **On a phone** (under 720 px): one column, a bar at the bottom (Board ·
  Search · Bag · Settings), and on a coin's page one green **Trade $TICKER** button that opens the trade panel as a sheet;
  the right column's boxes under an Info tab. Every grey its words use passes WCAG AA (its labels' grey is #8a8a93, a
  little lighter than the reference's: see the decisions log).
- **AGI-1** in the corner of the bar: her 8-bit face (the AGI GAMES intro's own frames, from her 2D art) with a mark for
  her mood and her words in a bubble (on a computer beside her face, in the bar's goal cell; on a phone under it), for as
  long as they take to read. 88 pre-written lines for 33 moments (a first buy, a rug, a migration, a 2x, the last
  minute…), lowercase, PG-13, never a tip; now and then she says it's play money. No AI, nothing sent.
- **Its sounds:** short blips made in the browser (no files), quiet, only after the player's first tap or key; the sound
  button mutes them (remembered).
- **The results:** its title ("Challenge complete", "Time's up", "Rugged out", "Busted", "Cashed out" or "Run ended"),
  its stars, its multiple, a line, its worth over the run as a line, its numbers (profit, peak, time, orders, coins
  traded, wins and losses, best and worst trade, fees paid, SOL's frozen price), AGI-1's line, **Play again**, **Share on
  X** (X's own post box with a ready-made post that always says it's play money, "(play money, made-up coins)" or, for a
  live run that traded a real coin, "(play money on live coins)", never "buy"; the player posts it, never us), **Save
  card** (a 1200 × 630 picture of the result), Choose another or Pick a mode, Home, and Rate it · All games.
- **Kept in this browser only** (`trench_v1` and `trench_sol` in localStorage): the player's settings, each challenge's
  best, each day's daily market, a few totals, SOL's last price. Nothing about the player is sent anywhere: only that a
  run started (below), and in Live mode which chain and which coins to keep live.

**How it works** (`src/games/trenchingsimulator/`, all in the browser; its pure parts read in Node by the tests):
- `page.js` (its entry: the intro first, then `shell.js`), `shell.js` (every screen, the run's bar, the pause and settings
  sheets, the results and the share card), `terminals.js` (the five, their words and colors, `SAFETY_NOTE`, which are
  ready), `challenges.js` (the nine, the daily market, stars), `run.js` (one run: its clock, orders, events, how it
  ends), `engine.js` (the made-up market: no clock of its own and no `Math.random`: a seed and the player's orders make
  it), `curve.js` (the bonding curve and the pool), `fates.js` (what becomes of each coin), `names.js` (coins, callers,
  chatter), `rng.js` (its seeded dice), `boards/board.js` (Pomp.fun), `chart.js`, `results.js`, `share.js`, `save.js`,
  `solprice.js` (SOL's price), `lines.js` and `agi.js` (AGI-1), `sound.js`, `format.js`, `ui.js`, `site.js` (its plays),
  `trench.css` (its look: the shell's `ts-` classes and Pomp.fun's `tsb-` ones), `keyart.webp`; and Live mode's
  `live-chains.js`, `live-feed.js` and `live-market.js` (below).
- Everything is made with `createElement` and set as text; styles only through classes and the CSS object model (the
  site's CSP). About 184 KB of code (70 KB compressed) and 53 KB of styles; no pictures (a made-up coin's picture is its
  emoji on a tile in its theme's color), its font the site's own Geist. Besides its own files, its only requests: SOL's
  price from DexScreener (already in the CSP), its plays to our `/api/wallet`, and in Live mode our relay.
- **A new terminal:** its own board in `boards/` (like `boards/board.js`'s `mountBoard()`), picked in `shell.js` for its
  terminal, and `ready: true` in `terminals.js`; the market, the run and the challenges are the same for every terminal.

3. **Live mode:** on since 2026-10-21 (its relay's steps below, done that day, then one small push opened it).

**Cost:** nothing new for the game: its plays are small reports to `/api/wallet` (about one a minute a player), a review
with words about $0.0003 (Gemini's look, from the site's prepaid credits, inside AGI games' 2,000 a day), SOL's price one
free DexScreener request from the player's own browser (at most every 5 minutes), and its code and styles, about 90 KB
compressed, from Vercel's CDN (its key art, 86 KB, on agi1.app/games). Live mode's relay: see its own "Cost".

**Troubleshooting:**

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The brief says "SOL $150 · a stand-in price" | DexScreener didn't answer and this browser kept no price | Nothing to fix: the run works in SOL, and the price only turns it into dollars. The next run asks again |
| agi1.app/games: "Ratings and reviews open soon", no numbers | `supabase/arcade.sql` isn't run in this Supabase project | AGI games' owner step 1 (the same for both games) |
| "Played" doesn't go up right after a run | By design: the numbers are shared a minute, and a run after the first is told within a minute (or when the page is hidden) | Nothing to fix |
| A terminal says "Coming soon" | Only Pomp.fun is built (2026-10-21) | Ask Claude for the next one |
| Live coins says "Soon" and can't be picked | A page from before Live mode opened (2026-10-21), or `LIVE_OPEN` set back to false | Reload the page (Ctrl+F5); else see "Live mode", step 9 |
| The daily market changed | A new UTC day (00:00 UTC is 8:00 the owner's time): everyone gets a new one | Nothing to fix |
| Progress gone (stars, bests) | It's kept in that browser only: a private window, cleared site data or another browser starts fresh | Nothing to fix (by design: nothing about players is kept on our side) |

### Live mode (2026-10-20 and 21)

**The owner's** (2026-10-20 and 21): real new coins in the game, with the names and pictures their makers gave them,
traded with play money only. While Claude researched where they'd come from, the owner: "there would be no restrictions
on the names and the coins the names and picturres are as is, the streams is only on clank and clank allows everything on
the stream", then "now continue". So: names, tickers and pictures as they are (no word filter, no picture check, no 18+
tap: the owner's call; Claude had offered an 18+ tap), and AGI-1's own lines never name a real coin. **Simulated stays
the default:** Live mode is a switch on the modes screen. Nothing is ever bought, sold or signed for real, and nothing a
player does leaves the page but which chain and which coins to keep live.

Two parts: **the game** (on the site since the owner's push of 2026-10-21) and **the relay** (`tools/trench-relay/`),
which runs on the owner's Hetzner server beside her live show, behind Caddy at **wss://live.agi1.app**: one connection
to each source, passed on to every player. **Running since 2026-10-21** (the owner's steps 1 to 8 below, `relay.sh
check` all ok), and **Live mode open on the site** since the push after it (step 9). If the relay ever stops, Live
mode says "The live feed isn't reachable right now" and plays simulated coins (it never breaks the game).

**"Coming soon" on the site (2026-10-21, until it opened that day).** The owner, the same day: "can you just finish the
first terminal first so i can try it. ill add other terminals later since the game is still on beta and put it on the
site also", then "wait why im using heztner? im just creating a game right". Claude's answer: the server is only for
Live mode's real coins, and the game needs none. The owner's choices: "Just the game for now (Recommended)" (the Helius
and server walkthroughs wait) and "Coming soon" (Recommended): "The Live coins button says Soon and can't be picked,
like the other four terminals. I switch it on when the server's ready (one small push)".
- **What players see while it's closed:** the Live coins chip dashed, its words muted, with a small "Soon" tag; it
  can't be picked (Tab passes it by; screen readers hear "Live coins, coming soon"); under the switch: "Live coins are
  coming soon: real new coins as they launch, with the names and pictures their makers gave them, traded with play money
  only. Until then, every coin here is made up."; How to play: "Live mode is coming soon: real new coins as they launch,
  on Solana, Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain or Base, with the names and pictures their makers gave them, still traded with
  play money only."; a Live choice a browser kept from a try is set back to Simulated; no WebSocket is opened, and
  nothing asks live.agi1.app.
- **How:** `LIVE_OPEN` in `live-chains.js` (false then, **true since 2026-10-21**), and `liveOpen(location)`: open when
  `LIVE_OPEN` is true, or on this computer with a relay of its own (`?relay=`, localhost only), so the tests can use it.
  Its words are `LIVE_SOON` and `LIVE_SOON_HOW` there, its look `.ts-chip:disabled` and `.ts-chip-soon` in `trench.css`.
- **Opened** (2026-10-21): `relay.sh check` all ok, then Claude set `LIVE_OPEN = true` and `tests/trench-live.test.js`'s
  check of it (the tests fail if only one of them changes), with agi1.app/games's words for the game made true for it
  (see "Open questions"), saved them here, and the owner pushed (step 9). **To close it again** (if the relay has to
  stay off for long): `LIVE_OPEN = false` and that check, one small push; the words and the look above come back.

**What players see once it's open:**
- **The modes screen:** "Market: Simulated · Live coins"; with Live coins picked, the chain (**Solana**, pump.fun's, first;
  **Robinhood Chain**, clank.trade's and, since 2026-10-21, other launchpads' listed ones; **BNB Chain**; **Base**; and
  since 2026-10-22 GMGN's other chains, **Ethereum**, **Monad**, **HyperEVM**, **Arbitrum** and **Tron**, their listed
  coins: the owner asked for GMGN's chains, so "never Ethereum" ended), a dot and words for how the feed is doing ("Live: every new pump.fun coin as it launches on Solana, traded
  with play money." / "Connecting to the live feed…" / "The live feed isn't reachable right now: a run would use
  simulated coins until it's back." / "Solana is quiet: no new coins for a while. Simulated coins fill in until real
  ones arrive.", only with fewer than 8 real coins live: a quiet chain with more plays them alone and says Live, since
  2026-10-21), and the live note: "Live mode shows real new
  coins, with the names and pictures their makers gave them. You trade them with play money: nothing is bought or sold
  for real, and nothing leaves this page. Not financial advice."
- **The daily market stays simulated** (the same coins for everyone that day), and so does Rug dodger, the challenge that
  ends on a rug: a real coin is never called a rug here. The other challenges and free play can be live.
- **A live run** runs on the real clock (one speed; its menu doesn't pause it: the real market never waits), its results
  say Live, its stars and bests are kept apart from the simulated ones, and its post for X says "(play money on live
  coins)" when it traded a real coin. Its live line, read out by screen readers when it changes: "Live · Solana · real
  coins from pump.fun · play money only", or the fallback's words. Under 1024 px it sits above the bar, so AGI-1's words
  never cover it.
- **Real coins on Pomp.fun:** their real name, ticker and picture (through our relay, made small), "from pump.fun" or
  "from clank.trade" on a card (or the chain, "on Robinhood Chain", for a coin listed on DexScreener), "Real coin · play
  money" on its page, only the first 6 characters of its address, "—" for what isn't known (never made-up holders, a
  thread, a dev, a rug or a caller). **No link or button anywhere: never a way to buy a real coin.** While the feed is
  down, or the chain is quiet with fewer than 8 real coins live (`REAL_ENOUGH` and `playState()` in `live-chains.js`),
  made-up stand-ins fill in, tagged "Simulated"; a quiet chain with 8 or more plays its real coins alone (the owner,
  2026-10-21: "on the live mode on robinhood chain use real coins not fake ones": Robinhood Chain is often quiet).
- **Trades:** quoted and filled against the coin's live curve (pump.fun's own constant product and its 1% fee; a pool's
  0.3% after it graduates); the player's own tokens move the curve in their own view, and a sell comes back along it.
  The buttons say "· play money".
- **Money per terminal** (the owner's): Pomp.fun the chain's own coin since 2026-10-21 (the owner: "why im using sol
  on robinhood chain when it uses ethereum", then "Each chain's money (Recommended)"; SOL on every chain before): ETH on
  Robinhood Chain and Base, BNB on BNB Chain, SOL on Solana, in every amount it shows or takes (the balance, quick buys
  as round amounts, fees, profits, the results and the post, priority fees). A challenge's SOL start and Free play's
  1, 5, 10 or 50 SOL become a round amount of the coin (two significant figures: at SOL $150 and ETH $3,000, 0.05 ETH),
  and the run starts with that in SOL: the game counts in SOL underneath (`format.js`: `unitOf()`, `money()`;
  `challenges.js`: `startSolFor()`, `freeStartSol()`; `live-chains.js`: `liveMoney()`). The coin's price is the relay's
  (DexScreener), frozen for the run like SOL's ("ETH $2.61K · SOL $105.73 … frozen for this run"); SOL until it's in.
  The daily market and Rug dodger stay simulated, in SOL. GNGM the chain's own coin, BasedBott ETH,
  Phomo dollars, Axium SOL (none built yet).
- **AGI-1** has 25 lines of her own for Live mode, none with a ticker: a real coin's "rug" or "dev sell" is never
  something she says.

**How it works, in the game** (`src/games/trenchingsimulator/`):
- `live-chains.js`: the chains, each terminal's money, the words, the relay's address (`wss://live.agi1.app/ws`, fixed;
  `?relay=` works only when the page itself is on localhost, and only for a relay on localhost: never from a link on the
  site), whether Live mode can be picked (`LIVE_OPEN` and `liveOpen()`, above), and every message from the relay checked
  before anything sees it (names made safe to show as text, numbers checked, addresses matched against their shape; no
  word filter: the owner's call).
- `live-feed.js`: one WebSocket for the picked chain, only while Live mode is on; its states: connecting, live, down,
  full; it reconnects by itself (2 s, 4 s … 30 s, a little random) and asks the relay to keep the coins a player has open
  or holds live (`watch`, 8 at most). It sends nothing else.
- `live-market.js`: the engine's market with the feed's coins in it, and which coins the lists show (live, or quiet with
  8 or more real coins live: the real ones, the stand-ins paused; quiet with fewer: both; down: the stand-ins, running).

**How it works, the relay** (`tools/trench-relay/`, on the owner's server):
- **Its sources, one connection each:** Solana: **PumpPortal**'s free WebSocket (new coins and migrations; one
  connection, as PumpPortal asks; the owner's OK, 2026-10-21: "oh im friends with them they its okay"), **PumpDev**'s as
  its backup (it takes over after 90 s without a new coin, and hands back when PumpPortal sends again;
  `PUMPPORTAL_WS_URL=off` = PumpDev alone from the start), each coin's curve live from **Helius** (a subscription to its
  bonding curve's account, read once more after every reconnect: the newest 150 coins plus up to 150 that players have
  open or hold, at most 950, under Helius's 1,000 a connection), and after its curve sells out, its pool from
  DexScreener. Robinhood Chain: **clank.trade's own coin list** (the API its site uses, the same as the site's risk
  check), its newest every 12 s, and since 2026-10-21 (the owner's "Add DexScreener coins") coins from its other
  launchpads (pools.trade, Pons, Long…) once their makers list them on DexScreener, as on BNB Chain and Base;
  clank.trade stays its own source (the chain's state is clank.trade's, and a coin both have is clank.trade's). BNB
  Chain and Base: **DexScreener's newest token profiles** (coins whose makers listed them there: not every launch),
  their markets every 20 s. SOL, ETH and BNB in dollars every minute. Every DexScreener request is counted (at most 240
  a minute, under its free limits).
- **Pictures through our own server** (`/p/<hash>.webp`): a coin's metadata and picture read once, from public IPFS
  gateways (Filebase, Pinata's public one, then ipfs.io) or, for any other address, with the safe request (https on port
  443 only, public addresses only, looked up first, never a redirect); only real PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or AVIF by their
  first bytes (never SVG), 8 MB and 40 million pixels at most; made a 128 px WebP square with sharp; kept in memory
  (64 MB). Never pump.fun's own host, and a browser never asks a coin's own host for anything.
- **Passing it on** (`lib/hub.mjs`): a new coin at once; market changes in one small batch every half second (each
  coin's newest only); pictures as they're ready. A slow viewer never slows the others (past 512 KB waiting it misses
  batches and gets a fresh copy once it catches up; past 4 MB it's dropped). A ping every 25 s (no answer: dropped).
- **Its door:** only the site's own pages (Origin `https://agi1.app` or `https://www.agi1.app`); 2,000 viewers at once
  (one more is let in only to hear "busy", then closed); 10 from one address; a browser's message at most 2 KB and about
  two a second (anything else is ignored; too much closes it); 900 pictures a minute per address.
- **`https://live.agi1.app/health`:** JSON (each chain's state and coins, viewers, sources, pictures, prices, problems),
  never a key or a viewer.
- **The Helius key** lives only in `/opt/agi1-trench/trench.env` on the server (mode 600): never in the code, the image,
  an answer, a browser or a log line (every line is scrubbed of it and of any `api-key=`).
- **Its image:** `node:22-bookworm-slim`, `npm ci --omit=dev` (its own `package.json` and lock: ws 8.21.0 and sharp
  0.35.5, exact versions, never the site's), run as the image's own user (never root), its port only on Docker's own
  network; at most 3/4 of a core and 512 MB (`--cpus 0.75 --memory 512m`), so her live show on the same 2-core CX23
  always has room; sharp one picture at a time.
- **Caddy** in front (`caddy:2.10`, the official image): automatic HTTPS for live.agi1.app (Let's Encrypt, renewed by
  itself), ports 80 and 443 (and 443/udp), HSTS, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, no access log (a viewer's
  address is never written down). Both start again by themselves after a reboot (`--restart unless-stopped`).
- **What the site needs:** only its CSP changes (`vercel.json`, in the push): `img-src` gains `https://live.agi1.app` (the
  coins' pictures) and `connect-src` gains `wss://live.agi1.app` (the feed). No setting in Vercel, no SQL, no new
  function. `ws` is a dev dependency only (the tests run the relay against stand-in services); the site's pages never
  load it.

**Its settings** (`/opt/agi1-trench/trench.env` on the server, from `tools/trench-relay/trench.env.example`; none of them
go to Vercel). After changing one: `sh /opt/agi1-live/site/tools/trench-relay/relay.sh start`.

| Name | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `HELIUS_API_KEY` | (empty) | **Secret.** The Helius API key (or Helius's whole address with `api-key=` in it). Empty: Solana stays off ("Solana isn't on the live feed right now"); the other chains work |
| `TRENCH_ORIGINS` | `https://agi1.app,https://www.agi1.app` | The pages that may connect |
| `TRENCH_TRUST_PROXY` | `1` | Caddy says who's connecting (the relay's own port is never open) |
| `TRENCH_MAX_CLIENTS` | 2000 | Viewers at once |
| `TRENCH_MAX_PER_IP` | 10 | Viewers from one address |
| `TRENCH_CHAINS` | `solana,robinhood,bnb,base,ethereum,monad,hyperevm,arbitrum,tron` | Its chains (the last five since 2026-10-22: a settings file from before names only the first four, so add them) |
| `TRENCH_ROOMS` | (on) | `off`: no race rooms (2026-10-22) |
| `TRENCH_ROOM_SEATS` · `TRENCH_ROOMS_MAX` · `TRENCH_ROOM_PLAYERS` · `TRENCH_ROOMS_PER_IP` | 8 · 200 · 1600 · 8 | Race rooms' caps: seats a room, rooms, racers at once, racers from one address |
| `TRENCH_SOLANA_TRACK` | 150 | The newest pump.fun curves followed live |
| `TRENCH_WATCH_MAX` | 150 | Coins players have open or hold, followed on top (both together at most 950) |
| `TRENCH_PIC_CACHE_MB` | 64 | Pictures kept in memory |
| `TRENCH_LOG` | `info` | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error` |
| `PUMPPORTAL_WS_URL` | PumpPortal's | `off`: PumpDev alone, from the start (not needed: the owner's OK for PumpPortal, 2026-10-21) |
| `PUMPDEV_WS_URL` | PumpDev's | `off`: no backup |

**Cost:** **$0 a month as built.** Helius's free plan (1M credits a month; following 150 to 300 curves is about 130,000
to 780,000 credits a month, from the research's measures: Helius bills WebSocket data since May 2026), PumpPortal's and
PumpDev's free new-coin feeds, DexScreener's free API, clank.trade's API, the public IPFS gateways, Caddy and Let's
Encrypt (free), and the CX23 the owner already pays for (20 TB of traffic a month included; a player gets a few KB a
second at most). If Helius's dashboard shows the month's credits running low: `TRENCH_SOLANA_TRACK=100` and
`TRENCH_WATCH_MAX=100`, then `relay.sh start`. Helius's paid plan ($49 a month) only if the owner wants more (never
needed to run). **Never** PumpPortal's paid trade streams (keyed, billed per trade), never any paid service.

**The owner's steps** (one at a time; **all done 2026-10-21**, the day of the owner's "Just the game for now": the
owner asked to go on that afternoon, and Claude walked them through it). Kept for a new server or a new key. Secrets go
only where these steps say: never in chat, git, a screenshot or a file anyone else can read.
1. **PumpPortal's OK: done** (2026-10-21, the owner: "oh im friends with them they its okay"): its feed is on from the
   start, with PumpDev as its backup; nothing to send. (Not legal advice: PumpPortal's terms give a "single, personal,
   limited license" and say its data "may not [be] … publish[ed], distribute[d]" unless they authorize it; a short yes
   from them in writing is good to keep. The other sources: DexScreener's terms allow commercial use but not "third
   parties" or a competing product; Helius's terms bar sublicensing or redistributing its products (prices worked out
   from its data aren't addressed); clank.trade's API is the one the site's risk check already reads. Worth a look
   before promoting Live mode widely: see "Open questions".)
2. **A Helius key (free):** dashboard.helius.dev → sign in (the free plan is enough) → **API Keys** → copy the key (a long
   code with dashes). Keep it in your clipboard for step 6, or in a password manager; never in chat or a screenshot.
3. **The site pushed** (the game's push carries the relay's files and the CSP). Live mode still says "Coming soon" on
   the site until step 9: nothing breaks meanwhile.
4. **The DNS record, live.agi1.app → the server:** Namecheap → your **hosting** account → **cPanel** → **Zone Editor** →
   agi1.app → **Manage** → **+ Add Record**: Type **A**, Name `live` (cPanel may show it as `live.agi1.app.`), Address
   **the server's IPv4** (Hetzner console → the server `agi1-live` → its IPv4: the address you `ssh` to), TTL as it
   suggests → **Save**. A few minutes later (at most an hour), from PowerShell on the PC:
   ```
   Resolve-DnsName live.agi1.app -Type A
   ```
   It shows the server's IPv4. (If the Namecheap account is still suspended (it was on 2026-10-03: see "agi1.app's DNS"
   in "Open questions"), this step waits for it, and the game plays simulated coins meanwhile.)
5. **Ports 80 and 443 open:** Hetzner console → **Firewalls**: if a firewall is attached to `agi1-live`, add inbound
   rules **TCP 80**, **TCP 443** and **UDP 443** (any IPv4 and IPv6); with none attached (Hetzner's default), nothing to
   do. Then on the server (`ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 root@<the server's IP>`), check nothing else uses them (her live
   show publishes no ports), one line at a time:
   ```
   ss -ltnp | grep -E ':(80|443) ' || echo "80 and 443 are free"
   ufw status
   ```
   If `ufw status` says `Status: active`:
   ```
   ufw allow 80/tcp && ufw allow 443/tcp && ufw allow 443/udp
   ```
6. **On the server, the relay's files and its settings file** (each line pasted on its own, in the server's window,
   `root@agi1-live`). The newest code (safe while her live show runs: it runs from its own image), then the settings file:
   ```
   cd /opt/agi1-live/site && git pull --ff-only
   mkdir -p /opt/agi1-trench && cp /opt/agi1-live/site/tools/trench-relay/trench.env.example /opt/agi1-trench/trench.env && chmod 600 /opt/agi1-trench/trench.env
   ```
   The Helius key: paste this line first, **then** copy the key in Helius's dashboard (so the clipboard holds the key,
   not the line), paste it once when it asks and press Enter. It stays hidden on screen and out of the shell's history.
   The line drops what a paste can add around a key (a terminal's paste markers, spaces, a line break, invisible
   characters; a whole Helius address is cut down to its `api-key=`) and saves it only if what's left looks like a key:
   "saved: N characters", or "NOT saved" with the characters that don't belong (never the key itself):
   ```
   read -rs -p 'Helius API key (hidden): ' K; echo; V=$(printf %s "$K" | sed 's/\x1b\[20[01]~//g; s/.*api-key=//; s/&.*//' | LC_ALL=C tr -d '[:space:]\200-\377'); unset K; if printf %s "$V" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9-]{16,100}$'; then sed -i "s|^HELIUS_API_KEY=.*|HELIUS_API_KEY=$V|" /opt/agi1-trench/trench.env && echo "saved: ${#V} characters"; else echo "NOT saved: ${#V} characters, these don't belong in a key:"; printf %s "$V" | LC_ALL=C tr -d 'A-Za-z0-9-' | od -An -c; fi; unset V
   ```
   (2026-10-21: the first try, with a plainer line, saved something that wasn't the key: `relay.sh check` said "NO
   HELIUS_API_KEY is neither a Helius key nor a Helius address". This line, then `relay.sh start`, fixed it.)
7. **Build it and start it:**
   ```
   cd /opt/agi1-live/site && sh tools/trench-relay/relay.sh update
   ```
   The first time takes a few minutes (Node's and Caddy's images and the relay's two packages). It ends with "started: the
   relay (agi1-trench) and Caddy (agi1-trench-caddy) for https://live.agi1.app".
8. **Check it**, a minute later (Caddy gets its certificate once the DNS record is there):
   ```
   sh tools/trench-relay/relay.sh check
   ```
   Every line should start with `ok`: the settings file (600), "HELIUS_API_KEY is set (never shown)", both containers
   running, "relay up … · solana live (… coins, … live) · robinhood live …", "Solana: PumpPortal connected · PumpDev
   idle · Helius connected, … curves live", the pictures and SOL's price, and "https://live.agi1.app/health answers (the
   certificate works)". BNB Chain and Base are often "quiet" (only coins whose makers listed them on DexScreener). In a
   browser, **https://live.agi1.app/health** shows JSON starting `{"ok":true,"service":"agi1-trench-relay"`.
9. **Open it** (one small push): tell Claude `relay.sh check` passes. Claude sets `LIVE_OPEN = true` in
   `src/games/trenchingsimulator/live-chains.js` and `tests/trench-live.test.js`'s checks of it, and saves them here;
   then `git push` on the PC, in this folder. The Live coins chip loses its "Soon", and the "coming soon" words go.
   (Done 2026-10-21, with agi1.app/games's words for the game made true for Live mode: see "Open questions".)
10. **Try it:** agi1.app/games/trenchingsimulator → Play → Pomp.fun → **Market: Live coins** → **Solana** (its dot
    green: "Live: every new pump.fun coin as it launches on Solana, traded with play money.") → Free play → Start: the
    line at the top says "Live · Solana · real coins from pump.fun · play money only", with real coins and their
    pictures. Try a phone too.

**Later:** after a push that touches `tools/trench-relay/`: `cd /opt/agi1-live/site && sh tools/trench-relay/relay.sh
update` (the game's own changes go live with Vercel, as always). `relay.sh stop` (both off: the game says the live feed
isn't reachable and plays simulated coins), `relay.sh start`, `relay.sh status`, `relay.sh logs` (the relay's last 100
lines; `logs 300`, `logs caddy`).

**Troubleshooting** (`sh tools/trench-relay/relay.sh check` and `relay.sh logs` on the server):

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The game: Live coins says "Soon" and can't be picked | A page from before Live mode opened (2026-10-21), or `LIVE_OPEN` set back to false | Reload the page (Ctrl+F5); else step 9 |
| The game: "The live feed isn't reachable right now…" | The relay isn't running, live.agi1.app doesn't point at the server yet, or the site isn't pushed (the browser's console: "Refused to connect … violates the Content Security Policy") | `relay.sh check`; https://live.agi1.app/health in a browser; step 3 |
| `check`: `NO https://live.agi1.app/health doesn't answer yet` | The DNS record (step 4), ports 80 and 443 (step 5), or Caddy's certificate | `getent ahostsv4 live.agi1.app` on the server must show its own IPv4; `relay.sh logs caddy`: "NXDOMAIN" = the record isn't there yet, "timeout during connect" = a firewall (step 5). Caddy tries again by itself |
| `relay.sh start`: "port is already allocated" / "address already in use" | Something else listens on 80 or 443 | `ss -ltnp` shows what; stop it, then `relay.sh start` |
| `check`: `NO HELIUS_API_KEY is empty: Solana stays off` | Step 6's key line wasn't run (or printed 0) | Step 6's key line again, then `relay.sh start` |
| `check`: `NO HELIUS_API_KEY is neither a Helius key nor a Helius address` | What was saved isn't the key: the clipboard held something else, or the paste added characters (2026-10-21, the first try) | Step 6's key line (it cleans and checks what's pasted, never shows it), then `relay.sh start` |
| The game: "Solana isn't on the live feed right now"; `check`: "Helius NOT connected" | Helius refused the key (`relay.sh logs`: "Helius: can't connect (… 401 …)"), or Helius is down | A new key (step 2, step 6's key line), `relay.sh start`; a Helius outage passes by itself |
| The game: "Solana is quiet…" for a long time | No new-coin feed: `check` shows "PumpPortal NOT connected" and PumpDev not running | It reconnects by itself (1 s … a minute), and PumpDev takes over after 90 s; if both stay down, `relay.sh logs` says why |
| "Robinhood Chain isn't on the live feed right now" | clank.trade's API didn't answer (`logs`: "clank.trade (newest): …") | Passes by itself; the site's risk check would say the same |
| BNB Chain or Base "quiet" most of the time | By design: only coins whose makers listed them on DexScreener, not every launch | Nothing to fix |
| Some coins show a plain coin (🪙) instead of their picture | An IPFS gateway was slow or didn't have it (tried again after 15 s and 60 s); `check`: "pictures … not shown" | Nothing to fix (a picture over 8 MB, or not a real picture, is never shown) |
| "The live feed is full right now" | `TRENCH_MAX_CLIENTS` (2,000) viewers at once | Raise it in trench.env (mind the CX23), `relay.sh start` |
| Helius's dashboard: the month's credits nearly used | Following many curves all month | `TRENCH_SOLANA_TRACK=100` and `TRENCH_WATCH_MAX=100` in trench.env, `relay.sh start` |
| Her live show stutters while the relay runs | Both on the CX23's 2 cores (the relay at most 3/4 of one) | Fewer curves (as above), or `relay.sh stop` during a show and `start` after |
| The key was shown somewhere by mistake | — | Helius dashboard → make a new key, delete the old one; step 6's key line, `relay.sh start` |

  characters, "play money" beside them, no link anywhere. No "Sandwich shield"/MEV switch (the game's sandwich bots are
  off: a switch that does nothing would be a lie).

**The player's optional name** (`src/games/player-name.js`, both games' `agi_player_name` in localStorage): on a run's
brief, in the settings, in GNGM's settings and on agi1.app/games; 1 to 24 characters, never a link, an address, an email,
a long number, or a name that passes for AGI-1, her team or a moderator. Our server checks it again (`reviewName`) before
a leaderboard shows it ("A player" when it's refused or empty). It goes on cards ("by <name>"), ranked runs and race
rooms (16 characters there).

**Leaderboards: checked runs** (the page: "AGI games" → "Leaderboards"): a daily market or a challenge, simulated, in SOL,
gets a ticket from our server (`/api/wallet` `game-ticket`: its seed picked there, SOL's price frozen), and at its end its
orders go back (`game-score`, at most 1,000 orders, 48 KB): our server plays the run again with the game's own code
(`verify.js`) and ranks it only if it comes out the same (`server/scores.js`). A win ranks by its time, then its
multiple; the daily market's other runs after every win, by their multiple; a run its player ends never ranks. Free play,
Live mode and races never rank. The results say "Ranked #N · …" or why not ("Free play isn't ranked…", "This run
couldn't be checked, so it isn't ranked.", "Leaderboards open soon."…). `run.js`'s clock steps exactly like the check
(0.1 s steps), so any frame rate gives the same run. A run played in Safari or Firefox may not check (their maths can
differ in the last digit): it just isn't ranked.

**Race rooms** (`race.js`; the relay's `tools/trench-relay/lib/rooms.mjs` at wss://live.agi1.app/room, the Live feed's
host, so no CSP change):
- **Race a friend** on the home screen: join with a code, or make a room for one of the nine challenges. The room's
  screen: its invite link (agi1.app/games/trenchingsimulator#room=<6 characters>: a fragment, so never in a server log;
  the page takes it out of the address) with Copy link, the players (ready, host), the host's Start (and rematch) and
  Remove, Leave. Leaving its screens leaves the room.
- Everyone gets the same seed (`race-<code>-<n>`), SOL price (the relay's, else $150) and start (a 5 s countdown on the
  relay's clock), and plays it in their own browser, simulated, on a clock that never stops: the standings (the top three
  and you) under the HUD, the room's standings on the results with "Back to the room". Each browser says how it's doing
  about once a second; the standings come every 2 s (a win first by its time, then multiples, busted last).
  Self-reported, just for fun: never ranked, counted as a play like any run.
- No wallet, no sign-in, nothing kept: rooms live in the relay's memory (a restart ends them; each run goes on). Caps: 8
  a room, 200 rooms, 1,600 racers, 8 from one address, 3 new rooms an address in 10 minutes, 10 wrong codes a minute,
  1 KB a message, about 2 a second; a lobby closes after 15 minutes without a race, an empty room after a minute, an
  ended one after 5; a dropped connection gets its seat back within a minute. Names: 16 characters, never posing, a link,
  an address or a crude word ("Trader 3" instead). Settings: `TRENCH_ROOMS=off` closes them; `TRENCH_ROOM_SEATS`,
  `TRENCH_ROOMS_MAX`, `TRENCH_ROOM_PLAYERS`, `TRENCH_ROOMS_PER_IP`. `/health` counts rooms, racers and races.
- Until the relay is updated, the game says "Race rooms aren't open right now. You can still play on your own."

**GMGN's other chains in Live mode** (the owner asked whether they need a key like Helius: **no**): Ethereum (ETH), Monad
(MON), HyperEVM (HYPE), Arbitrum (ETH) and Tron (TRX), their coins as listed on DexScreener (like BNB Chain and Base: not
every launch, so often quiet, with stand-ins filling in), each in its own money for Pomp.fun and GNGM. Tron's addresses

relay's settings file must name the new ones (`TRENCH_CHAINS`, as `trench.env.example` now does).
