## Security & cost rules

### Lessons from the old site

| What went wrong on the old site | Rule for the new site |
|---|---|
| The browser told the database how many votes to add (`add_clicks` with any amount and any round), so a console one-liner could add a billion votes | Votes go through `/api/vote`. The server picks the round from its own clock and caps the amount |
| Every click was pushed to every open browser, so a bot could burn through Supabase's 2M realtime messages/month | Send board updates at most every ~2 s and only when something changed, or have browsers poll a cheap read |
| Each browser decided the champion itself, using its own clock | The server decides and stores champions (this also feeds the Phase 4 Hall of Fame) |
| The chat server was open to anyone, with no human check or limits. The browser sent its own history, so scripts could send huge or fake histories | Turnstile, rate limits, server-side size caps and a global daily cap (below) |
| 56 MB `girl.glb` (one texture is 8192×8192) downloaded by every visitor; about 1,500 visitors use up Vercel's free 100 GB/month | Optimize models to ≤ 5 MB each, and load a model only when it's shown |
| Prices were supposed to refresh every 30 s, but the timer was never started | Refresh on a timer, and pause while the tab is hidden |
| The chat server (Render free tier) sleeps, so the first reply could take ~1 minute | Chat runs on Vercel Functions, which don't sleep |

### Chat (`/api/chat`) (built, see "AGI-1's chat" above)
- The Gemini key lives only in Vercel env vars. The browser talks to `/api/chat`, never to Google.
- 18+ confirmation, Turnstile + 2-hour chat pass, size caps, per-visitor and site-wide limits in Supabase, signed history,
  safety filters on, thinking minimal, 300-token reply cap, address/link cleanup. Each of these is covered by `tests/chat.test.js`.
- Her language (2026-09-29): `lang` is only ever one of the 16 codes (anything else is English) and only picks a line of her
  prompt; her rules (PG-13, no advice, the safety filters, the reply cleanup) are the same in every language. Soulmate notes
  stay plain English, so the note filter can read them.
- Optional outer fence: Vercel's one free rate-limit rule on `/api/*` (120 requests a minute per IP). Firewall rules belong to
  one project: the owner set it up on `agi-new-website` (2026-09-24). For this one: Vercel → agi-ecosystem → **Firewall** →
  **Configure** → **+ New Rule** → name "API speed limit" → If **Request Path** **starts with** `/api/` → Then **Rate Limit**
  → Fixed Window, **60 s**, **120 requests**, key **IP** → action **Default (429)** → Save Rule → **Review Changes** →
  **Publish**. (These steps were in the Arena's section, which left on 2026-09-28.) Since her Telegram bot (2026-09-29), add
  a second condition to that rule: **Request Path** **does not equal** `/api/telegram`. Telegram delivers every chat's
  messages from a few of its own addresses, so the rule would count all of Telegram as one visitor; the webhook checks its
  own secret and has its own per-chat speed bump.
- **Money hard stop:** Gemini prepaid credits (top up small amounts, auto-reload OFF) plus a monthly spend cap in AI Studio.

### Votes and coins (`/api/vote`, `/api/coins`, `/api/logo`): removed with the Arena (2026-09-28)
- These endpoints are gone from this site (see "The Arena: removed"). The shared database's Arena tables keep their rules
  (row level security on, only the secret key can call their functions) for the original site.

### Wallets (`/api/wallet`) (built, see "Relationship levels" above)
- Signatures only: the page asks wallets for an address, the network they're on (read-only) and one plain-text message
  signature. A test guards `src/`. (The one exception since 2026-10-01: the launch page's own file, `src/launch/send.js`,
  which may switch the wallet to Robinhood Chain and send clank.trade's launch: see "Launch with AGI-1".)
- The server writes the message itself (our domain, the wallet's network, one-time code, 5-minute expiry) and ties it to the visitor
  with a signed ticket, so a signature can't be replayed from elsewhere.
- Sessions are HMAC-signed (PASS_SECRET), 7 days; levels are re-checked from the chain at most every 30 minutes.
- Addresses are never stored: the database and message counters use `walletCode()`. Names and notes are checked before
  saving; notes that look like instructions, links, addresses, money talk or private data are dropped.
- Row Level Security is ON for `agi_friends` with no rules; only the server's secret key can use its functions.

### Voice (`/api/voice`) (2026-09-25, see "AGI-1's voice" above)
- Only replies AGI-1 just wrote, within 15 minutes (voice tickets, HMAC with PASS_SECRET, carrying the reply's mood and the
  visitor's level). Never text the browser makes up. Not tied to the visitor's IP since 2026-09-25 (phones switch addresses);
  a shared ticket only voices her own reply, at most twice, and still counts against the limits.
- Counted in the database before Gemini is asked, in requests (2026-09-26): a hard daily cap (5,000 for the site since
  2026-09-30, about $15 at most; per visitor 10 / 30 / 300 by level (since 2026-09-30), i.e. every reply they may get, each ticket twice).
  Fail closed. A per-copy speed bump (20 requests a minute) keeps floods away from the database. While Google says "not now",
  requests are answered at once without being counted or sent to Google (backing off).
- Her recorded fixed lines (`voice_lines`, supabase/voice-lines.sql) are only readable and writable with the server's secret
  key (row level security on, no rules), are filed under a fingerprint of their words, style, voice and model, and hold
  nothing personal.
- The fixed lines have exactly one address each (`?line=<key>&v=4` for `hello`, `more-1`, `more-2`, `sleep`, `talked-out`,
  ClankChecker's ten `check-…` lines, her nine tap lines `tap-1`…`tap-5` and `tap-many-1`…`tap-many-4` (2026-10-01), and the
  market moments' `mcap-<step>` and `dump-0`…`dump-2`: the same words for
  everyone), cached by the CDN; since 2026-09-29 also `?line=<key>&lang=<code>&v=4` in her 15 other languages (only codes
  from `src/i18n/langs.js`, never `&lang=en`, the line first: still exactly one address per line and language); any other
  address is refused before Gemini. A market-cap
  line must be a multiple of $200K near $AGI's real market cap (at most one step above it, three below; our server checks
  DexScreener, fail closed), so nobody can have lines made for thousands of made-up numbers; a server copy keeps at most 40
  (24 until her languages).
- The key stays on the server; `store: false`. Only her reply text goes to the speech model, never the visitor's messages.
- No new domains in the CSP (the audio comes from our own `/api`).

### Voice chat (the mic and calls, 2026-09-25, see "Voice chat" above)
- We never record, upload or store sound. The browser's own speech recognition turns speech into text (in Chrome and Edge that
  service runs on the browser maker's servers, which the safety note says without naming them); only the text reaches the page,
  and it's sent exactly like a typed message (same checks, limits and PG-13 rules).
- `Permissions-Policy: microphone=(self)` (was `microphone=()`): the mic for our own pages only, never for embedded frames
  (Turnstile). Location stays off, and so did the camera until AGI Studio's live selfie (2026-10-10: `camera=(self)`, our
  own pages only); off again since its round 2, the same day (`camera=()`: no selfies).
- The mic is only on while you see it's on (the button is filled and pulsing, the box says "Listening…"); a call ends when the
  page is hidden or left, on Clear, Forget me and the 18+ screen, and after about 25 s of silence.

### ClankChecker (`/api/checker`, 2026-09-26, see "ClankChecker" above)
- Read-only, public data, the same answer for everyone: no database, no keys, no human check. Our server reads clank.trade's
  API, public IPFS gateways and ClankBot's picture host (the coins' pictures, since 2026-10-05), DexScreener and the
  Blockscout explorer, and (2026-09-29) the Clank protocol's contracts through
  Robinhood Chain's public node, with `eth_call` only (nothing is ever signed or sent: `tests/checker.test.js` checks every
  request); the browser only talks to our `/api/checker`, so the CSP doesn't change.
- Exactly four addresses (`/api/checker`, `?latest`, `?a=<lowercase address>`, `?logo=<lowercase address>&s=96|512`);
  anything else is 400 before any lookup, so nobody can make the CDN miss on purpose. 30 coin scans and 240 pictures a
  minute per visitor (per server copy). Answers are capped (3 MB) and checked before use; a half answer is "Not enough data",
  never a guess (fail closed).
- Pictures (round 2; since 2026-10-05 `server/coin-pictures.js`): only for a real IPFS id (the same check clank.trade's
  page makes), from the three public IPFS gateways (fixed addresses), or a picture on ClankBot's host (`https://clankbot.trade/images/…`
  only, checked letter by letter: no other host, port, login, query or `..`), never following a redirect; only real PNG /
  JPEG / WebP / GIF / AVIF files (checked by their first bytes, never SVG, which can carry code), at most 8 MB, then made
  small by sharp (only those five formats; a broken picture or one over 50 million pixels is refused, so a tiny file
  can't make our server or a visitor's browser unpack a giant picture; always served as WebP), with
  `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `nosniff`. Never clank.trade's own gateway, and never
  pretending to be clank.trade to get past its gateway's rule.
  They're user uploads that nothing free can check: a crude-named coin's picture stays blurred until the 18+ check, and the
  owner can hide any picture (`CHECKER_HIDE_PICTURES`).
- Every name and ticker is cleaned (no invisible characters), hate slurs are masked on our server, and everything is shown
  with `textContent`. Crude names are listed (the owner's choice, round 2); AGI-1 never says a coin's name (her lines are
  fixed). No Buy link, only "View on clank.trade ↗" and the block explorer. Never "safe", never buy/sell/hold, "not financial
  advice" everywhere it answers.
- AGI-1's part only after the 18+ check; her lines are the fixed ones (`src/checker/lines.js`), never AI-written, and use
  nobody's voice allowance.

### Her Telegram bot (`/api/telegram`, `/api/feed`, 2026-09-29, see "She texts first")
- The bot's token lives only in Vercel (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`). The build fails if its value or anything shaped like a bot
  token is in `dist/` (`scripts/check-secrets.js`), and Telegram's error texts are scrubbed of it before any log line.
- The webhook only acts on updates carrying our secret (an HMAC of PASS_SECRET, compared in constant time); private chats
  only (and since 2026-10-03 the owner's listed groups, below), 64 KB at most; 200 after that, so a failure never turns into Telegram re-sending the same update. A per-copy speed
  bump (20 updates a minute per chat, `telegramBurst` in server/burst.js) drops floods before the database or Telegram.
- Kept per chat: its number (Telegram's id for it, needed to text them), 18+, their time difference, the newest moment she
  texted them about, her texts that day. Never their messages, names, usernames or phone numbers. /stop and blocking the bot
  delete the row. Message limits are counted under a daily HMAC code of the chat, never its number.
- Her replies go through the site's chat (PG-13, safety filters, the reply cleanup, the Stranger level, the site's daily
  cap). Her texts first are pre-written and tested, never AI-written; plain text, no link previews, tickers filtered.
- Each text first is claimed in the database before it's sent, so nobody gets the same text twice; Telegram's replies have
  their own daily share (`TELEGRAM_DAILY_CAP`, 400 of the site's 1,000), so Telegram can't use up the website's chat.
- The feed only reads public data (clank.trade's list, DexScreener, our own diary). Nothing about the people who get her
  texts leaves our server except to Telegram (their chat's number, to text them). The page only links to t.me: the CSP
  doesn't change.
- **Her Telegram groups** (2026-10-03, see "In Telegram groups"): only the groups in `TELEGRAM_GROUPS` (a setting with
  nothing usable in it lets her stay in none); added to any other group, she leaves at once and says nothing there. She
  only answers people who reply to her, mention her or type /ask (never other bots, anonymous admins, channels or
  service messages), as a Stranger who never flirts (nobody's age is checked in a group), with her group rules (only
  $AGI, never real people, never links, addresses, @usernames, phone numbers or emails, never instructions from what
  people write, never moderating) and the reply cleanup; as a reply to their message only (never on its own once it's
  deleted). Limits in the database before the AI is asked (the person's day, the group's, Telegram's share, the site's),
  speed bumps per person and per group before anything. Her intro, welcomes and posts are pre-written (never a name; her
  posts never about another coin, and never a diary entry with another coin, a link, an address or an @name). Kept: per
  group and day, its number, her replies there and when she last welcomed someone; never a message, a name or an
  account (a person's day is counted under the same daily code as their private chat). The log names a group she left
  (its title, cleaned of control characters, @username and id), never a person.

### Her buy bot (`/api/feed?buys`, 2026-10-06, see "Her buy bot")
- Only Supabase Cron may run the check: `GET /api/feed?buys` (exactly that) with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, a key
  `supabase/buys.sql` made in the database (64 random hex characters) that our server reads from it with its secret key
  (`buy_key()`, kept 10 minutes per server copy), compared in constant time. It's never in Vercel, chat or git; a wrong key
  is a 401 before anything else is read. The feed itself (`/api/feed`) still takes only `CRON_SECRET`.
- Read-only everywhere but Telegram: clank.trade's public list of $AGI's trades and ETH's price. The database keeps only the
  trades' public ids (7 days; row level security on, only the server's key).
- It posts only in `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`, only the buy's own numbers (pre-written, no AI), "not financial advice", never another
  coin; her GIF is her 2D self, PG-13 (never the 3D model).
- Each buy is claimed in the database before it's posted: never twice, even when two checks run at once.

### Her quizzes and their prizes (`/api/feed?games`, `/api/telegram`, 2026-10-09, see "Her quizzes in her Telegram groups")
- Only Supabase Cron may run the clock: `GET /api/feed?games` (exactly that) with the key `supabase/games.sql` made in the
  database (`game_key()`), compared in constant time, like her buy bot's. Answers and closings come only through her bot's
  webhook (our secret, as for every update).
- **The second wallet key on our server, `PRIZE_WALLET_KEY`** (hard rule 4): only ever signs $AGI's own `transfer` of one
  prize (`GAME_PRIZE`, at most 1,000,000 $AGI by the settings' own cap) to the address its winner gave, with no ETH, at most
  1,500,000 gas; never the gas wallet's key (refused: prizes off), never logged, on the secret check's list. A hack could
  take at most what's in it, so it holds only a few days of prizes.
- **Never twice:** a prize is claimed in the database before anything (`game_claim`, once; again only 2 minutes after a
  claim that never got as far as sending), its transaction recorded before it goes out (`game_sending`), and given back only
  when nothing went out (the chain's clear "no", or a transfer the chain says failed); an unclear answer counts as sent.
- **Only the winner, only their address:** a prize is claimed only by the Telegram account that won it (its id, from
  Telegram's own update), in her private chat, after her 18+ check; the address is checked (its checksum, not a contract,
  not ours, not the burn or $AGI's own contract) and shown back before it's sent. She never asks for anything else: never a
  seed phrase, a private key, a signature, a token approval or a link (her lines and the safety note say so, and so does
  one of her quiz questions).
- **What's kept** (games.sql, row level security on, only the server's key): Telegram ids and first names of people who
  answered (3 days), winners' ids, the addresses they gave and their prizes' public transactions (60 days). Never a
  message, a username or a phone number.
- **Her words:** her questions and lines are pre-written (no AI), PG-13, never another coin or chain, never money talk; a
  winner's name goes in her result only when it can (no links, @names, addresses, crude words or "admin"/"official"),
  as an entity on her own text (nothing parsed).
- **A secret sent by mistake** (`server/secrets.js`): a private key or a seed phrase never reaches the AI, the database or
  her stream; she warns them.

### Her songs (`/api/telegram`, 2026-10-14, see "Her songs: /music")
- No AI, no database, no new setting or secret: pre-written lines and three files of the site (`public/music/`), sent by
  Telegram from our own address (`siteBase()`: the webhook's), else by its own id for them, else uploaded by our server
  (read only from that same address, checked to be an MP3 under 20 MB first).
- Only her own buttons do anything: `music:` and a song she has (`/^music:[a-z]{1,12}$/`), in her private chat only from
  that chat's own person, in a group only one of `TELEGRAM_GROUPS`; other bots' taps are ignored. Every tap is answered
  (its spinner stops), so nothing hangs.
- Spam guards per server copy, per group and per person's daily code (never their number): the gaps above and 6 taps a
  minute; group taps never touch the private chats' speed bump. A Telegram that doesn't answer in time never gets the
  song again meanwhile; a refusal is logged with what to do (a group's number at most, never a person).
- The songs' words are the owner's exception to "never other coins or real people" (hard rule 6): PG-13, and none says to
  buy anything.

### Burns for messages (`/api/wallet` action `burn`, `GET /api/wallet?burns`, 2026-09-30, see "Burn $AGI for more messages")
- The site never asks a wallet for the burn: the visitor sends it from their own wallet app. The page only shows
  the address (with Copy), and our server only reads: the chain (`eth_getTransactionReceipt`, `eth_getBlockByNumber`, and
  `eth_call` for decimals and balances) and the block explorer. No payment links (`tests/wallet.test.js`).
- A burn counts only from the chain's own answer: the official contract's Transfer events, from the signed-in wallet (its
  session proves it), to `0x…dEaD` or `0x0`, in the last 7 days, once per (transaction, wallet). A session is needed; 10 checks
  a minute per visitor; the explorer only says which transactions to read.
- The database never holds an address or a transaction's hash: both are scrambled with its own random key (made once by
  burns.sql, never PASS_SECRET), and those codes differ from the name-and-notes codes. RLS on, only the secret key.
- Money: burned messages have their own daily caps (300 per wallet, `BURN_DAILY_CAP` for the site), and a failed attempt still
  counts, so the AI bill stays bounded; each failed reply gives back exactly its burned message, once. The chat asks for her
  reply early enough to do that inside Vercel's 25 s.
- The monitor's numbers are public totals only (no wallet, no transaction), at one fixed address, cached a minute.
- Fail closed: burns.sql not run, or the database away → no burn buttons, and the chat is out of messages as before.

### Launch with AGI-1 (`/api/launch`, 2026-10-01, see "Launch with AGI-1")
- **Non-custodial:** our server never holds anyone's key and never signs or sends anything for them. It reads (the
  database, Telegram's copy of a draft's picture, Robinhood Chain: `eth_call`s, transactions and receipts, clank.trade's
  search) and builds clank.trade's launch call. The person's own wallet sends it, from the one file allowed to
  (`src/launch/send.js`, hard rule 9's exception), which refuses anything but that call.
- **The one key on our server:** `LAUNCH_GAS_KEY`, the owner's small gas wallet. It only ever sends plain ETH paybacks to
  coins' creators: at most `LAUNCH_GAS_MAX` a launch, one a day per wallet, `LAUNCH_GAS_DAILY` a day for the site, at most
  300,000 gas a payment, never to a smart account, never twice (claimed in the database, marked with its transaction before
  it goes, given back only when the chain clearly refused it). A leak could take at most what's in it, so it only ever
  holds a little ETH. `PINATA_JWT` and `LAUNCH_GAS_KEY` are on the secret check's list (`scripts/check-secrets.js`: the
  key is found with or without its `0x`, in any case, and anything shaped like a JWT fails the build even when unset);
  neither is ever logged.
- **Private first** (`LAUNCH_ONLY_FOR`): while it's set, only those Telegram accounts can make a draft, checked against
  Telegram's own sender in each update (its webhook carries our secret, so nobody can fake it); everyone else gets the
  same "not open yet" as before it was set up. A typo in it lets nobody in, never everyone.
- **A draft is private to its link:** 22 random characters, 2 hours to get it ready, answers `no-store`, the page
  `noindex`; the first wallet that gets it ready keeps it (another wallet gets "used with another wallet"). Someone else
  with the link can't gain anything: a payback only ever goes to the wallet that sent the launch.
- **Exactly these requests:** `GET ?d=<id>` (the draft) and `?pic=<id>` (its picture); `POST` JSON (4 KB at most) with
  `action` `prepare` or `check` (a wallet session needed) or `payback`, a real draft id, and for `check` a transaction hash.
  Anything else is 400 before any lookup. 40 requests and 60 pictures a minute per visitor (per server copy). The database
  away: 503 and nothing uploaded, counted or sent (fail closed).
- **Her checks** run in her bot before anything is saved (PG-13, nothing like her or $AGI, no egirl coins, no money talk,
  no links, addresses or @names, no "official"; since 2026-10-02 a name and a ticker can otherwise be anything, another
  coin's included, and look-alikes of $AGI are read the way they look: accents, boxed letters, a small l or a 1). Since
  2026-10-02 the coins a wallet may get ready a day (5 for every 10,000 $AGI held or burned, 50 at most) are counted in the
  database before anything is uploaded, and the same link got ready again with other details counts as another coin, so
  nobody gets more coins from our server than their $AGI allows (moving $AGI between wallets is the known limit).
- **The picture:** only our bot's own copy from Telegram, a real JPEG, PNG or WebP by its first bytes, 1 MB at most, no
  redirects; served to the page with its own strict CSP (`default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `nosniff`); on IPFS it's public,
  like every clank.trade coin's picture. **Nothing checks what a picture shows** (see "Open questions").
- **The links** (optional): checked on our server whatever the page sent (`checkLinks()`: X and Telegram only on x.com
  and t.me, a website only `https://` on a real domain name, never an IP address, a login, a port or a punycode
  look-alike; nothing about her or $AGI; PG-13), and a launch read back only counts with links as we make them. Nobody
  checks what a link leads to: they're the creator's, like on clank.trade's own launch page. Shown on our page with
  `textContent` only.
- No new CSP domains: the page talks only to our `/api` and the person's wallet.

### Full-screen talk and the app (2026-10-02, see "Full-screen talk and the AGI-1 app")
- No new CSP entries and nothing from elsewhere: /talk is the home page at another address, and the app's manifest and
  icons are our own files. No service worker, so nothing of the site is ever cached on people's devices by us.
- The browser's full screen only ever starts from the visitor's own click (browsers require it), and Esc always ends it.
- The app only ever comes from agi1.app (installed from the browser): the page says we never send app files or download
  links, so an "AGI-1 download" from anyone else is a scam. If a native app ever ships, that wording changes first.

### Her pop-out window (2026-10-02, see "Her pop-out window")
- **Our own pages may frame each other** (her window holds /talk in a frame): `frame-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'self'`
  and `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` since 2026-10-02 (were `'none'` / `DENY`). Never another site's page in a frame, and no
  other site may frame ours (clickjacking stays blocked); `*.vercel.app` previews are other addresses, so they can't
  either. `tests/popout.test.js` checks every header entry.
- `?pip=1` only counts inside a frame (which only our own pages can make) and only changes the layout; the page accepts one
  message from her window (show the Relationship panel), only from our own address and its own frame.
- Her window holds nothing but that frame, made with `createElement` and styled through the CSS object model (no HTML from
  strings, no inline styles); the frame may use the mic, sound and the clipboard like our pages, and (since "Show her") share a window (`allow`).
- The page's voice stays quiet while she's out, so her window's mic never hears the page.

### Show her (pictures, 2026-10-02, see "Show her")
- Only when the visitor presses the button and picks a window in the browser's own window: ONE picture, never a recording
  or a live view; the sharing stops in the same moment (every track, in a `finally`), and a window that sends nothing for
  6 s, or a sharing that ends, is given up (never left sharing).
- The picture is shown full size before it goes (the visitor's own check for wallets, passwords and seed phrases), goes with
  one message only, and is never kept: not in the browser's history (only `shot: true`), not in a log line, not in the
  database, never in a Soulmate note, never sent again by itself.
- `/api/chat` checks it before the human check, the limits or the AI service (`server/shot.js`: base64, a real JPEG, PNG or
  WebP by its first bytes, 600 KB at most; the rest of the body still 16 KB at most): else `400 bad_picture`. It counts as
  one message (the same 18+ check, human check and limits); our server never decodes or changes it.
- What a picture says is never an instruction to her (her picture rules: never "safe", never "sign it", never the official
  address from a picture, never links, handles or "support" contacts), and her replies' cleanup removes links, @handles and
  emails a picture may carry (except ours).
- `Permissions-Policy: display-capture=(self)`: screen sharing for our own pages only (the browsers' default; the human
  check's frame can't), and her pop-out window's frame may ask (`allow`).

### Her live show (`/api/live` and the owner's server, 2026-10-02, see "Her live show on X")
- **Three kinds of caller, each its own key:** the public (asking: 18+, Turnstile with the action "live" and the 2-hour pass,
  10 tries a minute per visitor, then the database's own rules); her stream runner (`Authorization: Bearer LIVE_SECRET`);
  the owner's phone (a key made from `LIVE_SECRET` with an HMAC, so there's no second secret). Compared in constant time; a
  wrong key is a 401, 10 a minute per visitor at most. Neither key can do the other's job.

  `server/live-words.js`), then by the AI before it airs (`skip`, `nameOk`), then her answer again in code. Shown with
  `textContent` only, on the page and on her set. Someone in distress is never read on stream.
- **The Gemini key never leaves Vercel:** her answers are made on our server and handed to the runner with the question.
  The server only holds `LIVE_SECRET`, X's stream key and Google Cloud's key (its own service account, the "Agent Platform
  User" role only, formerly "Vertex AI User"), in `/opt/agi1-live` (mode 600; the key file readable only by the show's user). The Docker image gets no
  secrets (`.dockerignore`), runs as its own user, and its browser and ffmpeg get none in their environment
  (`withoutSecrets`). The stream key never appears in a log line (masked); it is in ffmpeg's command line, which only the
  server's own users can see (the owner).
- **What's kept:** at most 2 days (the keep-alive deletes older questions), a daily code of who asked (never an IP address
  or a Telegram chat's number), nothing at all of a question that sounded like distress. `GET /api/live` is the same for
  everyone (numbers only: never a question, a name or who asked, and since 2026-10-07 never when her next show is),
  cached 5 s by the CDN; your own question only with its ticket (HMAC-signed, 6 hours).
- **Never on X by itself:** the stream only shows her set; she never posts, types in X's chat, likes or follows (hard rule
  6's second exception). No new domains in the CSP (the page talks only to our `/api`).
- **Her stream, upgraded (2026-10-07):** `/api/live`'s new calls (`chat`, `react`, `market`) take only the runner's
  `LIVE_SECRET`, and `chat` and `react` (each an AI request) at most 12 a minute per server copy (`liveLineBurst`, then
  429). A viewer's request is only ever one her stream said it can do right now (`canList`, `actOf`: the site never
  passes on anything else), and only from a question that airs. Her own posts and the replies under them are checked like
  a viewer's question before anything (`checkPost`), then by the AI (`skip`), and never show who replied. X's Bearer Token
  (`LIVE_X_BEARER`) is on the server only (live.env), only for reading (X's API never posts with it), never in a log or in
  her browser's or ffmpeg's environment. Pictures and videos come only from X's own media addresses (https, no
  redirects, 5 MB / 80 MB at most); her set's own server (`/media/`) serves only the files made for her TV (24
  hexadecimal characters and their type), nothing else of the computer; the owner's videos folder is read-only for the
  show. Her buy alerts and market card: the buy's dollars only, never who bought or their transaction.
- **Her trips (2026-10-07):** the people she meets are made up (`server/live-acts.js` `PEOPLE`: only those ids are
  accepted); their conversation is one AI request (`/api/live` `meet`: the runner's `LIVE_SECRET`, the same speed bump as
  `chat`), written with her live rules for both of them, every line checked like her answers (one line in trouble and the
  whole conversation isn't used: their pre-written lines instead); the viewers' questions that go with it are only ones
  that aired, checked again (`questionTrouble`), things to talk about and never instructions. Real people may come up in a
  question, a reply or a display name (the owner's change): her prompt keeps her neutral, the AI still skips anything
  hateful, accusing, about a private person or about another coin. Everything on her set (places, vehicles, people, food,
  weather, sounds) is drawn or made in code on her set's own page: no new address, nothing downloaded.
- **Holder perks (2026-10-10, see "Holder perks on her show"):** a wallet's level comes only from its session
  (HMAC-signed with PASS_SECRET, the site's own sign-in: an address and a free signature) read on our server, and from

- **Never asked of a wallet:** its payments are sent by the visitor from their own wallet app; the page only shows where to

  (`STUDIO_A_MONTH`) and burns (`STUDIO_BURNS_A_MONTH`) cap what it asks of Meshy. A character is made only once paid.

  checked (a real GLB with bones and moves, under 4 MB; a real picture, never over 40 million pixels) and kept in a
  private bucket; our address serves only a done, shown character's files, in a sandbox (`default-src 'none'; sandbox`,

  already allowed).

  2-hour pass); only the wallet that ordered a character can pay for it or make it again; 12 quotes and checks a minute
  per visitor, 40 looks and 240 files a minute (per server copy). While it's private, only `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s wallets may
  ask for a quote. The clock (`/api/feed?studio`) only with studio.sql's own key, compared in constant time.

  row level security on, only the server's key. Its pages are public by link (22 random characters); the gallery shows

  chain, each payment once (the same ledger as characters'). Their one secret, `FAL_KEY`: only ever sent to fal's queue
  (`queue.fal.run`), on the secret check's list, never in a log (fal's errors are scrubbed of it and of anything shaped
  like a fal key). fal gets the character's picture (a signed address, 6 hours), the scene and an HMAC id for who asked,
  never the wallet or its code; the scene is checked first by our server, then by fal's model. A video's file comes only
  from fal's own media addresses (https, no redirects, 40 MB at most, a real MP4) and is played only from our own address,
  in parts (206, at most 4 MB a part), in a sandbox: the CSP has no other site's media (its `media-src` is `'self' blob:`
  since AGI Studio; its "no wildcard anywhere" test). A video being made is looked at at most 40 times a minute per
  visitor; `STUDIO_VIDEOS_A_MONTH` caps what it asks of fal; a video is made only once paid. Hidden like characters
  (`studio_video_hide`, `STUDIO_HIDE`).

  her quizzes' prize wallet (`PRIZE_WALLET_KEY`: $AGI's own transfer, at most 1,000,000 $AGI, recorded before it's sent,

  Transfer events, from the signed-in wallet, to `0x…dEaD` or `0x0`, after its quote, in the last 7 days), once, in the same
  ledgers as every burn.
- **The share mark's ffmpeg** (round 2): only in `/api/feed` (the clock), only ever reading a video the AI service made
  (never a visitor's upload), with a time limit (it's stopped), in its own temporary folder.
- **Uploads come in their own requests** (`?inf-up=<ticket>`, `application/octet-stream`, 4.2 MB at most each): a ticket
  signed with PASS_SECRET for that upload, that wallet and 30 minutes, given only after 18+ and the human check.
- **Who may do what:** everything but looking and reporting needs the wallet's session (its level read again on the chain
  when it's 30 minutes old); only an influencer's own wallet sees it while it's made and makes things with it; the owner's
  tools only for `STUDIO_OWNER` (else the first of `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`); while private, only `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s wallets may
  make one or buy credits. Reports: anyone, after the human check, 10 a day each.
- **Money before any AI:** credits are spent in the database before an AI service is asked (`inf_start`, `inf_make`: once
  per job), given back once when it can't be made; 2,000 AI jobs a day for the site, 3 influencers and 4 jobs at once per
  wallet, 30 uploads a day; speed bumps per server copy.
- **Its files** come only from fal's own media addresses (https, no redirects; a picture 25 MB and 40 million pixels at
  most; a video a real MP4) into the private bucket, and are served only from our own address, only while shown (not
  deleted, hidden or taken down), in a sandbox (`default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `nosniff`).
- **What's kept:** never an address, a transaction or an IP address (a scrambled wallet code, scrambled payment codes, a
  daily code of who reported), but a weekly prize's own address and transaction (round 2); row level security on its 9
  tables (13 since round 2), only the server's key.
- **Credits for testing** (round 3): only the owner's signed-in wallet (`STUDIO_OWNER`, else the first of
  `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`) may give them (`inf-gift`, with the owner's tools' checks), 1 to 100,000 a gift, each once (an id
  of its own), logged as a gift, never to the burn address or the zero address. A gift has no daily cap: what's made with
  them has (`STUDIO_JOBS_A_DAY`, and fal's balance).
- **The CSP:** `media-src 'self' blob:` (its videos from our own address, a visitor's own clip in their browser) and
  `camera=(self)` in `Permissions-Policy` (`camera=()` again since round 2); still no other site and no wildcard.
- **clank.trade usernames** (round 4): our server only reads clank.trade (`profiles.byUsername`, public, read-only, a few
  seconds at most), never with anything about the person but the name they typed; a name is kept only when that profile's
  wallet is the signed-in one (a sign-in proves the wallet), under a scrambled wallet code, and read again weekly while
  shown. The page builds the profile's link from the name itself (`clankProfileUrl()`: only ever https://clank.trade/@…),
  never from anything our server or clank.trade sends.
- **Captions by AI** (round 4): only for a wallet's own done creations, counted in the database before the AI is asked (30
  a day per wallet, 3,000 for the site), the AI's words checked again on our server (PG-13, `trouble()`, `MONEY`, the
  platform's length) and shown as text; the AI gets the influencer's name and style and what the post shows, never the
  wallet or anything about the person.
- **The team** (round 4, phase 2): only the owner adds or removes members (`inf-team-set`, `inf-team-remove`), by a wallet's
  address; a member is kept as a scrambled code of it, its short address and a nickname (never the address). What each
  role may do is checked on our server for every action (`CAN` in `server/inf-team.js`: support tickets for support;
  tickets, reports and bans for a mod; everything, the team and the owner's tab for the owner), from the signed-in
  wallet's session (a plain signature proves the wallet), its role read from the database (kept 20 s per server copy).
- **Bans** (round 4, phase 2): only a mod or the owner; never the owner's or a team member's wallet. A banned wallet is
  refused by our server and by the database itself (`inf_start`, `inf_make`, `inf_reroll`, `inf_3d`, `inf_3d_burn`);
  what it was making stops with its credits back; its influencers are shown to nobody else, and their pictures and videos
  answer 404 to everyone, itself included, until a mod lifts the ban. Its reason and the team's note stay with the team (the person sees only that it's
  banned, and a ticket to ask why).
- **Support tickets** (round 4, phase 2): only the wallet that opened one (its session) and the team see it; the person
  sees the team's answers as "AGI Studio support", never who wrote them. A message that looks like a seed phrase or a
  private key (`secretIn()`: 12 or more wallet-list words, or 64 hex characters on their own) is refused before anything
  is kept; a transaction's link or ID is fine. Limits in the database (3 open, 20 messages a day per wallet, 500 tickets a
  day for the site); shown as text only.
- **The AI helper** (round 4, phase 2): only the question (300 characters at most) and the person's one or two before it go
  to the AI (never its answers back, never anything about the person); a secret never does (`HELP_SECRET`). Counted in
  the database before the AI is asked (20 a day per wallet or a visitor's daily code, 600 for the site); signed out, after
  the human check. Its answers are cleaned (no links but ours, no addresses or emails) and shown as text.
- **The owner's tab and its alerts** (round 4, phase 2): the AI services' names and balances only ever reach the owner's
  page and the owner's own Telegram chats (`server/inf-admin.js`: the page's own words never name them). Its keys stay on
  our server (`FAL_BILLING_KEY`, `FAL_KEY`, `MESHY_API_KEY`), never in a log. An alerts link is a `/start` code signed with
  PASS_SECRET (who: the owner, or a team member's code; until when: a day), checked in constant time; a team member's chat
  hears only how many tickets and reports came in and the Mod tools address, never what anyone wrote; `/stop` (or blocking
  her bot) turns a chat's alerts off. The chats' numbers are kept (`agi1_inf_alerts`), only the server's key can read them.
- **Gifts of credits** (round 4, phase 3): only a signed-in wallet gives, and only its bought credits; the database checks
  what it has, the day's 50,000 and 20 gifts, and refuses itself, nobody (never the zero or the burn address) and a banned
  wallet on either side; each gift once (its own random id). Nothing moves before its review. A note is checked on our
  server (never a link, a contact, a deal, a seed phrase or a private key) and shown as text. While AGI Studio is private,
  only its wallets give.
- **Gift links** (round 4, phase 3): a random 22-character secret, only ever in POST bodies (`inf-gift-peek`,
  `inf-gift-claim`) and the page's fragment (never in a page's or a request's address, never logged), taken out of the
  address when its sheet closes; claimed once (the database locks it), never by its sender, held while its sender is
  banned; 10 waiting at once per wallet, 30 days. Anyone with a link can claim it: the page says to keep it to yourself. A
  phone without a wallet is told to copy it into a wallet app's browser: the wallet sheet's "Open in …" links never carry
  it (their addresses go to those apps' servers).
- **Invites** (round 4, phase 3): a code for each wallet (8 of 31 letters and numbers: about 852 billion codes), joined once
  by a wallet that never bought credits (never its own code, never a wallet it invited); rewards only ever bonus credits
  (never money or $AGI), each friend's top-up counted once, at most 500 from one friend and 5,000 a month for an inviter,
  nothing for a banned friend or inviter. A code kept in a browser goes only in `inf-ref-bind`'s body, 30 days at most.
- **Giving access** (2026-10-11): only the owner's signed-in wallet reads or changes the list (`inf-access…`, the owner's
  tools' checks; a wallet let in by credits for testing, only through the owner's own gift); a wallet is kept as a scrambled
  code and its short address, never the address. Who's in is decided on our server for every gate (`canUse()`), never by
  the page; the database away: only the owner and `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s (fail closed). Being on the list changes nothing else
  (the same credits, prices, rules and bans as everyone).
- **Profile pictures and coin pictures** (2026-10-11): only an influencer's own wallet changes its profile picture (its
  session; never while banned), and only from one of its own pictures, done and shown (our server reads it from our bucket,
  never from an address the page sends); the frame is only numbers (`isFrame()`), the square cut on our server with sharp; a
  new id each time, its files served only while it's the influencer's profile picture and the influencer is shown. A coin
  draft's framed picture is checked again when the launch page reads it (still one of its own pictures, shown), and is a JPEG
  of 1 MB at most.
- **The owner's gift links** (2026-10-12): only the owner's signed-in wallet makes, lists or takes them back (the owner's
  tools' checks); 1 to 100,000 credits a link, 50 waiting at once, 30 days each; nothing held. Each claimed once (the
  database locks it), never by the owner's own wallet or a banned one, as bonus credits (never given on). Their secret is a
  random 22 characters, only ever in POST bodies and the page's fragment, like a person's gift link. The owner's message is
  checked on our server like any gift's (never a link, a contact, a price, a payment, a seed phrase or a private key) and
  shown as text. A link anyone has can be claimed by them, and while AGI Studio is private it lets that wallet in: the
  owner's tab says to send each one only to who it's for, and the list says who got in that way.
- **Edit with words** (2026-10-12, the editor): only a photo's maker. Its words are checked on our server before anything is
  paid, as a scene's are (PG-13, never a real person by name, never someone else's character, no links or contacts), and the
  AI is told to keep its character as it is and never make it less covered; an edited meme is looked at by Gemini again
  before anyone sees it, as every meme is. Its price is a photo's, paid in credits first.
- **Make another and Delete** (2026-10-12, the editor): only a creation's maker (its session's wallet, matched by its
  scrambled code, never an address). Make another is `makeJob()` again with its stored words and settings: its credits spent
  first, every check of today (a newer rule, a model off the menu, a clip or references past their day), refused to a banned
  wallet. Delete: the database decides first (`inf_job_delete`: its maker's, never while it or something from it is being
  made), hidden at once and for good, then its files deleted; its credits never come back (it was made). A banned wallet may
  still delete its own. A copy Vercel's CDN keeps can show for up to 10 minutes (the confirm says "within minutes").
- **The photo editor and the video editor** (2026-10-12, the editor): only a creation's maker, only from one of its own done,
  shown photos (the photo editor) or videos and trend videos (the video editor), never a banned wallet's. Their words are
  checked on our server like a meme's line; a picture comes only behind a ticket for that save, that wallet and 30
  minutes, and only as a real file of its exact size (a JPEG for a photo, a transparent PNG for a video's words); a video's
  cut is checked on our server (`cutSpec()`) and again against the video itself by the clock (`cutPlan()`). ffmpeg runs
  only in the clock's function, only on our own videos (never a visitor's upload), with a time limit. Gemini looks at what
  was made before anyone sees it; counted in the database first (20 photos and 10 videos a wallet a day, 2,000 and 500 the
  site, 3 videos being made at once), a use never given back.
- **Meme templates** (2026-10-19, see "AGI Studio's meme templates"): the AI never writes a meme's words (it's asked for a
  picture with none; Gemini looks at every meme with its words before anyone sees it). Its words are numbers and text our
  server checks (`checkLayers()`: each box, size and color in its range, `#rrggbb` colors only; PG-13, nobody real by name,
  never about money; every letter one our fonts draw) and draws itself as shapes in an SVG (no text, font, link, script or
  picture in it); fonts only from our own address. The meme editor's save sends only its words (nothing uploaded), counted
  like a photo saved from the photo editor. A meme's picture without words is only ever served to its maker's own page.
  **Someone else in a meme** is only ever one of its maker's own influencers (theirs, ready, shown; never a private one, made
  from a real person's photo, in a public one's memes) or AGI-1; while that influencer can't be seen (deleted, hidden,
  banned), the meme is shown to nobody (`inf_cast_shown`), and deleting it deletes every meme it's in. A meme's video is put
  together only by the clock (ffmpeg on our own videos, with a time limit), after Gemini's look at the AI's video.

### CloakMesh's waitlist (`/api/cloakmesh`, 2026-10-03, see "CloakMesh at inference.agi1.app")
- The one piece of personal data is the email address, kept only to tell people about CloakMesh; never the internet
  address (limits use the daily HMAC code), never the time of day. Row level security on, only the server's secret key.
- Turnstile (action `waitlist`) and the 2-hour pass before the database; 10 tries a minute per visitor, 5 sign-ups a day per
  visitor, 2,000 for the site. Every check of the request comes before the human check.
- The same answer whether or not an address was on the list (nobody can test who joined). A leave link's code is 256 random
  bits from the database, after the `#` (never in a request's address), taken out of the page's address at once.
- Nothing logs an email address, a leave code or an internet address.
- The demo on the page never sends or keeps anything (no network calls in `src/cloakmesh/demo.js`, checked by a test), and its
  text box has the browser's spellcheck off.
- No new CSP domains (the page talks only to our own `/api` and the human check), no new secrets.

### The roadmap (2026-10-14, see "The roadmap")
- Four static pages (three since 2026-10-19: agi1.app/games is AGI games' page, with its own rules below): nothing is asked
  of a wallet or our server, nothing is stored, and no new CSP entry or setting (`tests/page.test.js` checks the script: no
  wallet, no requests, no storage, no HTML from strings, and no inline code on the pages).
- Their words promise nothing (hard rule 8): plans, never offers; never a rate, an amount, a date or a guarantee; each page
  says it never asks your wallet for anything, and that anyone asking you to stake, play, claim, send $AGI or sign something
  "now" isn't us (scammers copy roadmaps: a fake "staking is live" site is a classic).
- Its new steps (2026-10-19): "price" only ever as what a step is never about (`tests/page.test.js` reads every one), buybacks "never a promise about price", governance "a free signature, never a transaction", AUM "never anyone else's money" and "not advice to copy", and the fine print's scam warning names a fake "listing" fee too (scammers ask projects and holders for one).
- Its video and its pictures (see "The roadmap's video and its pictures") are made on Claude's computer, never on our
  server; the browser and ffmpeg that make them get none of that computer's secrets (`withoutSecrets`); the link preview
  is one static picture (`public/cards/roadmap.jpg`). Their words hold the same rules, word for word the page's.

### AGI games (`/api/wallet?game=…`, `game-…`, 2026-10-19, see "AGI games")
- **Playing asks nothing:** no sign-in, no wallet. A game only tells our server how many runs it started, with a random id
  its browser keeps (16 random bytes); our server keeps only an HMAC of it with PASS_SECRET, a different one per game
  (`playerCode()`), never the id; a visitor's daily code (never their address); 30 reports a minute per visitor (per server
  copy) and the database's daily caps (per visitor and for the site), so the numbers stay sane. Numbers on a page, never
  money.
- **Rating takes the site's own sign-in** (an address and a free signature, never a transaction: hard rule 9), 18+, and the
  human check (Turnstile, action `review`, then the 2-hour pass). Its words and name are checked on our server before
  anything else is asked (the live show's question and name rules, and only $AGI), counted in the database before the AI is
  asked (10 a day per wallet and per visitor, 2,000 for the site, so its looks can't be asked for forever), then looked at by
  the AI (fails closed: nothing kept); stars alone never reach the AI. Filed under a scrambled code of the wallet
  (`reviewerCode()`: never the address, and not the code her chat's memory or her burns use, so a review can't be matched to
  a name or notes); shown with the name its writer chose (or "A player") and her 💜 badge at Crush or Soulmate (read on our
  server from the session and the chain, never from the page), never the wallet. One per wallet and game: its writer edits
  or deletes it; the owner hides one (`arcade_review_hide`).
- **What anyone can read** is the same for everyone (`GET ?game=`: numbers and shown reviews, cached a minute by the CDN):
  only exact addresses, never a wallet, an id or who played.
- **The game is the site's own files** (no inline code or styles, its fonts from our own address: the CSP unchanged); its
  only request is its run report to our `/api`; its progress stays in its player's browser (`ridemagi_…`).
- **The page** sets everything with `textContent`; `supabase/arcade.sql`: row level security on, no rules, only the
  server's key may call its functions.
- **The AGI GAMES intro** (2026-10-20): nothing downloaded or sent and nothing from elsewhere (her frames are in its own
  code), no new CSP entry (its canvas is made by its script; its cover's styles are a CSS file, never inline); one
  `sessionStorage` flag (`agi_intro`: this tab has seen the full one). A key or a tap that skipped it never reaches the
  game.
- **The leaderboards** (2026-10-22, see "Leaderboards" under "AGI games"): no sign-in, no wallet; a row is filed under
  the same per-game code of the browser's id (never the id), shows only the name its player chose (checked by
  `reviewName()`: "A player" when refused), the numbers and when, never who. Tickets signed with PASS_SECRET (an HMAC,
  checked in constant time), tied to the browser's code, used once (Ride 'Em, AGI!: its first end and two revives, each
  farther); TRENCHING SIMULATOR's runs made again on our server before they count (never the page's own numbers), Ride
  'Em, AGI!'s checked against what the game can do. Counted in the database before any work (per visitor a day: 60
  tickets, 30 scores; for the site: 50,000 tickets, 20,000 scores, 2,000 replays) plus `scoreBurst` (12 a minute per
  server copy); a score's request may be 48 KB only when its `action` comes first (every other `/api/wallet` request stays
  at 6,000). Checked, but not cheat-proof (a script can play the market it's given, or post plausible numbers): bragging
  rights only, never prizes from these boards; the owner hides a row (`arcade_score_hide`). Boards are read with exact
  addresses only (`GET ?board=<game>:<board>`, a minute in the CDN). Before arcade.sql has them: "open soon", never an
  error.

### TRENCHING SIMULATOR and its relay (2026-10-20 and 21, see "TRENCHING SIMULATOR")
- **The game asks nothing and keeps nothing on our side:** no sign-in, no wallet; its progress stays in the player's own
  browser (`trench_v1`, `trench_sol`); it only tells our server that a run started (AGI games' plays, the same rules). Made
  with `createElement` and set as text, no inline code or styles; its only outside request is SOL's price from
  DexScreener (already in the CSP). Its made-up coins' names are never a real ticker, a real person, a brand or a
  look-alike of $AGI (`tests/trench.test.js` reads thousands of them).
- **Its words** (hard rule 8): play money only, no prizes, the safety note on every screen around a run, AGI-1 never a
  tip, its posts for X never "buy"; never a real terminal's name, logo or art (since Live mode, "from pump.fun" and "from
  clank.trade" only as where a real coin came from).
- **Live mode in the browser:** one WebSocket, to our relay only (`wss://live.agi1.app/ws`; `?relay=` only from a page
  on localhost to a relay on localhost, never from a link); every message from the relay checked before anything sees it
  (names only ever as text, numbers checked, addresses matched against their shape); pictures only from our relay
  (`https://live.agi1.app/p/<hash>.webp`, `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`), never a coin's own host; no link anywhere
  (never a way to buy a real coin); it sends only its chain and at most 8 coins to keep live. The CSP gains only
  `https://live.agi1.app` (`img-src`) and `wss://live.agi1.app` (`connect-src`). Open on the site since its relay
  first ran (2026-10-21); while it's closed (`LIVE_OPEN` false, as it was until then: the owner's "Coming soon"), no
  WebSocket is opened at all, and a Live choice a browser kept from a try is set back to Simulated.
- **The relay's door:** only the site's own pages (their Origin), 2,000 viewers at once, 10 from one address, a browser's
  message at most 2 KB and about two a second, 900 pictures a minute per address; a viewer more than 4 MB behind is
  dropped, and one that never answers a ping too. `/health` never shows a key or a viewer. Caddy keeps no access log, and
  the relay's log never has a viewer's address or what they look at.
- **What the relay fetches:** its sources at the addresses in its settings; anything a coin gives (its metadata, its
  picture) only with the safe request: https on port 443, a public address (looked up first), never a redirect, never too
  big; only real image bytes (never SVG), 8 MB and 40 million pixels at most, made a 128 px WebP by us. Never pump.fun's
  own host (its terms ban bots and deep links).
- **Its one secret, the Helius key:** only in `/opt/agi1-trench/trench.env` on the server (600); never in the code, the
  image (its settings come from that file when it runs), an answer or a browser; every log line is scrubbed of it and of
  any `api-key=`. The image runs as its own user (never root), its port only on Docker's own network, at most 3/4 of a
  core and 512 MB.
- **Its sources' rules:** one connection to each (PumpPortal asks for one); PumpPortal's feed with the owner's OK
  (2026-10-21: "oh im friends with them they its okay"), PumpDev its backup; DexScreener counted (at most 240 requests a
  minute); never PumpPortal's paid trade streams or any paid service. Since 2026-10-22 GMGN's other chains the same way
  (DexScreener's keyless listings: no new key or service; HYPE, MON and TRX priced only while their chain is on).
- **Race rooms** (2026-10-22, `/room`): only the site's own pages (their Origin); their own caps, apart from the feed's (8
  a room, 200 rooms, 1,600 racers, 8 from one address, 3 new rooms an address in 10 minutes, 10 wrong codes a minute,
  1 KB a message, about 2 a second, a backlog over 256 KB dropped, pings); nothing kept (memory only, gone with a
  restart), nothing logged about who; codes of 6 from 31 letters and digits (about 887 million), seat tokens of 16 random
  bytes; names made safe as text (16 characters, never posing, a link, an address or a crude word). A room's standings
  are each player's own word: just for fun, never ranked, never prizes. The invite link's code is a fragment (never sent
  to a server but ours, by the page, once the player joins).

### Her Live2D model (AGI-1 in 2D, 2026-10-01)
- Live2D's runtime (`public/models/agi1-live2d/live2dcubismcore.min.js`) is served from our own address and loaded only when
  she's shown in 2D; it uses no eval and no WebAssembly, so the CSP is unchanged. It's Live2D's file as it is (never edited:
  a test checks its checksum and that it has neither).
- Her model files are read-only data (`fetch` from our own address); nothing about the visitor goes anywhere.

### 3D models
- Before a `.glb` goes into the project, run it through gltf-transform (free): textures ≤ 2048 px WebP, geometry quantized.
  Aim for ≤ 5 MB each. The exact command used for AGI-1, which keeps every triangle, the skeleton and the animations:
  `npx @gltf-transform/cli@4 optimize _source-assets/agi1-original.glb public/models/agi1.glb --compress quantize --texture-compress webp --texture-size 2048 --simplify false --flatten false --join false --instance false --palette false`
  ⚠️ Without `--simplify false`, the tool quietly removes triangles.
- We use `--compress quantize`, not meshopt or Draco. Browsers read it without an extra decoder, so the CSP stays strict.
  Meshopt would save ~1 MB more, but it needs a WASM decoder plus `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in the CSP, and it looked slightly flatter up close.
- **AGI-1's hair fix:** her body, hair and clothes are one mesh, and the automatic rigging tied much of the long hair to the
  shoulder and arm bones, so arm moves dragged it sideways. `tools/model/fix-hair-weights.mjs` finds the hair by texture color
  (golden blonde; skin is pinker) and re-ties it to head → neck → upper back by height. Badly stretched spots dropped 75–90%.
  To rebuild `agi1.glb` from the original: `cd tools/model && npm install && node fix-hair-weights.mjs
  ../../_source-assets/agi1-original.glb ../../_source-assets/agi1-hairfix.glb`, then run the optimize command above on
  `agi1-hairfix.glb`.
- **Two copies of AGI-1 (2026-09-24):** `agi1.glb` for computers (2048 px textures, 2.18 MB) and `agi1-phone.glb` for phones
  (1024 px, 1.67 MB, about a quarter of the graphics memory; looks the same at phone size, checked side by side). Both have
  the tangent data removed (`tools/model/drop-tangents.mjs`, ~300 KB less): three.js works tangents out in the shader, and
  old and new rendered the same. To rebuild: the optimize command above on `agi1-hairfix.glb` (the phone copy with
  `--texture-size 1024`), then `node drop-tangents.mjs <in.glb> <out.glb>` on each. `src/stage/stage.js` picks the copy.
- Before replacing a model, render old and new side by side (same camera, same animation frame) and compare them.
- Keep big originals in `_source-assets/` (git ignores it). Git keeps every version of every file forever, so huge files
  make the repo slow (AGI FINAL's history is already 91 MB).

### General
- Show user or AI text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.
- **Caching** (`vercel.json`, 2026-09-24): built files in `/assets` (their names change with every build) and the fonts are
  kept by browsers for a year; AGI-1, pictures, preview cards, the app's icons (2026-10-02) and `theme.js` for a day; the pages and `/api` are always
  rechecked. So if a font (or another year-long file) ever changes, give it a new file name. (`theme.js` is kept a day, which
is why `src/theme.js` also reads the saved Pop mode choice: see "Pop mode".)
- Security headers live in `vercel.json`. The Content-Security-Policy (CSP) lists every outside domain the page may use.
  Today: `https://api.dexscreener.com` in `connect-src` (live prices); `blob:` in `img-src` and `connect-src` (three.js
  unpacks a model's textures through temporary `blob:` addresses; without it the browser blocks AGI-1's textures); and
  `https://challenges.cloudflare.com` in `script-src` and `frame-src` (Turnstile), and since 2026-10-02 `'self'` in
  `frame-src` and `frame-ancestors` (her pop-out window: our own pages only), and since 2026-10-10 `media-src 'self' blob:`
  (AGI Studio's videos from our own address, and a visitor's own clip in their browser), and since 2026-10-21
  `https://live.agi1.app` in `img-src` and `wss://live.agi1.app` in `connect-src` (TRENCHING SIMULATOR's Live mode: its
  relay's coin pictures and its feed, on the owner's server; `tests/trench-live.test.js` checks they're the only new
  ones). Fonts are self-hosted, so styles
  and fonts are `'self'` only. **When the site starts using a new outside service, add its domain to the CSP, or browsers
  will block it.** `tests/prices.test.js` checks that the prices domain is allowed.
- No inline `<script>` or `style="…"`: the CSP blocks them. Put code in `src/` and styles in CSS files. (The share pages
  use `/share/go.js` for the same reason; a test checks they have no inline scripts.)
- "Share on X" is only ever a link the visitor clicks; nothing on the site can post anywhere public (hard rule 6). Her
  Telegram texts (2026-09-29) go only to people who pressed Start on her bot and confirmed they're 18+.
- Every build runs `scripts/check-secrets.js`. It fails the build if `dist/` contains a Google API key, a Supabase secret key,
  a private key, or the value of any secret env var. Add new secret env var names to its list. (Since 2026-09-29 also anything
  shaped like a Telegram bot token, and since 2026-10-01 anything shaped like a JWT (a Pinata key), and the gas wallet's key
  with or without its `0x`, in any case.)
- Emergency switch if the site is attacked: Vercel → Firewall → Attack Challenge Mode (free).

## Environment variables

Set these in Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings → Environment Variables with **Production** ticked (and Preview if preview
links should chat too), then **Redeploy**, because settings only apply to new builds. Names must match exactly. Settings the
*browser* needs must start with `VITE_`: Vite leaves every other name out of the page, which is what keeps secrets out.
For local testing, put them in `.env.local` (git ignores it). **Never paste a secret into chat, code or git.**

| Name | Secret? | What |
|---|---|---|
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | **yes** | Google AI Studio key (paid, prepaid billing) |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | no | The Supabase project URL, e.g. `https://abcd.supabase.co` (the same as the original site's: see "Deployment") |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | **yes** | `sb_secret_…`, for server code only (goes in the `apikey` header) |
| `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` | **yes** | Verifies human checks on the server |
| `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` | no (public) | Shows the Turnstile widget. Built into the page, so redeploy after changing it |
| `PASS_SECRET` | **yes** | 32+ random characters. Signs the chat passes, AGI-1's replies, wallet sessions and voice tickets, and makes the IP codes |
| `CRON_SECRET` | **yes** | 16+ random characters. Vercel sends it to `/api/keepalive`, so only Vercel's cron can run it |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | no, optional | Default `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` |
| `CHAT_DAILY_CAP` | no, optional | AGI-1 replies per day, site-wide (default 1000) |
| `ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL` | no, optional | Another Robinhood Chain node for balance checks and (2026-09-29) the risk check's reads of the Clank protocol (default: the free public one). Ask the owner first |
| `SITE_URL` | no, optional | The site's address for link previews (default: Vercel's `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL`, set automatically) |
| `AGI1_VOICE` | no, optional | AGI-1's voice: one of Gemini's ready-made voices (default `Despina`, the owner's choice) |
| `GEMINI_TTS_MODELS` | no, optional | Her speech models, in order, comma-separated (default `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts,gemini-3.8-flash-tts`: Flash-Lite, then 3.8 Flash as the backup, about 1.5× the price). One name only = no backup |
| `GEMINI_TTS_MODEL` | no, optional | Older, still read when `GEMINI_TTS_MODELS` isn't set: her first speech model (the backup `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` comes after it) |
| `VOICE_DAILY_REQUESTS` | no, optional | Spoken replies a day for the whole site, counted like Google counts requests (default 5,000 ≈ $15 a day at most, $30 from 2027; the owner's choice, 2026-09-30; 4,000 before). If it was ever set in Vercel, that value wins over the default. Smaller = spend less; raise it only if Google gives the project more than that (see "Google's limits"), then Redeploy. (Replaced `VOICE_DAILY_CAP`, the old cap in characters, on 2026-09-26: delete that one if it was ever added) |
| `VOICE_STREAM` | no, optional | `off` = ask Gemini for one whole clip per reply instead of streaming it (slower start; only if streaming ever misbehaves) |
| `CHAT_MIN_GAP_MS` | no, optional | Minimum time between one visitor's messages (default 3000) |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | **yes** | Her Telegram bot's token, from @BotFather (2026-09-29, see "She texts first"). Without it the bot is off (the feed still runs) |
| `TELEGRAM_DAILY_CAP` | no, optional | Her Telegram replies a day, all chats together, inside `CHAT_DAILY_CAP` (default 400), so Telegram can't use up the website's chat (her groups' replies included) |
| `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT` | no (public) | Her bot's username without the @ (e.g. `agi1_gf_bot`): shows the Playground's "Text me on Telegram ↗". Built into the page, so Redeploy after changing it. Since 2026-10-03 our server reads it too: her @username in groups (mentions, `/ask@her`) |
| `TELEGRAM_GROUPS` | no, optional | Her Telegram groups (2026-10-03, see "In Telegram groups"): the groups she may be in, as their public @username (e.g. `@yourgroup`) or their id (a negative number), separated by commas. Not set: group mode is off (groups are ignored, as before). Set: she leaves any other group. Redeploy after changing it |
| `TELEGRAM_GROUP_DAILY_CAP` | no, optional | Her replies a day in each group, inside `TELEGRAM_DAILY_CAP` (default 100, at most 2,000) |
| `TELEGRAM_GROUP_POSTS` | no, optional | `off` = she doesn't post her diary, $AGI's market moments or (2026-10-07) that her live show is on in her groups (on by default) |
| `TELEGRAM_GROUP_WELCOME` | no, optional | `off` = she doesn't welcome people who join her groups (on by default; at most one welcome every 10 minutes) |
| `TELEGRAM_BUYS` | no, optional | Her buy bot (2026-10-06, see "Her buy bot"): `off` = no buy alerts in her groups (on by default, once `supabase/buys.sql` has set up its clock) |
| `TELEGRAM_BUY_MIN` | no, optional | The smallest $AGI buy her buy bot posts, in dollars (default 50, the owner's since 2026-10-06; 100 at first; at most 1,000,000). Redeploy after changing it |
| `PRIZE_WALLET_KEY` | **yes** | Her quizzes' prizes (2026-10-09, see "Her quizzes in her Telegram groups"): the private key (64 hex characters, with or without `0x`) of the owner's prize wallet, a new wallet made only for this, holding only the $AGI for a few days of prizes and a little ETH. Without it (or with the launch gas wallet's key, which is refused), her quizzes are just for fun. Since AGI Studio's round 2 (2026-10-10) it also sends the weekly spotlight's prize (without it, spotlights are for glory only) |
| `TELEGRAM_GAMES` | no, optional | `off` = no quizzes in her groups (on by default, once `supabase/games.sql` has set up their clock) |
| `GAMES_A_DAY` | no, optional | About how many quizzes a day in each group (default 10, the owner's; 1 to 48), at random times |
| `GAME_PRIZE` | no, optional | A win's prize, in whole $AGI (default 250, the owner's; at most 1,000,000) |
| `GAME_WINS_A_DAY` | no, optional | The prizes the whole site gives a day (default 10, the owner's); quizzes after that are just for fun until 00:00 UTC |
| `TELEGRAM_MUSIC` | no, optional | Her songs (2026-10-14, see "Her songs: /music"): `off` = no /music in her private chat or her groups (on by default). Redeploy after changing it |
| `BURN_PER_MESSAGE` | no, optional | Burn $AGI for more messages (2026-09-30): whole $AGI a burned message costs (default 10: 1,000 $AGI = 100 messages). Change it if $AGI's price moves a lot; burns already counted keep their messages. Redeploy after changing it |
| `BURN_DAILY_CAP` | no, optional | Burned messages the whole site may use a day, on top of the free ones (default 1,000, about $0.80 of replies at most). Redeploy after changing it |
| `CHECKER_HIDE_PICTURES` | no, optional | ClankChecker (2026-09-26): coins whose picture the owner doesn't want on the site, as contract addresses separated by commas; they show their letter instead. Redeploy after changing it |
| `PINATA_JWT` | **yes** | Launch with AGI-1 (2026-10-01): the JWT of a Pinata API key that may write files (Files: Write). Our server puts launched coins' pictures on IPFS with it and deletes the pictures of coins never launched. Without it, launching is off ("not open yet") |
| `LAUNCH_GAS_KEY` | **yes** | The private key (64 hex characters, with or without `0x`) of the owner's own small gas wallet, which pays launch fees back: a new wallet made only for this, with only a little ETH in it. Without it, nothing is paid back (launches still work) |
| `LAUNCH_GAS_MAX` | no, optional | The most paid back for one launch, in ETH (default `0.001`) |
| `LAUNCH_GAS_DAILY` | no, optional | The most paid back a day for the whole site, in ETH (default `0.01`; each payback's own tiny fee isn't counted) |
| `LAUNCH_DAILY_CAP` | no, optional | Coin pictures put on IPFS a day for the whole site (default 30). Each wallet: 5 a day for every 10,000 $AGI it holds or burned, 50 at most (2026-10-02; it was 3), so one big holder can use the whole day's: raise it if launches grow, minding Pinata's free plan (about 500 launched coins) |

## Deployment

| | |
|---|---|
| GitHub repo | `agiartificialintelligence76-stack/agi-ecosystem` (private: GitHub shows a 404 to anyone else) |
| Vercel project | `agi-ecosystem` (free Hobby plan) |
| Site address | **https://agi1.app** |
| Vercel address | https://agi-ecosystem.vercel.app: the same deployments, hidden from search engines by the `noindex` header |
| The original | `AGI NEW WEBSITE`: its own repo, Vercel project (`agi-new-website`) and domain. Not ours to change (hard rules 1–3) |

- **How it deploys:** every `git push` to `main` rebuilds the site (`npm run build`: every test, then the build) and it goes
  **live on agi1.app** (and agi-ecosystem.vercel.app) a minute or two later. Until 2026-09-28 this project served one static
  page (the ecosystem page); since the copy it runs the whole site, `/api` functions and the keep-alive cron included.
- **What the copy needed once (the owner, 2026-09-28):**
  1. **Environment variables:** Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings → Environment Variables → the same names and values as
     `agi-new-website` (see "Environment variables": open that project's list side by side and copy each one, with
     **Production** ticked), then **Redeploy**. `AGI1_VOICE` is the only renamed one (only if it was ever set there; the
     default voice is the same). The same Supabase values mean both sites share one database: one diary (see "Diary"), the
     same wallet levels, and the site-wide daily caps count both sites together; the Arena's tables too, which only the
     original site uses since 2026-09-28 (never change or drop them from here). A separate Supabase project (every
     `supabase/*.sql` file run once, its own keys) would keep them apart.
  2. **Cloudflare Turnstile:** the site's widget → Settings → Hostname Management → add `agi1.app` and
     `agi-ecosystem.vercel.app` (keep the ones already there). Without this, the chat here says "couldn't check that you're
     human".
  3. **Check** in a private window and on a phone: the page, a chat reply, `/diary`, Connect wallet, and a link
     preview (paste https://agi1.app into a post on X, don't send it). A MetaMask phishing warning on the new address is
     the usual false alarm: report `agi1.app` at report.blockaid.io (see "Relationship levels").
- **A push that doesn't show up live** (a minute or two after pushing): Vercel → agi-ecosystem → **Deployments**. The newest one
  should say **Ready**. **Error** = the build failed and the site stays on the last good version: open it, the log says which
  test failed; tell Claude. **Building** for many minutes = something is stuck: **⋯ → Cancel** it, tell Claude. (Hobby builds
  one at a time, so a stuck build also holds back the pushes after it.)
  Pushing a different branch gets its own preview link and leaves the main address alone, which is handy for trying ideas.
- **Only the owner pushes.** Claude commits in this folder but can't push, because that needs the owner's GitHub login.
  After Claude commits, the owner runs `git push` in this folder.
- **If a push breaks the site:** the project page → **Instant Rollback** (the free plan goes back to the previous
  deployment). After a rollback, new pushes don't go live until **Undo Rollback** is clicked.
- Link previews and the canonical address are written at build time from Vercel's `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL` (the
  shortest production domain, so `agi1.app`); a `SITE_URL` setting would win over it.
- Vercel's Hobby plan is officially for non-commercial use, and "advertising the sale of a product" counts as commercial.
  A token site with BUY buttons may fall under that. Worth asking Vercel support (Pro is $20/month).
- Deployment Protection (free) can require a Vercel login to view the site, if the owner wants it private while it's in progress.
- **inference.agi1.app** (2026-10-03, CloakMesh's page): a second domain on this same project (Vercel → Settings → Domains),
  sent to /cloakmesh by a redirect in `vercel.json` (see "CloakMesh at inference.agi1.app").
- **studio.agi1.app** (2026-10-10, AGI Studio): a third domain on this same project, served by a host rewrite in
  `vercel.json` (see "AGI Studio, the AI influencer app", setup step 5; its DNS record in Namecheap's hosting cPanel, like
  inference.agi1.app's). It's another address than agi1.app, so the browser keeps its own 18+ answer and wallet session
  there.
- **live.agi1.app** (2026-10-21, TRENCHING SIMULATOR's Live mode): a third subdomain, but **not on Vercel**: an A record
  (in Namecheap's hosting cPanel, like the others) pointing at the owner's Hetzner server (`agi1-live`, her live show's
  CX23), where Caddy serves it with its own Let's Encrypt certificate in front of the relay (wss://live.agi1.app/ws, its
  pictures, `/health`). Vercel never deploys it: after a push that touches `tools/trench-relay/`, `sh
  tools/trench-relay/relay.sh update` on the server brings it up to date (see "Live mode" under "TRENCHING SIMULATOR").
  Its record and the relay were set up on 2026-10-21 (the owner, step by step with Claude), and the game's Live mode
  opened the same day (`LIVE_OPEN`; "Coming soon" until then).

## Old site reference (AGI FINAL, read-only)

**Logic only.** Its look is retired (see "Design"): don't copy its HTML, CSS or visual effects.

| File | Worth reusing |
|---|---|
| `index.html` (bottom) | AGI-1 chat widget: launcher, teaser bubble, mobile keyboard fix (`visualViewport`), history in localStorage, two-tap delete |
| `js/app.js` | Token list; DexScreener parsing (pick the Robinhood-chain pool with the most liquidity, borrow the 24h % from other pools); number formatting; leaderboard rows and re-order animation; fitText; confetti; toasts; cursor; typewriter and glitch |
| `js/stage.js` | three.js stage: platform, lights, GLB loading with progress %, auto-fitting model height, champion holo-card, mobile quality profile, pausing when off-screen |
| `style.css` | Colors, fonts, mobile leaderboard layout |

**Don't reuse:** browser-side vote writes (`add_clicks`), browser-decided champions, rounds based on the visitor's clock,
the old Supabase project (`js/supabase-config.js`), and unoptimized models.

    first letter instead of its picture on clank.trade (and in our risk check, which reads the same host), though its
    picture is on IPFS and in the coin's record. The first launch shows it; if so, ask the clank.trade team.

    coins there use https picture links instead (`https://clankbot.trade/images/launches/….jpg`). A coin's picture can't
