  - **(2026-10-22) Not tried yet:** any of that day's work in a browser (GNGM, the games page's leaderboards, race rooms),
    real phones, `supabase/arcade.sql` in the real database, the relay's update on the server (rooms, the new chains),
    Node 20 and 22 (only Node 24 on the owner's PC), and the full test suite's list of failures on Windows (`npm test`
    exits 1 there; its output was too long to read in Claude's tool: run it in a terminal).

## Working in this repo

- Small steps. After each one, explain simply what changed and why.
- Test at phone width (360 px) and on desktop.
- Before committing, make sure `npm run build` passes and the diff contains no secrets.
- Use clear commit messages, e.g. "Add AGI-1 wave reaction".
- Update this file whenever a decision changes, including the decisions log.
- Image files Claude copies into this folder (SVG, PNG, …) may get a small "content credentials" (C2PA) metadata block
  saying Claude made them. That's expected and harmless: keep it. Audio too (2026-10-07): her song
  `tools/live/songs/feel-the-agi.mp3` got it as an ID3 tag in front (one GEOB frame of type `application/c2pa`, 5,822
  bytes; the sound itself unchanged), so `tests/stream.test.js` allows that label and no other tag. Videos and WebP pictures
  too (2026-10-11, AGI Studio's guide videos): each MP4 got a 5,875-byte `uuid` box right after its `ftyp` (its `stco`
  chunk offsets moved by as much, its `moov` still before its `mdat`, its video data unchanged), and each WebP a `C2PA`
  chunk after its image data (5,768 bytes; the picture unchanged); `tests/guide.test.js` and the build pass with them. JPEGs too (2026-10-13, her two pictures for "💜 With AGI-1"): a 5,771-byte APP11 segment right after the file's start (the picture unchanged; `agi1Names()` names them by these bytes); `tests/influencer.test.js` passes with them. So
  these files' checksums here differ from Claude's copies.
- **Claude never runs git in this folder through its link to the owner's computer**, not even `git status`: that link can't
  delete files, so git leaves an empty `.git/index.lock` behind and the owner's next `git add` fails ("index.lock: File
  exists"). It happened once (2026-09-25; removed with the owner's permission). Claude compares files by checksum instead. If
  it ever happens again: delete `.git\index.lock` in this folder (only when no git command is running), then retry.
  (2026-10-14: Claude ran a `git log` there by mistake; it left nothing behind, checked, and the rule stands for every
  git command.)
- **Tests never depend on the build's own settings** (2026-10-02): Vercel runs `npm test` with the project's real
  environment variables present (the owner's keys). A test that needs a setting to be missing deletes it first (in its
  `beforeEach`). The first push of "Launch with AGI-1" failed that way (Vercel: Error after 41 s): three Telegram tests
  expected launching to be off, but the owner's Pinata key was already in Vercel. Since then Claude also runs every test
  with all the settings in "Environment variables" set to real-looking values before handing over a change. A failed build
  never touches the live site: Vercel keeps serving the last good deployment.
- **Tests pass on any day, at any time** (2026-10-10): a test may give the code its own `now` (a fixed date, to say
  which minute or week it is), but the code must never compare that with the real clock. AGI Studio's round 2 failed on
  Vercel that way: its clock's deadline was `now + 19 s`, so two tests that passed 12:00 and 12:30 UTC of that day as
  `now` ran out of time once the real clock passed them (it passed on Claude's computer in the morning). Every server
  deadline is the real clock's since then (`tests/influencer.test.js` checks it). Before handing over a change Claude
  also runs the whole suite with the clock moved forward (a preloaded `Date` shim, `CLOCK_SHIFT_MS`, in Claude's
  scratch): across midnight, into a Monday, a week on, across a month's and a year's end, six months on; and with
  `TZ=UTC` (Vercel's) as well as the workspace's own time zone. One kind stays, and is harmless: a test of a day's count
  that is running at the very moment 00:00 UTC passes fails (its first half counts under one day, its check reads the
  next); the run moved to 2026-12-31 23:59:20 hit it once, in a 20 ms launch test, and (2026-10-21) the run moved to
  2026-10-21 23:59:20 hit it in AGI Studio's stats board test, whose jobs are done a second before its now (a 1-second
  window: its "made today" read 0; confirmed with a frozen clock). A build meets that about once in tens of thousands:
  if a build that ran right at 00:00 UTC (8:00 the owner's time) fails on a count "for today", Redeploy.
- **A test that moves `Date.now` reads its day with `new Date(Date.now())`** (2026-10-12, the video editor's clock test):
  `new Date()` with no date reads the real clock, not a replaced `Date.now`. The clock test moves `Date.now` on a minute
  at a time and the fake database counts "today" by it, so a day read with `new Date()` disagreed with it for about a
  minute before 00:00 UTC (found by the clock shift to 23:59:00 UTC; it would have failed a build started then).
- **Claude checks every file it saves into this folder by checksum, on the owner's computer, after saving.** A file saved
  twice in one session goes the second time from a new place in Claude's workspace (2026-10-02: the second save of
  CLAUDE.md from the same place wrote the first copy again; the checksum check caught it).
- A recording of her show on Claude's computer (`node tools/live/run.mjs --record …`) uses her set as it was last built
  in `tools/live/dist/` (git ignores it): after changing anything in `tools/live/page/`, record with `LIVE_REBUILD=1`
  (2026-10-10: a first recording without it showed her cards without their new 💜 badge). The server's image always
  builds her set fresh (`run.mjs --build` in its Dockerfile), so `update` there needs nothing more.
- Claude's end-to-end tests build the site with Cloudflare's public test site key
  (`VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000BB npx vite build`): without a site key the chat answers "i'm still getting
  ready for the new site" and every suite that chats fails (2026-09-26). The real key only comes from Vercel's settings.
- **Lightning CSS (Vite's CSS minifier) keeps only the last of a prefixed pair** (2026-10-10, AGI Studio's blurs): write
  `-webkit-backdrop-filter` first, then `backdrop-filter` with the same value. The other way round, the build dropped the
  unprefixed one, and Chrome lost the blur. `tests/influencer.test.js` checks every blur in `studio-app.css`.
- **The unit tests read the app's files as text, so a syntax error in a view only shows in the Vite build** (2026-10-10,
  AGI Studio's round 3: an extra parenthesis in `views/gallery.js`, with every unit test passing). Claude always runs the
  build (and a browser test) too before handing a change over; Vercel's `npm run build` would have failed on it.
- **Downloads in a browser test** (2026-10-12, clean downloads): Playwright's routes never see an `<a download>` click (the
  browser's download manager fetches it: it reached Vite's preview and saved `launch.html`), so such a link's bytes are
  read from our server for its own href; and under Playwright's request interception, a navigation redirected to another
  site's attachment (our 302 to a video's signed address, the long-live `?inf-video-dl` link too) shows Chromium's error page
  before downloading, while real Chromium without interception downloads it and stays on the page (Claude's scratch
  `dlprobe/probe.mjs`): a test serves such a target from a real local server instead.
- **Browser tests wait for what closing a sheet does, never a fixed pause** (2026-10-11, phase 3's browser test): a native
  dialog's `close` event comes in a task of its own, and in Claude's software-drawn Chromium a frame can take long enough
  that what it does (a gift link's secret taken out of the address) came more than 400 ms after the click. Wait for the
  result itself (`waitFor`).
- **sharp's `.extract(…).stats()` describes the whole picture, not the part extracted** (2026-10-10, found in a test of
  the share mark): to measure part of a picture, read its raw pixels (`.extract(…).raw().toBuffer()`) and average them.
- **Browser tests read words with `textContent`, not `innerText`** (2026-10-10): `innerText` follows the CSS
  (`text-transform: uppercase` made "Nova" read "NOVA"). And Playwright calls the label of a disabled input "not enabled":
  a label that opens a file picker is clicked with `force: true`, after clearing toasts that may cover it.
- **A button whose words change is found by where it is, not by its words** (2026-10-11): a Playwright locator by its name
  ("Copy address") loses the button once it says "Copied", and waits until the words come back (2.5 s later), so the check
  read "Copy address". And two forms on one page never share a class a test looks inside (`.sa-team-form .sa-err` found the
  access form's too: it has its own class, `sa-access-form`, since).
- **Browser tests count a fake service's requests from before the click they wait for** (2026-10-11): waiting for "two
  requests" in all found one made earlier, and checked the wrong request. And a word's edge (`\b`) is never between a
  letter and a number: a button's `textContent` reads "Create8 credits" (its parts have no space between them).
- **Claude runs the whole suite in a copy of this folder with only the change being handed over** (2026-10-11), when its
  workspace holds unfinished work (the meme templates' files and `opentype.js` that day): this folder's own `package.json`,
  the workspace's `node_modules` linked in, and `NODE_PRESERVE_SYMLINKS=1` (else the share mark's ffmpeg test reads the
  link's real path and fails).
- **A page with a guide keeps its `data-guide` names** (2026-10-11): the guide's arrows point at them, and
  `tests/guide.test.js` fails the build if a step's name isn't on its page. After changing how such a page looks, Claude
  films its videos again (`tools/studio/guide-record.mjs`) and looks at each one's contact sheet (`--sheet`) before saving
  them; a scene that fails leaves a picture of the screen in `node_modules/.cache/agi1-guide/failed/`.
- **In AGI Studio's pages, `app.allowed()` is null until the wallet's own answer arrives** (2026-10-12): words that depend
  on whether this wallet may use AGI Studio wait for it (`app.meReady()`, at most 4 s); reading null as "no" told a wallet
  that's in already that a gift link "lets you in".
- **Browser tests that share one fake database across their flows find a row by what it is, not by being among the newest
  shown** (2026-10-12: by the claim flow, the owner's first gift link was the 11th, behind Show all). And the Coin tool's
  picture, like everything a closed sheet does, is waited for (see the sheets' `close` event above).
- **An accessibility scan waits for a sheet's fade-in** (2026-10-12): a sheet comes in from 0.4 opacity (`sa-up`), and axe
  read a red button's colors mid-fade as too little contrast. Browser tests wait for the page's animations to end first.
- **A guide video's poster is the frame where `film.poster()` is called** (2026-10-12): call it once the camera has arrived and
  what it shows is painted (`painted()` in `tools/studio/guide-scripts.mjs`), never as a camera move starts (the phone's
  `make-creations` poster was the blur behind a sheet still coming up).
- **A canvas is read only after the page drew it** (2026-10-12, the photo editor's browser test): the editor draws in the
  browser's next frame, and Claude's software-drawn Chromium draws a page with a sheet's blurred backdrop about once a
  second, so a check waits two animation frames (`requestAnimationFrame`) before reading a canvas's pixels. And a tile found
  in a gallery that's drawn again when a job finishes can be gone a moment later: a check looks for it again.
- **The guide recorder runs on its own** (2026-10-12): Claude starts it with `setsid`, so a stopped command never stops its
  ffmpeg halfway (a half-written video, and the clips' list left as it was: record that clip again). A clip over the
  guide's 14 s is tightened with a cut while something loads (`film.cut()`), what's pressed in view before the camera rolls,
  shorter pauses and, only if it must, a little faster (`film.fast(1.45)`: the photo editor's on a computer).
- **A test compares big buffers and arrays by hash or a loop, never with `deepEqual`** (2026-10-13, the launch video's
  voice-over): a failed `deepEqual` prints both (`assert`'s diff has no length limit), and on two small videos it ran out
  of memory and the test process was killed (`SIGKILL`), so the failure said nothing. Small arrays are fine.
- **Playwright's Chromium plays no H.264 or AAC** (2026-10-12, the video editor): its browser test plays stand-ins made by
  ffmpeg (VP9, with Opus for sound, in MP4), and the clock's ffmpeg there makes VP9 with Opus instead of H.264 with AAC
  (the guide recorder's `cutRun`); the real H.264 and AAC are made and read back in Node, by `tests/influencer.test.js`.
- **Anything a page shows that depends on a choice is said again when the choice changes** (2026-10-12): a tab's panel
  isn't drawn again for every change, so the video editor's Shape panel kept "It's made 640 × 360" after Square 1:1 was
  picked (its browser test found it). And what the editor sets in its next animation frame (its frame's shape, its hint,
  its play buttons after the video's own "play" event) is waited for by a test (`waitFor`), never read after a fixed
  pause; a canvas's sample points stay clear of what's drawn on purpose (a frame's thirds' lines).
- The Claude desktop app saves copies of files Claude sends in chat into `Claude outputs/`. Git ignores that folder,
  and its copies (including any CLAUDE.md there) may be out of date. The CLAUDE.md at the top of this folder is the current one.
- **Never `ln -s` onto a path that's already a link** (2026-10-13, a test copy): `ln -s <folder> node_modules` where
  `node_modules` is already a link to a folder puts the new link inside that folder (`node_modules/node_modules`), and the
  copy runs against other packages than it should. Remove the old link first (`rm node_modules`, never `rm -r`), or use
  `ln -sfn`.
- **A test's influencer names have no spaces** (2026-10-13): the tests' fakes make an id from a name (`idOf()`), so
  `readyInf({ name: 'Nova Star' })` made an id the database refuses; a test that needs a name with a space sets it after
  (`fake.db.infs.get(id).name = 'Nova Star'`).
- **An OBJ without a material has no `mtllib` line** (2026-10-13, `objZip()`): a 3D app looks for the file it names, and
  warns when it isn't in the zip (found by the unit test of a model without textures).
- **A browser test's fake world is one test file's fakes** (2026-10-13): `app/realfakes.mjs` is made from
  `tests/influencer.test.js`'s fakes, which don't have `tests/studio.test.js`'s `studio_step`, so in the browser test a 3D
  model with choices failed at its first step ("studio_step not found", `ai:motion1`) while the code was right (`real19.mjs`
  adds it). When a browser test's server log says a function isn't found, look at the fake before the code.
- **A browser test clicks a word inside its own group** (2026-10-13): `getByText('Studio', { exact: true })` found the top
  bar's logo first and left the page; the 3D page's backdrop is `.sa-tool-bg`'s "Studio". And a 3D page's clip is 10 s
  until 5 s is picked (Spin on, 10 s make one whole turn).
- **The page imports opentype.js's own ES module, `opentype.js/dist/opentype.mjs`** (2026-10-19, the meme editor): its
  package's `browser` field points at its UMD build, which Vite reads first for the page (before `module`), so the page
  names the ES module itself (loaded only when the meme editor opens, a separate file). Our server imports `opentype.js`
  as Node reads it (`main`, the same UMD build: `server/meme-render.js`).
- **A font's layout features are tried, every one, before it ships** (2026-10-19): opentype.js reads a font's lookups
  lazily, so a lookup it can't apply (Bangers' `ccmp`) only throws when a word uses it. `tests/memes.test.js` lays out
  every font's every letter in a row, and mixed groups of three of them, so a new font with one fails the build, not a
  person's meme.
- **A browser test finds a mark by what it is, not by words it used to show** (2026-10-19): a meme's tile said "Meme" in a
  tag; it's a round mark in its top right corner since (its words in its `title`), so the edit flow's two checks failed
  (`app/real21.mjs`, 244 of 246) though the page was right: they look for `.sa-media-corner[title="Meme"]` now, and where
  it is in its tile.
- **Playwright runs the route registered last first** (2026-10-19, AGI games' browser test): a test that blocks every outside
  address with one route and lets one through with another (Cloudflare's human check, stood in for) registers the one it
  lets through after the one that blocks, or the block wins and the stand-in never runs.
- **A browser test waits for a smooth scroll to end, never a fixed pause** (2026-10-19): "Rate it" glides the page to
  `#rate` (`scroll-behavior: smooth`), and in Claude's software-drawn Chromium the glide can outlast any pause; a check of
  what's in view waits until the page stops moving.
- **Measure an element after its entrance animation** (2026-10-19): AGI games' "beta" lands from about twice its size, so
  its box measured as the page opened was too big; a test waits for `el.getAnimations()`'s `finished` first.
- **A browser test counts only the fake service's requests it's about** (2026-10-19): AGI games' page asks for its own
  numbers and reviews as it opens (and again after a save), so a count of "every request to the fake database" was off by
  those; a test filters by what each request is.
- **Never edit a tool's output by hand** (2026-10-19): the game's `src/games/rideemagi/game.js`, `game.css` and
  `rideemagi.html`'s markup between `<!-- game:start -->` and `<!-- game:end -->` are written by
  `tools/games/import-rideemagi.mjs` (its fonts' `fonts.css` by `tools/games/game-fonts.py`), like AGI Studio's guide
  videos' list: a change goes in the tool (a patch), then the tool is run again.
- **A skip list matches an exact path or the path plus "/", never a bare start** (2026-10-20): Claude's comparison of
  this folder with its workspace skipped `tools/roadmap-promo/media` (a folder git ignores) as the start of a name, so
  `tools/roadmap-promo/media.mjs` beside it was never compared, and its old copy here failed the roadmap's first push on
  Vercel. Every path check of Claude's is `path === p || path.startsWith(p + '/')`. And before telling the owner to push a
  change that touched many files, Claude builds a clean copy the way Vercel does: a throwaway git index over its workspace
  (so `.gitignore` is followed, never git in this folder), a fresh `npm install`, Node 24 and Vercel's settings.
- **Never `pkill -f` with a pattern that appears in its own command** (2026-10-20): `pkill -f "spinpics/serve.mjs"`
  matched the shell running it and killed it (exit 144). Find the process first (`ps aux | grep "[s]erve.mjs"`: the
  brackets keep the grep itself out) and `kill` its number.
- **A browser test on a game's page waits for the AGI GAMES intro first** (2026-10-20): its cover is over the game for
  about 2.5 s, and a click on it skips it and is swallowed (it never reaches the game). `introGone()` in Claude's scratch
  `games/gm-lib.mjs` waits for its cover to be gone (at most about 6 s).
- **Claude's made-up Vercel settings hold every name in "Environment variables"** (2026-10-21): they had lacked five
  (`ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL`, `GEMINI_TTS_MODEL`, `VOICE_STREAM`, `TELEGRAM_MUSIC`, `STUDIO_CLEAN_AGI`), and with
  `ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL` set, 7 of `tests/checker.test.js`'s tests failed: their fake node answers only the free public
  node's address, and the test never deleted the setting (it does now, in its `beforeEach`, like the other tests that
  fake the node). If the owner had ever set another node in Vercel, every build would have failed. Before each run with
  the settings, Claude checks its list against the table's names.
- **The relay's packages are its own** (2026-10-21): `tools/trench-relay/package.json` and its lock (ws and sharp, exact
  versions) are what its Docker image installs; never add the relay's packages to the site's `package.json`. The site
  has `ws` only as a dev dependency, for the tests that run the relay against its stand-ins (`tests/clips.test.js` allows
  only `vite` and `ws` there).
- **A browser test of a page that talks to a server on this computer serves the page from this computer too**
  (2026-10-21, Live mode's browser test): a page Playwright makes up itself (`route.fulfill`) counts as a public site, and
  Chromium then holds its requests to 127.0.0.1 (a public page reaching a private address). The test serves the built
  game through a small local proxy that adds the site's real CSP, and points the game at the local relay with `?relay=`
  (which only works on localhost).
- **A test waits for a stand-in service to hear each message, never assumes it** (2026-10-21): Live mode's reconnect
  test passed on Node 20 and 24 and failed once on Node 22 under load, because it went on before the stand-in Helius had
  heard each subscription; it waits for them now (12 runs on each Node, 18 under load).
- **Lightning CSS drops a plain fallback written before a `dvh` value** (2026-10-21, Pomp.fun's chart: `height:
  300px` then a `clamp(…dvh…)`): it assumes every browser knows `dvh`, so browsers older than Chrome 108 or Safari 15.4
  size the chart from its attributes. `color-mix()` with a plain color before it is kept. (Prefixed pairs: see "Lightning
  CSS" above.)
- **Screenshots that must come out the same every time take the page's clock** (2026-10-21, TRENCHING SIMULATOR's key
  art): Playwright's clock, paused; its ticks put on a whole 16 ms frame first, its wall clock on a fixed moment, then
  moved only in whole frames, with the game's dice seeded: two runs gave byte-identical screenshots
  (`tools/games/trench-art.mjs`).
- **An accessibility scan of a game waits for AGI-1's bubble to finish fading** (2026-10-21): an axe probe of
  Pomp.fun in free play at 4× caught her bubble halfway through its fade (blended colors, 4.49:1, just under AA); at rest
  it's #15161f on white (18:1) and passes. Like a sheet's fade-in above. Since then Claude's axe probe (its scratch
  `trench/axeprobe.mjs`) notes her bubble's state before and after each scan, and scans again (up to 4 times) when it
  moved during a scan that flagged it.
- **A share card listed in `scripts/share-pages.js` must exist in `public/cards/` before a change is handed over**
  (2026-10-21): `trenchingsimulator.jpg` was listed on 2026-10-20, before its picture was made, and `tests/share.test.js`
  (and the build's own "share cards missing" check) failed until it was.
- **AGI games' browser harness serves the site's real CSP** (2026-10-21): Claude's scratch `games/gm-lib.mjs` answers
  with `vercel.json`'s headers, so its `connect-src` refuses a `?relay=ws://127.0.0.1…`: Live mode's "Coming soon" test
  (`trench/livesoon.mjs`) takes the CSP's refusal as proof the page tried to connect, and Live mode's own browser test
  (`trench/live/live-e2e.mjs`) serves the game through a proxy of its own.
- **A mutation made with `perl -0pi -e 's/…/…/'`** (the whole file as one string) changes only the first match in the
  file (2026-10-21): aimed at the "Soon" chip's CSS rule, it changed an earlier line, so that broken version went
  uncaught. Aim the pattern inside the rule's own block, and check the line meant was the one that changed.
